## 4bdddc46-3b80-45ec-bc37-523e74d4fda6
The official Figma MCP server. Use this server whenever the user wants to create, generate, edit, implement, or sync any design, UI, screen, component, mockup, or visual — in Figma, FigJam, Figma Make, or Figma Slides — and whenever the user mentions Figma or provides a figma.com URL.

This server bridges code and design in both directions, and supports designing from scratch using existing design systems and codebases.

CAPABILITIES:
- Read designs FROM Figma into code (get_design_context, get_screenshot, get_metadata, get_figjam)
- Write designs INTO Figma from code, intent, or existing components (use_figma, generate_figma_design, create_new_file, upload_assets)
- Bridge code and design via Code Connect (get_code_connect_map, add_code_connect_map)
- Create diagrams and FigJam content (generate_diagram, get_figjam)

WHEN TO USE THESE TOOLS:
- The user wants to create, mock up, or generate any UI, screen, component, or design — even if Figma isn't named
- The user wants to implement a design as code (design-to-code)
- The user wants to push a page, view, or component into Figma (code-to-design)
- The user wants to update, sync, or edit an existing Figma file
- The user shares a figma.com URL
- The user wants to build or extend a design system, design tokens, or component library
- The user wants to create a diagram in FigJam

SKILLS (Prefer the skills shipped with the Figma plugin on the agent being used. If no Figma plugin is installed, use the skills served by the Figma MCP resource):
- /figma-use — MANDATORY before calling use_figma; fallback: skill://figma/figma-use/SKILL.md
- /figma-generate-design — for translating an app page or layout into Figma; fallback: skill://figma/figma-generate-design/SKILL.md
- /figma-generate-library — for building a design system in Figma from code; fallback: skill://figma/figma-generate-library/SKILL.md
- /figma-code-connect — for mapping Figma components to codebase components; fallback: skill://figma/figma-code-connect/SKILL.md
- /figma-use-figjam — for FigJam-specific use_f

- figma:figma-create-new-file: **MANDATORY prerequisite** — you MUST invoke this skill BEFORE every `create_new_file` tool call. NEVER call `create_new_file` directly without loading this skill first. Trigger whenever the user wants a new blank Figma file — a new design, FigJam, or Slides file — or when you need a fresh file before calling `use_figma`. Usage — /figma-create-new-file [editorType] [fileName] (e.g. /figma-create-new-file figjam My Whiteboard, /figma-create-new-file slides Q3 Review)
- figma:figma-design-to-code: **MANDATORY prerequisite** — you MUST invoke this skill BEFORE calling the `get_design_context` Figma MCP tool. You MUST trigger this skill whenever the user wants to implement, build, port, or code up a Figma design as code. Example prompts (not exhaustive) are 'implement this Figma design', 'build this screen from Figma', 'turn this Figma into code', 'design to code'. This skill provides critical instructions and steps to the agent on how to correctly implement Figma designs in code and must NOT be skipped.
- figma:figma-generate-design: Use this skill alongside figma-use when the task involves translating an application page, view, or multi-section layout into Figma. Triggers: 'write to Figma', 'create in Figma from code', 'push page to Figma', 'take this app/page and build it in Figma', 'create a screen', 'build a landing page in Figma', 'update the Figma screen to match code', 'convert this modal/dialog/drawer/panel to Figma'. This is the preferred workflow skill whenever the user wants to build or update a full page, modal, dialog, drawer, sidebar, panel, or any composed multi-section view in Figma from code or a description. Discovers design system components, variables, and styles from Code Connect files, existing screens, and library search, then imports them and assembles views incrementally section-by-section using design system tokens instead of hardcoded values.
- figma:figma-generate-diagram: MANDATORY prerequisite — load this skill BEFORE every `generate_diagram` tool call. NEVER call `generate_diagram` directly without loading this skill first. Trigger whenever the user asks to create, generate, draw, render, sketch, or build a diagram — flowchart, architecture diagram, sequence diagram, ERD or entity-relationship diagram, state diagram or state machine, gantt chart, or timeline. Also trigger when the user mentions Mermaid syntax or wants a system architecture, decision tree, dependency graph, API call flow, auth handshake, schema, or pipeline visualized in FigJam. Routes to type-specific guidance, sets universal Mermaid constraints, and tells you when to use a different diagram type or skip the tool entirely (mindmaps, pie charts, class diagrams, etc.).
- figma:figma-generate-library: Build or update a professional-grade design system in Figma from a codebase. Use when the user wants to create variables/tokens, build component libraries, create individual components with proper variant sets and variable bindings, set up theming (light/dark modes), document foundations, or reconcile gaps between code and Figma. Also use when the user asks to create or generate any component in Figma — even a single one — since components require proper variable foundations, variant states, and design token bindings to be production-quality. This skill teaches WHAT to build and in WHAT ORDER — it complements the `figma-use` skill which teaches HOW to call the Plugin API. Both skills should be loaded together.
- figma:figma-implement-motion: Translates Figma motion and animations into production-ready application code. Use when implementing animation/motion from a Figma design — user mentions "implement this motion", "add animation from Figma", "animate this component", provides a Figma URL whose node is animated, or when `get_design_context` returns motion data or instructs you to call `get_motion_context`.
- figma:figma-swiftui: SwiftUI ↔ Figma translation. Use whenever the user mentions Swift, SwiftUI, iOS, iPhone, or iPad — in EITHER direction — translating a Figma design into SwiftUI (design → code), or pushing SwiftUI views / screens / tokens back into a Figma file (code → design). Triggers on phrases like 'implement this Figma design in SwiftUI', 'build this screen in Swift', 'push this SwiftUI view to Figma', 'mirror my Swift code in a Figma file', or whenever a Figma URL appears alongside `.swift` files / an `.xcodeproj`. Routes to a direction-specific reference doc; loads alongside `figma-use` for the code → design path.

- figma:figma-use-slides: This skill helps agents use Figma's use_figma MCP tool in the Slides context. Can be used alongside figma-use which has foundational context for using the use_figma tool.

- anthropic-skills:pptx: Use this skill any time a .pptx or .potx file is involved in any way — as input, output, or both. Trigger whenever the user asks for a PowerPoint or .pptx file, or references a .pptx or .potx filename, regardless of what they plan to do with the content afterward. However, when the user asks for a deck, slides, a slide deck, or a presentation without naming a file format, default to using a dedicated slide-deck artifact type or a separate slides skill if this session offers one; otherwise, use this skill.
- anthropic-skills:schedule: Create or update a scheduled task that runs automatically. Use when the user says things like "every day", "each morning", "remind me in an hour", "run this at noon", or wants to reschedule an existing task.
- anthropic-skills:setup-cowork: Guided Cowork setup — install role-matched plugins, connect your tools, try a skill.
- anthropic-skills:skill-creator: Create new skills, modify and improve existing skills, and measure skill performance. Use when users want to create a skill from scratch, edit, or optimize an existing skill, run evals to test a skill, benchmark skill performance with variance analysis, or optimize a skill's description for better triggering accuracy.
- anthropic-skills:xlsx: Use this skill any time a spreadsheet file is the primary input or output. This means any task where the user wants to: open, read, edit, or fix an existing .xlsx, .xlsm, .xltx, .csv, or .tsv file (e.g., adding columns, computing formulas, formatting, charting, cleaning messy data); create a new spreadsheet from scratch or from other data sources; or convert between tabular file formats. Trigger especially when the user references a spreadsheet file by name or path — even casually (like "the xlsx in my downloads") — and wants something done to it or produced from it. Also trigger for cleaning or restructuring messy tabular data files (malformed rows, misplaced headers, junk data) into proper spreadsheets. The deliverable must be a spreadsheet file. Do NOT trigger when the primary deliverable is a Word document, HTML report, standalone Python script, database pipeline, or Google Sheets API integration, even if tabular data is involved.
- design: Create a design canvas - a multi-artboard visual design published as an Artifact that runs Claude Design's canvas editor (an early preview of Claude Design inside Claude Code). You DRAFT the design as .dc.html artboards laid out on one pan/zoom canvas; where saving is enabled for the user's account they refine every element visually (click-to-select, a properties panel, inline text editing, undo/redo) and Save publishes a new version for everyone, otherwise they get a view-and-export (PNG/PDF) preview of your draft. Good for UI mockups and screen flows, landing pages, marketing and social graphics, and print pieces - posters, flyers, brochures as single-page artboards; memos and reports as one flowing artboard. Use when someone wants a design, mockup, wireframe, UI or screen design, landing page, poster, flyer, brochure, banner, card, one-pager, or any visual layout they would rather tweak by hand than in code. Only for CREATING or re-seeding a canvas; an existing one is edited in its published Artifact.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. When the destination is a first-party document connector (host-designated, never self-described) that renders live charts, hand it the rows (inline, or as an uploaded data file the chart cites) rather than a rendered PNG/SVG — a picture of a chart loses hover, data inspection and per-value comments. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".

- artifact-diagramming: Diagramming know-how for Artifacts - when a picture earns its place, how to draw one that shows the real mechanism, and the inline-SVG mechanics that keep it legible in both themes.

- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.

- workflow-authoring: Reference for writing a Workflow tool script (script API and gotchas, resume, quality patterns, worked examples). Load before authoring a script for a workflow the user already opted into; it does not itself authorize running one.
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

## SECTION C — FULL OWNER BRIEF (the board card, verbatim, 80 sections)
===============================================================================

You are working on the complete redesign of the Nxeon customer portal.

This is NOT a cosmetic redesign.

This is a full product-level UI/UX transformation and visual identity overhaul of the entire customer-facing Nxeon platform.

The existing portal has been developed incrementally over many months by continuously adding features on top of previous features. As a result, there is significant inconsistency across navigation, layouts, spacing, components, typography, forms, cards, buttons, flows, visual hierarchy, terminology, asset usage, and overall UX.

Your job is to establish a completely new, coherent Nxeon design system and then migrate the entire portal into that system.

The result should feel like a premium, venture-backed, multi-million-dollar infrastructure / AI / cloud technology company.

It must NOT feel like a generic SaaS dashboard.
It must NOT feel like a typical Claude-generated application.
It must NOT feel "vibecoded."
It must NOT simply copy Vercel, Linear, DigitalOcean, Cloudflare, Stripe, or any other existing product.

Nxeon needs its OWN visual identity.

==================================================
01. CRITICAL NON-NEGOTIABLE CONSTRAINT
==================================================

DO NOT CHANGE THE BACKEND.

This redesign is primarily a frontend architecture, UI, UX, interaction, visual identity, and information architecture project.

Preserve:

- Existing backend functionality
- Existing APIs
- Existing API contracts
- Existing database behavior
- Existing provisioning logic
- Existing billing logic
- Existing authentication
- Existing server operations
- Existing hosting operations
- Existing domain functionality
- Existing mailbox functionality
- Existing DNS functionality
- Existing game server functionality
- Existing VPS functionality
- Existing shared hosting functionality
- Existing payment processing
- Existing subscription logic
- Existing account logic
- Existing support functionality
- Existing permissions
- Existing team functionality
- Existing infrastructure integrations
- Existing server controls
- Existing one-click installers
- Existing provisioning systems
- Existing server lifecycle operations

Do not remove functionality simply because it is not visible in the screenshots.

There are many screens, states, flows, modals, drawers, forms, dialogs, server-management operations, mailbox operations, DNS operations, billing flows, and deployment workflows that are NOT represented in the supplied screenshots.

The redesign must account for the entire existing application.

Before changing code, audit the existing codebase thoroughly.

Understand:

1. Every major route.
2. Every page.
3. Every reusable component.
4. Every modal.
5. Every drawer.
6. Every form.
7. Every API interaction.
8. Every server action.
9. Every deployment flow.
10. Every checkout flow.
11. Every billing flow.
12. Every domain flow.
13. Every email/mailbox flow.
14. Every hosting flow.
15. Every game-server flow.
16. Every VPS flow.
17. Every settings flow.
18. Every empty/loading/error/success state.
19. Every responsive/mobile behavior.
20. Every existing asset.

Do not assume the screenshots represent the complete application.

The screenshots are evidence of the current design problems.

They are NOT visual references to copy.

==================================================
02. FIRST STEP — AUDIT BEFORE IMPLEMENTATION
==================================================

Before making major visual changes, inspect the repository.

Map the existing product architecture.

Create an internal understanding of:

- Current routing
- Page hierarchy
- Product hierarchy
- Navigation
- Components
- Data dependencies
- State management
- Backend/API dependencies
- Existing design tokens
- Existing CSS
- Existing Tailwind configuration if applicable
- Existing component library
- Existing icons
- Existing images
- Existing SVGs
- Existing animations
- Existing loading states
- Existing form components

Identify duplicated UI patterns.

Identify inconsistent UI patterns.

Identify components that are visually similar but implemented separately.

Identify components that should become shared primitives.

Identify pages that currently behave differently despite representing similar concepts.

DO NOT immediately start changing random pages.

First establish the new system.

==================================================
03. THE NEW NXEON PRODUCT IDENTITY
==================================================

The new Nxeon identity should communicate:

- Infrastructure
- Reliability
- Intelligence
- Speed
- Precision
- Technology
- Trust
- Premium quality
- Modern cloud computing
- Automation
- Simplicity
- Control

The visual identity should feel like:

"Enterprise-grade infrastructure presented through an exceptionally refined consumer/developer experience."

Think:

Deep atmospheric navy
+
Precision typography
+
Subtle luminous technology
+
Premium surfaces
+
Intelligent motion
+
High information density without visual clutter
+
Exceptional hierarchy
+
Purposeful visual details

Avoid:

- Generic purple SaaS gradients everywhere
- Excessive glassmorphism
- Huge rounded cards everywhere
- Random glowing blobs
- Stock AI imagery
- Generic 3D illustrations
- Excessive gradients
- Neon overload
- Excessive shadows
- Excessive border boxes
- Template-looking dashboards
- Cookie-cutter SaaS cards
- "AI startup landing page" aesthetics
- Copying competitor layouts

Nxeon should feel engineered rather than decorated.

The design should look like a real product team spent months defining the system.

==================================================
04. NAVY MUST REMAIN — BUT REINVENT IT
==================================================

Keep Nxeon's navy foundation.

However, do not simply keep the current navy and purple UI.

Develop a much more sophisticated color system.

Suggested direction:

Background:
- Near-black navy
- Deep midnight blue
- Layered navy surfaces

Primary surface:
- #0D1224-ish territory

Secondary surface:
- Slightly elevated navy

- Slightly lighter blue-gray

Borders:
- Extremely subtle blue-gray borders
- Never harsh gray borders

- Nxeon blue

- Controlled electric blue / indigo

Success:
- Sophisticated green

- Controlled red

Information:
- Blue

Do not hardcode colors throughout the application.

Create a centralized design-token system.

==================================================

- background

- surface
- surface elevated
- surface interactive
- border

- text primary

Z-INDEX TOKENS

Do not allow each page to invent its own spacing, radius, button size, or card style.

==================================================
06. TYPOGRAPHY
==================================================

Typography needs to become significantly more premium.

Avoid oversized generic SaaS headings.

Use typography to create hierarchy.

The interface should feel compact and intelligent.

Important information should be visually dominant without requiring huge font sizes.

Use:

- strong metric typography
- precise labels
- restrained secondary text
- clear numeric hierarchy
- monospace typography where appropriate for infrastructure values
- code-like styling for IP addresses, SSH commands, DNS values, server IDs, ports, hashes, etc.

Infrastructure data should visually feel like infrastructure data.

Examples:

IP addresses
Server IDs
Node IDs
SSH commands
DNS records
Ports
CPU values
RAM
Storage
Bandwidth
Plan specifications

should use a consistent technical data treatment.

==================================================
07. LAYOUT SYSTEM
==================================================

The current portal frequently feels like pages were assembled independently.

Fix this.

Establish a universal page layout.

Recommended structure:

GLOBAL APP SHELL
|
├── Primary sidebar
├── Global top bar
├── Contextual page header
├── Main content canvas
└── Persistent support / feedback layer

Every page should use the same fundamental geometry.

The sidebar should establish the Nxeon product architecture.

The top bar should establish global utilities.

The content area should establish context.

Pages should NOT randomly change width.

Pages should NOT randomly change card density.

Pages should NOT randomly change heading alignment.

Pages should NOT randomly change tab styling.

==================================================

The current navigation should be reconsidered from the perspective of customer mental models.

However, DO NOT blindly implement this exact structure.

Inspect the existing product and determine the best information architecture.

The important principle is:

Customers should understand WHERE to go without needing to understand how Nxeon's backend infrastructure is structured.

==================================================
09. GLOBAL SEARCH / COMMAND EXPERIENCE
==================================================

Upgrade the global search.

It should become a premium command-center style experience.

- Servers

==================================================

Build a true reusable component system.

Components should include:

- AppShell
- Sidebar
- Topbar

Every component should follow the same visual language.

==================================================
11. ICONOGRAPHY
==================================================

This is extremely important.

DO NOT recycle the existing portal's icon treatment simply because it already exists.

The current iconography contributes to the "assembled over time" feeling.

Create a new Nxeon icon strategy.

Use a consistent icon family with:

- matching stroke width
- matching corner treatment
- matching optical size
- consistent visual weight
- consistent padding
- consistent active state

Infrastructure-specific icons should be designed or selected deliberately.

CPU
Memory
Storage
Network

Datacenter

DNS
SSL

Firewall

Deployment
Migration

Do NOT use random icon libraries mixed together.

If using an icon library, establish one primary icon family and customize its presentation.

Where a generic icon is insufficient, create custom Nxeon SVG icons.

==================================================
12. ABSOLUTELY NO ASSET RECYCLING
==================================================

This is a major requirement.

The existing portal assets should NOT simply be reused because they are already available.

Claude Code must NOT automatically reuse the same:

- illustrations
- decorative SVGs
- old icons
- old graphics
- old background effects
- old cards
- old visual motifs
- old generated imagery

unless the asset is explicitly identified as part of the new Nxeon brand system.

The redesign must create a NEW visual asset library.

Before implementation, inspect the existing assets and categorize them as:

KEEP
REWORK
REPLACE
REMOVE

The default should be REPLACE for decorative assets.

The screenshots should NOT become a source of assets.

They are references for understanding the current application only.

==================================================
13. NEW NXEON ASSET LANGUAGE
==================================================

Create a unique visual asset language.

Potential visual motifs:

- orbital infrastructure
- data pathways
- node networks
- geographic infrastructure
- abstract compute architecture
- subtle energy flows
- layered system diagrams
- server topology
- data-center inspired geometry
- precision grids
- atmospheric navy environments

BUT:

Do not turn every page into a sci-fi interface.

The visuals should be restrained.

The goal is:

"Premium infrastructure technology"

not

"gaming RGB cyberpunk."

Use visuals strategically.

==================================================
14. PREMIUM IMAGERY
==================================================

For pages where imagery adds value, use high-quality original or properly sourced assets.

Examples:

- high-quality game artwork
- carefully cropped game imagery

Infrastructure

Do NOT use low-resolution assets.

Do NOT mix unrelated illustration styles.

Do NOT use AI-generated generic "server room" images simply because they look impressive.

Images must have a purpose.

If suitable licensed imagery is unavailable, create custom SVG/CSS visualizations instead.

==================================================
15. MOTION DESIGN
==================================================

Motion should be a core part of the new identity.

But motion must be subtle and intentional.

Do NOT animate everything.

Use motion to communicate:

- state
- progress
- hierarchy
- causality
- system activity
- transitions

Examples:

- subtle active-state movement

Cards:
- very subtle hover elevation

Buttons:
- tactile hover/press states

Deployment:
- progressive provisioning animation

Server status:
- subtle live pulse

Graphs:
- smooth data transitions

Wizard:
- horizontal step transitions

Modals:
- spring-like entrance

- smooth directional motion

Notifications:
- subtle slide/fade

==================================================

MAXIMIZE CONVERSION

# NXEON PORTAL REDESIGN — PHASE 1 CARRY FILE
# Give this whole file to a fresh chat to run Phase 1. It contains: (A) how to use it + the hard rules,
# (B) the Phase-1 audit/blueprint prompt, (C) the full owner brief (board card), (D) the screenshot manifest
# + pointers to an already-completed sub-audit. Everything referenced lives on THIS machine and is readable.

## MODEL: Opus 4.8 is fine for this Phase-1 audit (retrieval + synthesis). Save Fable 5.1 for the later
## design/build phase where aesthetic judgment compounds. (Fable-for-everything is the no-compromise
## alternative if you'd rather not switch models; cost is the only reason not to.)

## HARD RULES
1. PHASE 1 IS READ-ONLY. Audit + research + produce the blueprint document ONLY. Do NOT edit/create/delete
   any file under /opt/nxeon, /opt/nxeon-staging, or /opt/nxeon-sandbox; no build/db/prisma/git-write/service
   commands. Your only writes are your own scratchpad report + the final blueprint. STOP after the blueprint
   and wait for approval before ANY implementation.
2. COMPLETELY FRESH TAKE. Do NOT use the old redesign memory files (nxeon-marketing-design,
   nxeon-redesign-generic-drift) or the prior "Portal Redesign Atlas" artifact. Clean-sheet identity.
3. BACKEND NEVER CHANGES (now and in later phases). Redesign is frontend/UI/UX/IA/visual-identity only.
   The capability-inventory audits are the "nothing gets lost" safety net.
4. When implementation eventually begins (a LATER phase, only after this blueprint is approved), it goes in an
   ISOLATED sandbox with NO real backend connectivity — reset /opt/nxeon-sandbox or spin a new one, fully
   sandbox-gated, no real Stripe/name.com/customer data. (A sandbox already exists: flow.k9x4rq7wpz2ah6t.nxeon.cloud
   -> service nxeon-sandbox-web :3002 -> tree /opt/nxeon-sandbox -> vhost /etc/nginx/sites-available/nxeon-sandbox.)

## HOW TO RUN PHASE 1
- Read the full brief (Section C below) — it is the spec.
- Read a representative subset of the screenshots (Section D) — dashboard, a server detail, the domain detail,
  a game deploy step, billing, email, checkout. They are the "BEFORE" evidence, NOT to be copied. Don't burn
  budget reading all 35.
- Fan out parallel READ-ONLY sub-agents for the audits (one writes each report). Domains/SSL/email/webmail is
  ALREADY DONE — see /root/nxeon-phase1-completed-audit-domains.md (do NOT re-run it; fold it in). Still needed:
  (1) routes/nav/IA; (2) design-system/CSS/component-duplication + icon census; (3) assets/icons KEEP/REWORK/
  REPLACE/REMOVE; (4) VPS/server backend capability inventory; (5) games/free-MC/shared-hosting/sites/volumes/
  nxcloud/migration/build-AI capability inventory; (6) account/billing/support/team/settings capability inventory
  (skip domains+email, already covered); (7) purchase/deployment funnels (step map + required-before-payment vs
  post-payment matrix + provisioning-state + friction); (8) states/responsive/a11y/terminology; (9) competitor
  UX research (DigitalOcean/Hetzner/Vultr/Lightsail/Linode/Vercel/Render/Railway/Coolify/Cloudflare/Namecheap/
  Porkbun/Google Workspace/game hosts) — principles only, copy nothing.
- Codebase facts to anchor on: /opt/nxeon = Next.js 15 App Router, React 19, Tailwind v4 (config in app/globals.css
  @theme + @layer components), Prisma/Postgres, separate worker/ process. Customer portal = app/dashboard/** +
  components/customer/** + components/portal/Shell.tsx (+ CommandPalette). ~180 customer components. Tokens today:
  Geist font, navy-950..600 + brand(violet)-50..900 + accent-blue #3b82f6 + accent-cyan #22d3ee; component classes
  .card/.btn-primary|secondary|danger|ghost|deploy/.input/.label/.nav-item-active/.table-shell/.eyebrow/.grad-text;
  no real light theme (only a marketing .tone-light). Known overlap-to-untangle: servers vs games vs hosting vs
  sites vs build vs projects vs claude-code vs nxcloud vs volumes vs matrix.

## DELIVERABLE
One document, "Nxeon Portal Redesign Blueprint," with the 35 numbered sections listed in the Phase-1 prompt
(Section B). For every major recommendation, say WHY. Publish it as a persistent Artifact (a real designed
document). End with the exact line "PHASE 1 COMPLETE — READY FOR REVIEW" and STOP.

===============================================================================
## SECTION B — PHASE 1 PROMPT (audit & design blueprint only)
===============================================================================

Nxeon Portal Redesign — PHASE 1: AUDIT & DESIGN BLUEPRINT ONLY

IMPORTANT: DO NOT redesign, rewrite, refactor, or modify the application yet. Do not make visual changes, do
not replace components, do not delete functionality, do not modify backend logic, do not start implementing pages.

MISSION: completely rethink the Nxeon customer portal. The current portal functions, but its visual identity,
information architecture, UX hierarchy, purchase flows, component system, navigation, asset usage, and overall
polish need reconsidering. The final product should feel like a premium, venture-backed, multi-million-dollar
infrastructure/AI/cloud company — not a generic SaaS dashboard and not a "vibecoded" Claude-style interface.
Navy must remain a brand foundation, but the entire visual language should be reconsidered.

PHASE 1 OBJECTIVE: before touching the UI, understand EVERYTHING that exists. Audit every route/page, nav item,
product area, reusable component, modal/drawer/wizard, form, API call, backend capability exposed to the
frontend, important user action, loading/error/empty/success state, purchase/deployment flow, hidden feature,
design token/style, icon, image/illustration asset, typography, and responsive behavior. Produce a complete
capability inventory so NO functionality is lost. Do not assume something is unimportant because it is not in
the screenshots.

PURCHASE + DEPLOYMENT UX: pay special attention to PRODUCT -> PLAN -> CONFIG -> CHECKOUT -> PAYMENT ->
PROVISIONING -> SETUP -> READY. Investigate a two-stage model: (1) a short conversion-focused checkout that
only requires config affecting price/capacity/region/availability/eligibility/provisioning, using intelligent
defaults for everything else; (2) an optional post-payment setup (OS/image, apps, hostname, SSH keys, security,
WordPress, game settings) that users can skip if it is safely changeable later. Do NOT assume this model fits
every product — evaluate it per product (VPS, Shared Hosting, Game Servers, Domains, Business Email) against
the real backend capabilities and recommend the best approach for each.

RESEARCH/BENCHMARKING: study current UX patterns from DigitalOcean, Hetzner, Vultr, AWS Lightsail,
Akamai/Linode, Vercel, Render, Railway, Cloudflare, Namecheap, Porkbun, Google Workspace, and major
game-server hosts — their purchase/deployment flows, information hierarchy, configuration patterns, pricing
presentation, progressive disclosure, onboarding, error handling, trust-building. Use their UX PRINCIPLES only.
DO NOT COPY their visual design, branding, layouts, components, illustrations, copy, or colors.

DESIGN DIRECTION TO EXPLORE: a new Nxeon design language — premium navy-based color system, sophisticated
typography hierarchy, custom/curated iconography, better spacing/density, stronger information hierarchy,
intentional imagery, a technical/infrastructure visual language, sophisticated data-viz, purposeful motion,
better empty/loading/error states, responsive layouts, accessibility, progressive disclosure, contextual help.
AVOID: generic SaaS dashboards, endless rounded cards, excessive gradients, random glows, generic purple AI
aesthetics, glassmorphism everywhere, default icon-library soup, copying Linear/Vercel/Stripe/Cloudflare, or
reusing the existing visual treatment simply because it exists. Someone should immediately recognize it as Nxeon.

ASSET AUDIT: audit every icon, illustration, logo treatment, image, background, graphic, product visual, and
decide KEEP / REWORK / REPLACE / REMOVE — default REPLACE for decorative assets; do not recycle existing assets
in new cards. Screenshots are not an asset source.

INFORMATION ARCHITECTURE: evaluate whether the current navigation is the best mental model for customers.
Consider how Compute (VPS, Shared Hosting, Game Servers, Volumes, Server Directory), Build (AI, Matrix, deploy
tools), Network (Domains, SSL), Mail (Business Email, Mailboxes), Tools (Migration, utilities, updates), and
Account (Billing, Team, Referrals, Partners, Support, Activity, Settings) should relate. Do not automatically
preserve the current grouping; recommend a better structure if one exists. Customers should know WHERE to go
without understanding how Nxeon's backend is structured.

PRODUCT UX AUDIT: specifically analyze VPS (list/overview/control panel/metrics/console/files/snapshots/
backups/networking/upgrades/activity/deployment); Shared Hosting (overview/websites/files/databases/domains/
email/apps/cron/backups/settings/WordPress); Game Servers (deployment/console/files/mods/plugins/backups/
players/worlds/commands/history/schedules/settings/activity); Domains (registration/setup/DNS/nameservers/
redirects/WHOIS privacy/transfer lock/EPP/renewal/health); Business Email (purchase/domain verification/DNS/
mailboxes/aliases/deliverability/subscription). Also audit Dashboard, Billing, Team, Support, Activity,
Settings, Migration Center, SSL, Volumes, Server Directory, AI/build tools, and anything else discovered.

DELIVERABLE (do NOT implement anything): a detailed document "Nxeon Portal Redesign Blueprint" containing:
1 Executive summary; 2 Current-state UX diagnosis; 3 Complete capability inventory; 4 Current route/page
inventory; 5 Current component/design-system audit; 6 Current asset/icon audit; 7 Navigation/IA
recommendations; 8 New Nxeon design philosophy; 9 Proposed visual identity; 10 Proposed design-token system;
11 Proposed component system; 12 Proposed motion system; 13 Responsive strategy; 14 Accessibility strategy;
15 VPS UX architecture; 16 Shared Hosting UX architecture; 17 Game Server UX architecture; 18 Domain UX
architecture; 19 Business Email UX architecture; 20 Purchase/checkout architecture; 21 Post-purchase setup
wizard architecture; 22 Dashboard architecture; 23 Account/billing/support architecture; 24 Recommended page
hierarchy for every major route; 25 Recommended user flows; 26 Backend capability -> new UI mapping; 27
Features that must NOT be removed; 28 Features that should be consolidated; 29 Features that should use
progressive disclosure; 30 Competitor/industry UX findings; 31 Buyer-psychology/conversion recommendations;
32 Implementation phases; 33 Recommended implementation order; 34 Risks and technical considerations;
35 Acceptance criteria. For every major recommendation, explain WHY it improves the experience.

This phase is ONLY about understanding, planning, researching, and designing the blueprint. Do not implement
until the blueprint is complete. At the end, clearly state "PHASE 1 COMPLETE — READY FOR REVIEW" and stop.

===============================================================================
## SECTION C — FULL OWNER BRIEF (the board card, verbatim, 80 sections)
===============================================================================

You are working on the complete redesign of the Nxeon customer portal.

This is NOT a cosmetic redesign.

This is a full product-level UI/UX transformation and visual identity overhaul of the entire customer-facing Nxeon platform.

The existing portal has been developed incrementally over many months by continuously adding features on top of previous features. As a result, there is significant inconsistency across navigation, layouts, spacing, components, typography, forms, cards, buttons, flows, visual hierarchy, terminology, asset usage, and overall UX.

Your job is to establish a completely new, coherent Nxeon design system and then migrate the entire portal into that system.

The result should feel like a premium, venture-backed, multi-million-dollar infrastructure / AI / cloud technology company.

It must NOT feel like a generic SaaS dashboard.
It must NOT feel like a typical Claude-generated application.
It must NOT feel "vibecoded."
It must NOT simply copy Vercel, Linear, DigitalOcean, Cloudflare, Stripe, or any other existing product.

Nxeon needs its OWN visual identity.

==================================================
01. CRITICAL NON-NEGOTIABLE CONSTRAINT
==================================================

DO NOT CHANGE THE BACKEND.

This redesign is primarily a frontend architecture, UI, UX, interaction, visual identity, and information architecture project.

==================================================

First establish the new system.

==================================================
03. THE NEW NXEON PRODUCT IDENTITY
==================================================

The new Nxeon identity should communicate:

- Infrastructure
- Reliability
- Intelligence
- Speed
- Precision
- Technology
- Trust
- Premium quality

- Automation
- Simplicity

Deep atmospheric navy
+
Precision typography
+
Subtle luminous technology
+
Premium surfaces
+
Intelligent motion
+
High information density without visual clutter
+
Exceptional hierarchy

Purposeful visual details

- Generic purple SaaS gradients everywhere
- Excessive glassmorphism
- Huge rounded cards everywhere
- Random glowing blobs

- Generic 3D illustrations
- Excessive gradients
- Neon overload
- Excessive shadows
- Excessive border boxes
- Template-looking dashboards
- Cookie-cutter SaaS cards
- "AI startup landing page" aesthetics

Nxeon should feel engineered rather than decorated.

The design should look like a real product team spent months defining the system.

==================================================
04. NAVY MUST REMAIN — BUT REINVENT IT
==================================================

Keep Nxeon's navy foundation.

However, do not simply keep the current navy and purple UI.

Develop a much more sophisticated color system.

Suggested direction:

==================================================
59. DEPLOYMENT PROGRESS SHOULD BE REAL
==================================================

Where backend events are available, connect the UI to real provisioning state.

Do not fake progress.

If backend state is limited, create a truthful state model.

Never claim:

"Installing"

if the backend cannot verify installation.

Use:

"Provisioning"

when the system only knows provisioning is occurring.

==================================================
60. SUCCESS EXPERIENCE
==================================================

Success screens should feel rewarding.

But do NOT use confetti or cheesy celebration animations.

Use:

- subtle light movement
- elegant checkmark
- infrastructure visualization
- status confirmation

Example:

"You're live."

Then:

Server
IP
Region
Plan

[Open Server]

==================================================
61. PREMIUM DESIGN STANDARD
==================================================

Every screen should pass this test:

Would this look credible in a product demo to a $10M+ technology company?

Would a professional developer trust it?

Would a non-technical customer understand it?

Does it feel intentional?

Does every element have a purpose?

Does it look like the same company as every other page?

If the answer is no, redesign it.

==================================================
62. DO NOT COPY COMPETITORS
==================================================

Research competitor UX patterns where useful.

You may study:

DigitalOcean
Hetzner
Vercel
Cloudflare
Vultr
AWS
Render
Railway
Coolify
other relevant infrastructure platforms

But use them for:

UX research
information architecture inspiration
friction reduction
deployment concepts
pricing presentation
configuration patterns

Do NOT copy their:

branding
layouts
visual identity
component styling
illustrations
copy
color schemes
unique UI patterns

Nxeon must remain distinctive.

Competitor research indicates that strong infrastructure products increasingly win by reducing the amount of infrastructure knowledge required to get from intent to deployment, while still preserving advanced controls for expert users. Use this principle throughout the product.

==================================================
63. DESIGN FOR TWO TYPES OF USERS
==================================================

Nxeon has:

BEGINNERS

They want:

"I need a website."

"I need a Minecraft server."

"I need email."

"I need a VPS."

They should not need to understand:

vCPU
nodes
networking
DNS propagation
SSH
firewalls
storage classes

EXPERTS

They want:

SSH
IP
DNS
ports
firewall
snapshots
backups
advanced configuration
technical logs
API
networking

The UI must support both.

Use progressive disclosure.

Simple by default.

Powerful when expanded.

==================================================
64. DESIGN LANGUAGE FOR TECHNICAL INFORMATION
==================================================

Technical information should feel deliberate.

Use:

Monospace values

Small technical labels

Subtle code surfaces

Copy buttons

Technical metadata chips

Structured key/value layouts

Examples:

IP
51.79.192.200

SSH
ssh root@51.79.192.200

Server ID
srv_01H...

Node
sgp-02

Technical details should feel premium rather than developer-tool ugly.

==================================================
65. DO NOT OVERUSE PURPLE
==================================================

The current portal uses blue/purple extensively.

Keep Nxeon's recognizable accent treatment.

But stop making every active element purple.

Use the brand accent strategically.

Primary CTA:
Brand

Secondary:
Neutral

Danger:
Red

Success:
Green

Information:
Blue

Selected:
Brand

This creates hierarchy.

==================================================
66. DESIGN SYSTEM DOCUMENTATION
==================================================

Before migrating every page, establish a design system.

Create or update:

Design tokens
Typography
Color system
Spacing
Buttons
Forms
Cards
Tables
Navigation
Tabs
Badges
Modals
Drawers
Toasts
Charts
Empty states
Loading states
Error states
Wizard components

Build a small internal showcase / style guide route if appropriate.

This allows every page to use the same system.

==================================================
67. MIGRATION STRATEGY
==================================================

Do NOT redesign random pages one by one.

Recommended order:

PHASE 1
Audit

PHASE 2
Design system

PHASE 3
Global application shell

PHASE 4
Navigation

PHASE 5
Deployment / purchase system

PHASE 6
Dashboard

PHASE 7
VPS

PHASE 8
Game Servers

PHASE 9
Shared Hosting

PHASE 10
Domains

PHASE 11
Email / Mailboxes

PHASE 12
Server management

PHASE 13
Billing

PHASE 14
Account / settings

PHASE 15
Support

PHASE 16
Remaining screens

PHASE 17
Responsive/mobile

PHASE 18
Accessibility

PHASE 19
Final consistency audit

==================================================
68. CRITICAL: DEPLOYMENT SYSTEM FIRST
==================================================

The deployment/purchase system should receive the highest UX priority.

Because this is where Nxeon makes money.

A beautiful dashboard does not compensate for a confusing checkout.

The deployment funnel should be treated as a core product.

Measure every step conceptually:

Discovery
→ Product selection
→ Plan selection
→ Configuration
→ Checkout
→ Payment
→ Provisioning
→ Setup
→ First successful use

At every step ask:

"What could cause this customer to leave?"

Remove unnecessary friction.

==================================================
69. CHECKOUT UX TEST
==================================================

A customer should be able to answer:

What am I buying?
Why should I choose this?
How much does it cost?
What will I pay today?
What will I pay later?
Where will it be deployed?
What happens after I pay?

without hunting around the interface.

==================================================
70. PRE-PURCHASE CONFIGURATION
==================================================

The system should make a recommendation.

Example:

"Recommended for your Minecraft server"

8 GB RAM
4 vCPU
100 GB NVMe
Singapore

"Best for up to 20 players"

Then:

Customize configuration

This is much better than presenting a giant technical configuration screen.

==================================================
71. POST-PURCHASE SETUP
==================================================

Consider the customer's psychological state after payment.

They have just paid.

They are asking:

"Did it work?"

"Where is my server?"

"What do I do now?"

Answer those immediately.

The post-payment screen should eliminate uncertainty.

Show:

Payment successful

Order confirmed

Provisioning status

Estimated readiness only if reliable

Live progress

Next actions

==================================================
72. FIRST VALUE
==================================================

Optimize for:

TIME TO FIRST VALUE.

For a VPS:

First successful login.

For game server:

First player connection.

For shared hosting:

First website online.

For domain:

Domain connected.

For email:

First email sent/received.

The portal should guide users toward this outcome.

==================================================
73. DO NOT HIDE POWER
==================================================

Advanced features still need to exist.

But organize them properly.

Example:

Server

Overview

Management

Networking

Storage

Backups

Security

Advanced

Instead of dumping everything into Overview.

==================================================
74. PAGE CONSISTENCY RULE
==================================================

Every page should have:

1. Clear context
2. Clear page title
3. Clear primary action
4. Clear status
5. Consistent content width
6. Consistent spacing
7. Consistent typography
8. Consistent components
9. Consistent actions
10. Consistent responsive behavior

If a page needs a special layout, it should be intentionally special.

Not accidentally inconsistent.

==================================================
75. FINAL VISUAL TEST
==================================================

After implementation, compare every major page against the design system.

Ask:

Does this look like Nxeon?

Does this look like the same product?

Are the spacing values consistent?

Are cards consistent?

Are buttons consistent?

Are icons consistent?

Are status colors consistent?

Are headings consistent?

Are tabs consistent?

Are forms consistent?

Are animations consistent?

Are empty states consistent?

Are error states consistent?

Are loading states consistent?

Are mobile behaviors consistent?

If not, fix them.

==================================================
76. IMPORTANT IMPLEMENTATION RULE
==================================================

Do NOT rewrite backend code simply because the frontend is being redesigned.

Do NOT modify API contracts unnecessarily.

Do NOT remove features.

Do NOT remove existing functionality because it was not represented in the screenshots.

Do NOT assume a screenshot represents the entire page.

Do NOT simplify away advanced functionality.

The objective is:

NEW EXPERIENCE
+
EXISTING CAPABILITIES

==================================================
77. SCREENSHOTS
==================================================

The provided screenshots represent the current Nxeon portal.

Use them to understand:

- Current hierarchy problems
- Inconsistent spacing
- Card overuse
- Navigation problems
- Density problems
- Typography problems
- Poor visual hierarchy
- Domain-page complexity
- Server-page complexity
- Deployment opportunities
- Inconsistent components

DO NOT copy the screenshots.

DO NOT reuse their visual language.

DO NOT reuse their decorative assets simply because they appear in the screenshots.

The screenshots are the "before" state.

The objective is a fundamentally better "after" state.

==================================================
78. THE NORTH STAR
==================================================

The new Nxeon portal should feel like:

"An intelligent infrastructure operating system."

Not:

"A hosting company dashboard."

The customer should feel:

"Nxeon handles the infrastructure complexity for me."

while still knowing:

"If I want full control, it's there."

==================================================
79. FINAL QUALITY BAR
==================================================

Do not stop at:

"It technically works."

Do not stop at:

"The colors look better."

Do not stop at:

"The cards look nicer."

The redesign is complete only when:

The entire portal feels like one product.

The entire portal feels like one brand.

The deployment experience is dramatically easier.

The purchase funnel is low-friction.

The information architecture makes sense.

Advanced functionality remains available.

The UI has a unique Nxeon identity.

The visual system is reusable.

The asset library is new.

The motion language is consistent.

The responsive experience is intentional.

The portal feels premium.

The portal feels trustworthy.

The portal feels fast.

The portal feels engineered.

And most importantly:

IT MUST NOT LOOK LIKE A GENERIC CLAUDE/VIBECODED SAAS APPLICATION.

==================================================
80. EXECUTION INSTRUCTIONS
==================================================

Start by auditing the repository.

Do not immediately modify every page.

First produce an internal implementation plan covering:

1. Current architecture
2. Existing routes
3. Existing components
4. Existing backend dependencies
5. Current design problems
6. Proposed information architecture
7. Proposed design system
8. Proposed component architecture
9. New asset strategy
10. Deployment architecture
11. Migration order

Then implement the design system.

Then implement the global shell.

Then implement the deployment/purchase experience.

Then migrate the remaining portal.

At every stage:

Preserve backend behavior.

Preserve functionality.

Preserve data.

Preserve permissions.

Preserve APIs.

Preserve operational capabilities.

Do not create fake backend functionality simply to make the UI look complete.

If a feature exists in the current application but is not visible in the screenshots, preserve it and redesign its interface according to the new system.

==================================================
FINAL DIRECTIVE
==================================================

I do not want a reskin.

I do not want the current portal with better colors.

I do not want the current cards rearranged.

I do not want the current assets recycled.

I do not want generic SaaS UI.

I do not want a clone of another cloud provider.

I want you to establish a completely new Nxeon product identity and propagate that identity across the entire application.

Think like:

- a senior product designer
- a design systems architect
- a conversion-focused UX designer
- a cloud infrastructure UX specialist
- a brand designer
- a frontend architect
- a motion designer

working together.

The existing portal is the raw functionality.

The new Nxeon system is the product.

Build the experience around the customer.

Make infrastructure feel simple.

Make advanced functionality feel powerful.

Make deployment feel effortless.

Make payment feel safe.

Make provisioning feel exciting.

Make management feel precise.

Make Nxeon feel like a company that is going somewhere.

The final product should be unmistakably Nxeon.

You are one of several READ-ONLY audit agents for the Nxeon customer-portal redesign (Phase 1 = audit only, nothing gets implemented). Codebase: /opt/nxeon (Next.js 15 App Router, React 19, Tailwind v4 with tokens in app/globals.css, Prisma/Postgres, separate worker/ process). Customer portal = app/dashboard/** + components/customer/** + components/portal/Shell.tsx (+ CommandPalette.tsx). API routes live under app/api/**.

HARD RULES: STRICTLY READ-ONLY. Do NOT edit/create/delete ANY file under /opt/nxeon, /opt/nxeon-staging or /opt/nxeon-sandbox. No build, npm, prisma, db, git-write, or service commands. Do not read .env* files or anything that looks like a secret. Your ONLY write is your report file: /tmp/claude-0/-root/1716c7ee-ae35-4cf5-b557-9059709e07c4/scratchpad/audit-01-routes-nav-ia.md (write it with the Write tool). Be exhaustive and factual, cite repo-relative file paths for every claim, use tables, mark anything uncertain as UNVERIFIED. This is an inventory + diagnosis, NOT a design proposal.

YOUR AUDIT: ROUTES / NAVIGATION / INFORMATION ARCHITECTURE.
Produce:
1. COMPLETE customer-facing route inventory. Walk app/dashboard/** recursively (every page.tsx, layout.tsx, loading.tsx, error.tsx, not-found, route groups, dynamic segments). Also find customer-facing routes OUTSIDE app/dashboard: order/checkout/deploy/pricing/login/signup/onboarding/verify/reset/partner/kodely-sso/riddle/whatever exists (list app/* top-level dirs and classify marketing vs portal vs admin vs api). For every portal route give: path pattern, one-line purpose, is it server or client component, main data sources (which API routes / server actions / prisma calls it hits), which feature flags gate it, whether it has loading/error boundaries, and the primary component files it renders.
2. NAVIGATION: dissect components/portal/Shell.tsx fully — sidebar groups + items + order + icons + badges + collapsed behaviour + which items are conditional (feature flags, account state, roles), top bar contents (search, notifications, account menu, currency, support), mobile behaviour, footer/support layer, any secondary nav (tabs inside product areas). Also dissect CommandPalette.tsx: what it indexes, categories, keyboard shortcuts, actions.
3. In-page sub-navigation: for each product area (servers, games, hosting, sites, domains, email/mail, volumes, nxcloud, build, projects, claude-code, migrate, tools, billing, settings, team, support) list the tabs/sections and how they're implemented (tabs component? query param? nested routes?). Note inconsistencies in tab implementation.
4. OVERLAP MAP: the known confusing overlap is servers vs games vs hosting vs sites vs build vs projects vs claude-code vs nxcloud vs volumes vs matrix vs deploy vs order vs tools. For each, state precisely what it is, what backend concept it maps to, what it shares with the others, and where a customer would be confused. Identify dead/legacy/redirect-only routes.
5. Middleware / redirects / auth gating: read middleware.ts and any redirects in next.config; list route-level auth and role requirements (team roles, partner, etc.).
6. Entry points into purchase flows: every link/button that starts a purchase or deploy (from dashboard, sidebar, empty states, marketing) and where it goes.
7. Diagnosis section: IA problems observed (duplication, naming inconsistency, orphan pages, depth issues, mixed mental models), with evidence.
Finish by writing the report, then reply with a ~10-line summary including the total route count and the top 5 IA problems.

input.description: Audit design system + duplication
input.prompt:
You are one of several READ-ONLY audit agents for the Nxeon customer-portal redesign (Phase 1 = audit only, nothing gets implemented). Codebase: /opt/nxeon (Next.js 15 App Router, React 19, Tailwind v4 with tokens in app/globals.css @theme + @layer components, Prisma/Postgres). Customer portal = app/dashboard/** + components/customer/** + components/portal/** (+ components/ui or similar if it exists).

HARD RULES: STRICTLY READ-ONLY. Do NOT edit/create/delete ANY file under /opt/nxeon, /opt/nxeon-staging or /opt/nxeon-sandbox. No build, npm, prisma, db, git-write, or service commands. Do not read .env* files. Your ONLY write is your report file: /tmp/claude-0/-root/1716c7ee-ae35-4cf5-b557-9059709e07c4/scratchpad/audit-02-design-system.md (Write tool). Exhaustive, factual, cite repo-relative file paths, use tables, mark uncertain items UNVERIFIED. Inventory + diagnosis only, no design proposals.

YOUR AUDIT: DESIGN SYSTEM / CSS / COMPONENT DUPLICATION / ICON CENSUS / TYPOGRAPHY / MOTION.
Produce:
1. TOKENS: dump and explain everything in app/globals.css (@theme colours, fonts, radii, shadows, animations, @layer components classes like .card/.btn-*/.input/.label/.nav-item-active/.table-shell/.eyebrow/.grad-text, .tone-light, any utilities). Also tailwind config if any, postcss config, font loading (app/layout.tsx, next/font), any CSS modules or styled files. List every named colour scale and its hex values.
2. HARDCODED STYLE CENSUS across components/customer/**, components/portal/**, app/dashboard/**: count of hex colours / rgb() / arbitrary Tailwind values like bg-[#...] / text-[..px] / inline style= attributes; list the top 30 most-used arbitrary values; count usages of each brand colour utility (brand-*, navy-*, accent-*, violet/purple/indigo/cyan/blue) to show where purple dominance comes from; count of gradient utilities (bg-gradient, from-, via-), blur/glow/backdrop-blur, shadow-*, rounded-* distribution (how many rounded-xl/2xl/3xl), border usage.
3. COMPONENT DUPLICATION: find visually-similar-but-separately-implemented patterns. For each of: buttons, badges/status pills, cards, tabs, segmented controls, modals/dialogs, drawers/sheets, confirmation dialogs, toasts/notifications, tables, key/value lists, empty states, skeletons/spinners, progress bars/steps, wizards/steppers, copy-to-clipboard, code/mono value display, metric/stat tiles, charts/graphs, resource meters, file browsers, terminals/consoles, log viewers, DNS editors, form fields (input/select/textarea/toggle/checkbox/radio/slider), page headers, section headers, region selectors, plan cards, pricing cards, app/one-click cards, game cards — list every implementation (file path + how it's styled), count them, and note which could collapse into one primitive. Identify any existing shared primitive dir (components/ui?) and how consistently it's used.
4. ICON CENSUS: which icon libraries are imported (lucide-react, @heroicons, react-icons, radix-icons, tabler, phosphor, custom) with import counts per library across the portal; count of inline <svg> elements in customer/portal components; list custom icon components; note stroke-width / size inconsistencies (grep for strokeWidth, size=, className w-3/w-4/w-5/w-6 on icons); emoji used as icons (grep for emoji chars in JSX).
5. TYPOGRAPHY: font families used, all text-size utilities distribution (text-xs..text-6xl counts), font-weight distribution, tracking/leading usage, heading patterns (how h1/h2 look per page — inconsistencies), monospace usage for technical values (font-mono count and where), number formatting.
6. MOTION: animation libs (framer-motion? motion? gsap? css only?), keyframes defined, animate-* utilities usage, transition patterns, reduced-motion handling (prefers-reduced-motion grep).
7. LAYOUT GEOMETRY: page max-widths used per route (max-w-* census), padding patterns, grid patterns, how page headers are built per page; z-index census; breakpoint usage (sm/md/lg/xl/2xl counts).
8. Chart/visualisation libs (recharts? chart.js? custom svg?) and where used.
9. Diagnosis: top inconsistencies with concrete evidence and rough counts (e.g. '7 different badge implementations', '4 tab styles').
Finish by writing the report, then reply with a ~12-line summary with key counts.

input.description: Audit assets KEEP/REWORK/REPLACE/REMOVE
input.prompt:
You are one of several READ-ONLY audit agents for the Nxeon customer-portal redesign (Phase 1 = audit only). Codebase: /opt/nxeon (Next.js 15 App Router). Customer portal = app/dashboard/** + components/customer/** + components/portal/**. Static assets in public/**.

HARD RULES: STRICTLY READ-ONLY. Do NOT edit/create/delete ANY file under /opt/nxeon, /opt/nxeon-staging or /opt/nxeon-sandbox. No build, npm, prisma, db, git-write, or service commands. Do not read .env* files. Your ONLY write is your report file: /tmp/claude-0/-root/1716c7ee-ae35-4cf5-b557-9059709e07c4/scratchpad/audit-03-assets.md (Write tool). Exhaustive, factual, cite repo-relative file paths, use tables, mark uncertain items UNVERIFIED.

YOUR AUDIT: VISUAL ASSET INVENTORY with a KEEP / REWORK / REPLACE / REMOVE verdict per asset. The owner's rule: the default for DECORATIVE assets is REPLACE; nothing gets recycled just because it exists; the logo/wordmark and legitimately-licensed game artwork are the main KEEP candidates; screenshots are never an asset source.
Produce:
1. public/** inventory: every image/svg/video/font/ico/og-image file (use find + du + identify/file for dimensions and format). Group by folder (logos, game art/heroes/posters, illustrations, backgrounds, icons, og images, favicons, app/one-click icons, region/flag images, screenshots, misc). For each: path, dimensions, size, format, what it depicts (open the image if not obvious — you can Read PNG/JPG/SVG files), where it is referenced (grep the src for its filename; note UNREFERENCED files), and a verdict KEEP/REWORK/REPLACE/REMOVE with one-line reason. For game artwork, note whether it looks like official artwork vs generated, and any licensing notes you can find (README, LICENSE, comments, a games manifest).
2. Logo / wordmark treatments: every variant of the Nxeon logo (svg/png, colour variants, favicon, og image, email logo, loading logo), where used, inconsistencies.
3. Inline decorative graphics inside components (grep for <svg in components/customer, components/portal, app/dashboard and also app/ marketing pages if they share components): glows, blobs, orbs, grids, mesh gradients, noise, particle/starfield effects, hero backdrops, gradient text — list each with file:line and verdict.
4. CSS-generated decoration: background-image utilities, radial-gradient/conic-gradient in globals.css or components, animated backgrounds, blur orbs — list with verdict.
5. Illustrations for empty states / onboarding / success / error — what exists, style consistency, verdict.
6. Game catalogue visuals: how games are represented (which manifest/lib file lists games, image fields, aspect ratios, per-game hero/poster/logo), count of games, missing images, mixed aspect ratios.
7. One-click app / OS / region imagery: what's used for Ubuntu/Debian/Docker/WordPress/etc. and for regions (flags? maps?), source and verdict.
8. Email templates' imagery (if there are email templates in lib/ or emails/) — list only, verdict.
9. Summary table: counts per verdict, and the short list of what the new asset library must provide (categories + rough counts), without designing them.
Finish by writing the report, then reply with a ~10-line summary with counts per verdict.

input.description: Audit VPS backend capabilities
input.prompt:
You are one of several READ-ONLY audit agents for the Nxeon customer-portal redesign (Phase 1 = audit only). Codebase: /opt/nxeon (Next.js 15 App Router, Prisma/Postgres, separate worker/ process for provisioning jobs). Customer portal = app/dashboard/** + components/customer/**; API under app/api/**; business logic in lib/**; schema in prisma/schema.prisma.

HARD RULES: STRICTLY READ-ONLY. Do NOT edit/create/delete ANY file under /opt/nxeon, /opt/nxeon-staging or /opt/nxeon-sandbox. No build, npm, prisma, db, git-write, or service commands. Do NOT run any command against the live database or live infrastructure. Do not read .env* files. Your ONLY write is your report file: /tmp/claude-0/-root/1716c7ee-ae35-4cf5-b557-9059709e07c4/scratchpad/audit-04-vps-capabilities.md (Write tool). Exhaustive, factual, cite repo-relative file paths, use tables, mark uncertain items UNVERIFIED. The purpose is the 'nothing gets lost' safety net: every backend capability the VPS UI exposes must be listed so the redesign preserves it.

YOUR AUDIT: VPS / SERVER CAPABILITY INVENTORY (app/dashboard/servers/**, the server control panel, related components, API routes, worker jobs).
Produce:
1. Data model: the Prisma models behind VPS servers (Server/Vps/Instance/Plan/Region/Node/Snapshot/Backup/SshKey/Firewall/IpAddress/Activity/etc.) with the fields that the UI shows; the status enum(s) and their meaning; lifecycle transitions.
2. CAPABILITY TABLE: every user action available on a VPS, one row each: action name | where in UI (file + tab/section) | API route or server action | backend function (lib/...) | what it does on infra (Proxmox? which API) | confirmation/danger level | current UI state handling (loading/success/error) | reversible? | notes. Cover at minimum: list/filter/search servers, create/deploy, start, stop, shutdown, reboot, force reset, reinstall/rebuild (OS list), resize/upgrade/downgrade plan (which dims), rename, hostname, tags/labels, console/VNC/noVNC/web terminal, SSH keys (add/remove/attach), root password reset, rescue mode, snapshots (create/restore/delete, limits, pricing), backups (schedule/on-demand/restore/retention/pricing), files/SFTP/file manager, firewall/security groups (rules), networking (IPv4/IPv6/additional IPs/rDNS/private network/bandwidth), monitoring/metrics (which metrics, ranges, data source, refresh), activity/audit log, alerts, one-click apps/app installer (full app catalog list with source file), cloud-init/user-data, DNS quick-link, migration in/out, delete/destroy (with what's lost), billing links (upgrade, renew, cancel), transfer to team member, any 'control panel' features (cPanel-style panel from memory: what exists), any 'server directory' / public listing, health checks, ISO mount, boot order, kernel, any 'matrix' feature. Also any AI/agent features attached to servers (claude-code? build?).
3. Plans & regions: source of truth for VPS plans (file/db), each plan's specs and prices (monthly/yearly, currency handling), regions/datacenters available, stock/availability logic, promo/first-month-free logic that affects VPS.
4. Provisioning pipeline: exactly what happens after payment for a VPS (worker job chain, each step, the status/progress fields written to DB, what the client can poll/subscribe to — endpoints, intervals, SSE?), typical durations if logged/commented, failure modes and how they surface. The owner wants to evaluate a two-stage model: (1) a short conversion-focused checkout that only asks for config that affects price/capacity/region/availability/eligibility/provisioning, with intelligent defaults for everything else; (2) an optional post-payment setup (OS/image, apps, hostname, SSH keys, security, WordPress, game settings) that users may skip if safely changeable later. 2. STEP MAP: exact ordered steps, the component file for each, every field per step (name, type, default, validation, required?), price-affecting fields, and the URL/state mechanism (query params, local state, localStorage draft, DB draft/order record). 5. POST-PAYMENT: exact redirect/landing after success per product, what provisioning status the client can see (endpoint, polling interval, SSE), the real state machine (list every status value and which worker step sets it), whether there is any 'setup' step today, and the first-value moment (SSH creds shown? game IP shown? site URL? DNS instructions?). What emails are sent at each stage.
6. RENEWALS / UPGRADES / ADD-ONS purchase paths (upgrade plan, add backups, add IP, add mailbox, renew domain, transfer domain in) — where and how they charge.
7. FRICTION LIST per product: concrete friction points with evidence (e.g. fields asked too early, no defaults, unclear price, hidden renewal price, no progress preserved, spinner-only waiting, dead ends, ambiguous CTA labels, terminology), and dead/broken/half-wired steps.
8. A consolidated 'funnel facts' table: product | steps today | fields today | fields that truly must be pre-payment | fields that can move post-payment with existing APIs | payment mechanism | provisioning states available | time-to-ready if known.
Finish by writing the report, then reply with a ~15-line summary including that consolidated table.

input.prompt:
You are one of several READ-ONLY audit agents for the Nxeon customer-portal redesign (Phase 1 = audit only). Codebase: /opt/nxeon (Next.js 15 App Router, React 19, Tailwind v4). Customer portal = app/dashboard/** + components/customer/** + components/portal/**.

HARD RULES: STRICTLY READ-ONLY. Do NOT edit/create/delete ANY file under /opt/nxeon, /opt/nxeon-staging or /opt/nxeon-sandbox. No build, npm, prisma, db, git-write, or service commands. Do not read .env* files. Your ONLY write is your report file: /tmp/claude-0/-root/1716c7ee-ae35-4cf5-b557-9059709e07c4/scratchpad/audit-08-states-responsive-a11y-terms.md (Write tool). Exhaustive, factual, cite repo-relative file:line, use tables, mark uncertain items UNVERIFIED. Inventory + diagnosis, no design proposals.

YOUR AUDIT: UI STATES / RESPONSIVE / ACCESSIBILITY / TERMINOLOGY / COPY.
1. LOADING STATES: every loading.tsx; every skeleton component; every spinner implementation (count distinct spinners); pages that show nothing while loading; long-running action feedback (provisioning, reboot, DNS propagation, payment) — what the user sees, with file refs; use of Suspense; optimistic updates.
2. EMPTY STATES: for every list/table/collection in the portal (servers, games, hosting, sites, domains, mailboxes, volumes, invoices, tickets, activity, team, ssh keys, snapshots, backups, dns records, etc.) what the empty state shows (text + CTA + illustration) and how many distinct empty-state implementations exist.
3. ERROR STATES: error.tsx files, error boundaries, how API errors are surfaced (toast? inline? alert?), the actual error copy (grep for 'Something went wrong', 'Failed to', 'Error'), whether errors explain what/why/how-to-fix, retry affordances, 'view technical details' patterns, 404 handling in portal.
4. SUCCESS STATES: after create/deploy/pay/save — what happens (toast? redirect? inline?); any celebration effects (confetti etc.).
5. TOASTS / NOTIFICATIONS: which toast lib(s) (sonner? react-hot-toast? custom?), how many systems, positions, variants; in-app notification center; banners (promo, win-back, warnings, degraded chat, unverified email, overdue).
6. MODALS / DRAWERS / DIALOGS: implementations (headless-ui? radix? custom?), count of distinct implementations, focus trapping, escape/overlay close, confirmation dialog patterns for dangerous actions (do they state what happens / what is lost / reversibility?), typed-confirm patterns.
7. RESPONSIVE: how Shell handles <lg (sidebar drawer? bottom nav?), tables on mobile (overflow-x? stacked cards?), wizards/checkout on mobile, server panel tabs on mobile, charts on mobile, modals on mobile, min-width hazards (grep for min-w-, w-[...px], fixed widths, grid-cols-N without breakpoints), touch targets; list pages that clearly break. If Playwright is installed (check node_modules/playwright or /root scripts) you may render the LIVE site https://nxeon.cloud public pages at 390px ONLY for read-only screenshots — but do NOT log in and do NOT hit the portal; portal analysis stays code-based.
8. ACCESSIBILITY: counts of aria-* attributes, role=, aria-label on icon-only buttons (find icon-only buttons WITHOUT labels), focus-visible styling in globals.css, keyboard support in custom dropdowns/tabs/menus/command palette, prefers-reduced-motion handling, colour-contrast risks (muted text colours on navy — list the text-* utilities used for secondary text and estimate contrast against the navy surfaces from globals.css hex values), form label association (label htmlFor / aria-labelledby counts vs inputs), skip links, heading order, alt text on images (count img without alt), live regions for async status.
9. TERMINOLOGY: build a glossary of every user-facing noun for the same concept and where each appears: server/VPS/instance/machine/node/droplet; game server/game/instance; hosting/website/site/project/app/deployment; domain/zone/DNS; mailbox/email/account; plan/package/tier/size; region/location/datacenter/zone; snapshot/backup/image; deploy/order/create/launch/provision/buy/checkout; team/organization/workspace; wallet/balance/credits; and internal jargon leaking to customers (node IDs, Proxmox, Mailcow, name.com, worker, prisma, sandbox, etc.). Note CTA label inconsistencies (Continue/Next/Deploy/Order/Buy/Pay).
10. COPY TONE: sample 20 headings/subheadings/CTAs across pages to characterise tone inconsistencies (marketing-y vs terse vs technical); any lorem/placeholder/TODO copy; any references to a third-party 'provider' in customer copy (brand rule: Nxeon speaks as the owner); the '47 seconds' tagline is intentional — do not flag it.
Finish by writing the report, then reply with a ~12-line summary with key counts.

input.description: Competitor UX research
input.prompt:
You are the competitor-UX RESEARCH agent for the Nxeon customer-portal redesign (Phase 1 = audit/research only). Nxeon is a Singapore-based cloud company selling VPS, shared hosting, game servers, domains and business email through a customer portal, with a free Minecraft tier and an AI website builder. You may use WebSearch and WebFetch. Do NOT touch anything under /opt/nxeon. Your ONLY write is your report file: /tmp/claude-0/-root/1716c7ee-ae35-4cf5-b557-9059709e07c4/scratchpad/audit-09-competitor-ux.md (Write tool).

RULE: extract UX PRINCIPLES and flow structures only. Do NOT describe or capture their visual design, colours, branding, illustrations, layouts-as-pixels, or copy to be reused. Nothing you write may be a template for copying. Cite sources (URLs) for each factual claim; if something is from memory rather than a fetched page, mark it MEMORY and keep it to well-known behaviour.

Cover: DigitalOcean, Hetzner Cloud, Vultr, AWS Lightsail, Akamai/Linode, Vercel, Render, Railway, Coolify, Cloudflare (registrar + DNS + dashboard), Namecheap, Porkbun, Google Workspace (signup/domain verification/mailbox setup), and game-server hosts (pick 4–5 of: Apex Hosting, Shockbyte, BisectHosting, Nitrado, G-Portal, Aternos, PebbleHost, Hostinger Game Panel, Pterodactyl-based panels).
For EACH product/company produce a structured entry:
- Purchase/deploy flow: ordered steps, what is asked BEFORE payment vs deferred, where payment sits, guest vs account-first, whether a 'draft' persists.
- Defaults & progressive disclosure: which decisions are defaulted, how 'advanced' is hidden, recommendation/'best for' cues, marketplace/one-click app positioning.
- Pricing presentation: hourly vs monthly, today-vs-renewal, add-on pricing, tax display, currency, promo handling, how they avoid surprise.
- Information hierarchy on the resource detail page: what is above the fold, primary actions vs danger zone placement, tab structure (names only).
- Navigation/IA: top-level grouping model (by product? by project? by task?), project/team scoping, global search/command palette scope.
- Post-purchase: what the user sees during provisioning (real progress? states?), first-value guidance (SSH/IP/connect info), setup checklists/onboarding.
- Error handling & trust: error copy structure, status pages, confirmations for destructive actions (typed confirm, what-will-be-lost), receipts/renewal reminders.
- Mobile behaviour if known.
- Notable UX PRINCIPLE (not visual) worth learning, and notable anti-pattern to avoid.
Then a CROSS-CUTTING SYNTHESIS: (a) the common step sequence in modern infra purchase flows and where they diverge per product type (compute vs domain vs email vs game); (b) a comparison table 'fields asked pre-payment' per competitor per product type; (c) principles for two-stage (checkout → post-payment setup) models and where competitors already do this; (d) IA models compared (product-centric vs project-centric vs task-centric) with pros/cons; (e) provisioning-progress honesty patterns; (f) domain-search UX principles; (g) email setup verification UX principles; (h) game-server picker principles (categorisation, player-count-to-plan recommendation, mod support signalling); (i) pricing transparency principles; (j) 12 concrete UX principles Nxeon should adopt, each with WHY and the evidence source; (k) 8 anti-patterns to avoid.
