Shared chrome facts (needed to read everything below) - **Nav** (`app/dashboard/layout.tsx:53-77`): these routes live in **two different sidebar groups**. - Group **"Network"** → `Domains` `/dashboard/domains` (icon `globe`), `Website builder`, `Calendar`, `SSL certificates` `/dashboard/ssl` (icon `shield`). - Group **"Mail"** → `Inbox` `/dashboard/mail` (icon `chat`), `Mailboxes` `/dashboard/email` (icon `server`). Comment at `layout.tsx:65-67` says Mailboxes was "formerly the ambiguous 'Business email'" — but the page still says Business Email (see §8). - `Domains` is feature-flagged behind `feature_domains` (`layout.tsx:24`, `:139`). SSL/Mail/Mailboxes are **not** flagged. - `Inbox` carries a live badge polled from `/api/mail/unread` every 60 s (`components/portal/Shell.tsx:425-441`). - **Content width** (`components/portal/Shell.tsx:973-981`): every route gets `mx-auto w-full flex-1 px-4 py-8 sm:px-6 max-w-7xl` — **except** full-bleed routes, which get `min-h-0 flex-1 overflow-hidden` with zero padding and no max-width. `/dashboard/mail` is in that full-bleed set (`Shell.tsx:285-292`). `/dashboard/email`, `/dashboard/ssl`, `/dashboard/domains*` are normal `max-w-7xl`. - **Two header components coexist**: `PortalHero` (`components/portal/PortalHero.tsx:80`) — big glass band, eyebrow, variant glyph, actions under the sub-text; and older `PageHeader` (`components/ui/primitives.tsx:4-22`) — plain `h1` + right-aligned actions, no decoration. ## 1. Domain step = datalist of ACTIVE domains without a sub, free-typing external allowed. Plan step = 3 cards + hardcoded "popular" pill on the middle + TermLadder (default annual). ` / card `PaymentStep`), PayPal/Coinbase stubbed off. You are one of several READ-ONLY audit agents for the Nxeon customer-portal redesign (Phase 1 = audit only, nothing gets implemented). Customer portal = app/dashboard/** + components/customer/** + components/portal/Shell.tsx (+ CommandPalette.tsx). API routes live under app/api/**.

HARD RULES: STRICTLY READ-ONLY. Do NOT edit/create/delete ANY file under /opt/nxeon, /opt/nxeon-staging or /opt/nxeon-sandbox. No build, npm, prisma, db, git-write, or service commands. Do not read .env* files or anything that looks like a secret. Your ONLY write is your report file: /tmp/claude-0/-root/1716c7ee-ae35-4cf5-b557-9059709e07c4/scratchpad/audit-01-routes-nav-ia.md (write it with the Write tool). Be exhaustive and factual, cite repo-relative file paths for every claim, use tables, mark anything uncertain as UNVERIFIED. This is an inventory + diagnosis, NOT a design proposal.

EFFICIENCY: use `ls -R`, `find`, `grep -rn` and `head`/`sed -n` ranges rather than reading whole large files; you have a big job, so batch independent shell calls in single messages and avoid re-reading files.

YOUR AUDIT: ROUTES / NAVIGATION / INFORMATION ARCHITECTURE.
Produce:
1. COMPLETE customer-facing route inventory. Walk app/dashboard/** recursively (every page.tsx, layout.tsx, loading.tsx, error.tsx, not-found, route groups, dynamic segments). Also find customer-facing routes OUTSIDE app/dashboard: order/checkout/deploy/pricing/login/signup/onboarding/verify/reset/partner/kodely-sso/riddle/whatever exists (list app/* top-level dirs and classify marketing vs portal vs admin vs api). For every portal route give: path pattern, one-line purpose, is it server or client component, main data sources (which API routes / server actions / prisma calls it hits), which feature flags gate it, whether it has loading/error boundaries, and the primary component files it renders.
2. NAVIGATION: dissect components/portal/Shell.tsx fully — sidebar groups + items + order + icons + badges + collapsed behaviour + which items are conditional (feature flags, account state, roles), top bar contents (search, notifications, account menu, currency, support), mobile behaviour, footer/support layer, any secondary nav (tabs inside product areas). Also dissect CommandPalette.tsx: what it indexes, categories, keyboard shortcuts, actions.
3. In-page sub-navigation: for each product area (servers, games, hosting, sites, domains, email/mail, volumes, nxcloud, build, projects, claude-code, migrate, tools, billing, settings, team, support) list the tabs/sections and how they're implemented (tabs component? query param? nested routes?). Note inconsistencies in tab implementation.
4. OVERLAP MAP: the known confusing overlap is servers vs games vs hosting vs sites vs build vs projects vs claude-code vs nxcloud vs volumes vs matrix vs deploy vs order vs tools. input.description: Audit purchase/deploy funnels
input.prompt:
You are one of several READ-ONLY audit agents for the Nxeon customer-portal redesign (Phase 1 = audit only). Codebase: /opt/nxeon (Next.js 15 App Router, Prisma/Postgres, Stripe, separate worker/ process). Customer portal = app/dashboard/** + components/customer/**; API under app/api/**; logic in lib/**; schema in prisma/schema.prisma. Products: VPS, Shared Hosting, Game Servers, Domains (name.com registrar), Business Email (Mailcow), plus Volumes, free Minecraft, Kodely/AI builder credits.

HARD RULES: STRICTLY READ-ONLY. Do NOT edit/create/delete ANY file under /opt/nxeon, /opt/nxeon-staging or /opt/nxeon-sandbox. No build, npm, prisma, db, git-write, or service commands. Do NOT touch the live database, Stripe, name.com, or infrastructure. Do not read .env* files. Your ONLY write is your report file: /tmp/claude-0/-root/1716c7ee-ae35-4cf5-b557-9059709e07c4/scratchpad/audit-07-funnels.md (Write tool). Exhaustive, factual, cite repo-relative file paths, use tables, mark uncertain items UNVERIFIED.

EFFICIENCY: batch independent shell calls; use grep/sed ranges over whole-file reads for the big wizard components; a deploy hub component (components/customer/DeployHub.tsx) and per-product wizards are the core of this audit.

NOTE: the domains + business-email funnels have ALREADY been audited in detail elsewhere; cover them only at the level needed for your cross-product comparison tables (steps, payment mechanism, pre- vs post-payment fields) and spend your effort on VPS, Shared Hosting, Game Servers.

YOUR AUDIT: PURCHASE + DEPLOYMENT FUNNELS, end-to-end, per product. This is the most business-critical audit. The owner wants to evaluate a two-stage model: (1) a short conversion-focused checkout that only asks for config that affects price/capacity/region/availability/eligibility/provisioning, with intelligent defaults for everything else; (2) an optional post-payment setup (OS/image, apps, hostname, SSH keys, security, WordPress, game settings) that users may skip if safely changeable later. You must gather the FACTS needed to judge that per product; do not design.
For EACH product (VPS, Shared Hosting, Game Servers, then briefly Domains, Business Email, Volumes, free-MC, AI credits, add-ons):
1. ENTRY POINTS: every route/CTA that starts the flow (marketing pricing pages, /order/*, /dashboard/deploy, product list empty states, upsells, Kodely partner flow), and whether logged-out users can start (guest checkout? signup mid-flow?).
2. STEP MAP: exact ordered steps, the component file for each, every field per step (name, type, default, validation, required?), price-affecting fields, and the URL/state mechanism (query params, local state, localStorage draft, DB draft/order record). Note auto-advance behaviour, back navigation and whether state is preserved, and what happens on page refresh or on leaving the wizard (draft saved?).
3. REQUIRED-BEFORE-PAYMENT vs POST-PAYMENT MATRIX: for every config field, classify: affects price / affects capacity / affects region-availability / affects eligibility / needed by provisioner at create time / purely cosmetic-or-changeable-later. For 'changeable later' cite the existing API route that changes it after provisioning (this determines whether it can move to a post-payment setup step WITHOUT backend changes). Flag fields that the provisioner needs at create time and that have no post-provision change API (these cannot move post-payment without backend work — backend must not change, so they must stay pre-payment or get a safe default).
4. CHECKOUT + PAYMENT: how payment is taken (Stripe Checkout Session redirect? Payment Element embedded? saved card charge? wallet/credits?), where billing details are collected, promo code handling (COMEBACK50, first-month-free HOSTING-ONLY, riddle $100 credit, referral codes), currency (display vs charge), tax/VAT, the order/subscription records created and their status enums, webhooks and what they trigger, idempotency, what the user sees while waiting for webhook, payment-failure path (does config survive? where does the user land?), 3DS handling, the deploy-abandonment win-back email trigger conditions (timer), analytics events fired per step.
5. POST-PAYMENT: exact redirect/landing after success per product, what provisioning status the client can see (endpoint, polling interval, SSE), the real state machine (list every status value and which worker step sets it), whether there is any 'setup' step today, and the first-value moment (SSH creds shown? game IP shown? site URL? DNS instructions?). What emails are sent at each stage.
6. RENEWALS / UPGRADES / ADD-ONS purchase paths (upgrade plan, add backups, add IP, add mailbox, renew domain, transfer domain in) — where and how they charge.
7. FRICTION LIST per product: concrete friction points with evidence (e.g. fields asked too early, no defaults, unclear price, hidden renewal price, no progress preserved, spinner-only waiting, dead ends, ambiguous CTA labels, terminology), and dead/broken/half-wired steps.
8. A consolidated 'funnel facts' table: product | steps today | fields today | fields that truly must be pre-payment | fields that can move post-payment with existing APIs | payment mechanism | provisioning states available | time-to-ready if known.
Finish by writing the report, then reply with a ~15-line summary including that consolidated table.

# NXEON DESIGN DIRECTION — clean-sheet draft (my own work; sections 8-14 of the blueprint)
# Written BEFORE audit results land, deliberately: identity is a clean-sheet mandate.

## 8. DESIGN PHILOSOPHY — "Engineered, not decorated"

Five principles, each with a testable consequence:

1. STRUCTURE OVER CONTAINERS. Hierarchy comes from rules, spacing and alignment, not from
   wrapping every thought in a bordered rectangle. Consequence: a card must represent an OBJECT
   (a server, a domain, a mailbox, a plan) or an ACTION GROUP. Prose, settings groups and
   sections get a labelled rule instead. Kills the "cards inside cards" look.
2. DATA IS THE ORNAMENT. The most visually interesting thing on any page should be real
   information: a metric, a status, an IP, a topology. No decorative glow, blob, or mesh earns
   space that data could use. Consequence: zero purely-decorative background art inside the app
   shell; atmosphere is a single very low-contrast field, never a feature.
3. ONE SIGNAL COLOUR AT A TIME. Colour means something: brand = the one primary action here;
   semantic = state. Consequence: at most ONE brand-filled control per view region; everything
   else is neutral. This is what stops the "everything is purple" problem.
4. PROGRESSIVE POWER. Every surface answers the beginner in its first screenful and the expert
   in its second. Consequence: default view = outcome language + recommended config; expert
   controls exist on the same page behind a named disclosure, never on a different page and
   never removed.
5. HONEST MACHINERY. The UI never claims more than the backend knows. Consequence: provisioning
   states, health, and progress map 1:1 to real backend states; where the backend only knows
   "provisioning", we say provisioning.

## 9. VISUAL IDENTITY

Navy stays as the foundation, but re-pitched from "purple-blue product" to "instrument panel".
Reference language: precision instruments, rack elevations, technical drawings, orbital/route
diagrams. NOT: sci-fi HUD, gaming RGB, glassmorphism, AI-startup gradient.

SIGNATURE ELEMENTS (the things that make a screenshot identifiably Nxeon):
- THE NOTCH. Object surfaces (a server, a domain, a game server, a plan) carry a single 10px
  chamfer on the top-left corner; container surfaces do not. A hardware cue that instantly
  separates "a thing you own" from "a box holding text". Radius otherwise small (6px), never 2xl.
- THE STATUS FILAMENT. A 2px full-height edge on the leading side of any resource row/card,
  carrying state colour. Live/transitional states get a slow travelling highlight; steady states
  are static. Replaces the dot + pill + coloured text triple-encoding used today.
- THE LABELLED RULE. Section headings sit ON a hairline: small-caps label, hairline continuing to
  the right edge. This is the primary grouping device and replaces most card borders.
- DATA PLATES. Technical values (IP, SSH, IDs, node, ports, DNS values, hashes) render on a
  recessed mono plate with an integral copy affordance. One treatment everywhere, so infra data
  reads as infra data.
- THE DEPLOYMENT LADDER. A vertical, honest provisioning timeline; each rung is a real backend
  state. Becomes the signature post-payment moment.
- TOPOLOGY, NOT CLIPART. Regions, networking and infrastructure are drawn as custom vector
  topology/route diagrams, never flags, stock maps or 3D server illustrations.

TYPOGRAPHY (recommendation + rationale)
- Display/UI: ARCHIVO (variable, incl. width axis). An American grotesque with engineered,
  slightly squared shapes; the width axis gives real display presence without huge sizes. Not
  the Inter/Space-Grotesk/Manrope default that reads "generic SaaS/AI".
- Data/technical: IBM PLEX MONO. Technical heritage, excellent digit texture, distinguishable
  0/O and 1/l — matters when the value is an IP or a hash.
- Labels: Archivo at small size, +tracking, small-caps treatment.
- FALLBACK PAIRING if a single-superfamily is preferred: IBM Plex Sans + IBM Plex Mono +
  IBM Plex Sans Condensed for labels.
- Rule: hierarchy comes from weight, width, tracking and colour before size. Display sizes stay
  modest; the interface should read compact and intelligent, never marketing-poster.

## 10. TOKENS (shape of the system; exact values to be finalised in Phase 2)
Layers: ink.base / ink.raised / surface / surface.raised / surface.interactive
Borders: hairline / hairline.strong (blue-grey, never neutral grey, never harsh)
Text: primary / secondary / muted / disabled / inverse
Brand: signal (azure, cooler + deeper than the generic 3b82f6, and deliberately not
  DigitalOcean's blue) / signal.hover / signal.subtle / signal.edge
Reserved: violet is DEMOTED to a single meaning — AI/Build surfaces only. This is how violet
  stops being wallpaper and starts being information.
Semantic: success (desaturated jade) / warning (amber) / danger (controlled vermillion) /
  info (azure) / neutral
Data-viz: a separate sequential + categorical ramp, cyan-leaning, tested on the navy layers.
Also: space (4-based), radius (2/6/10 + notch), elevation (shadow used sparingly; separation is
by layer + hairline, not by drop shadow), glow (ONE token, used only for live/active state),
motion (durations + easings), z-index, breakpoints, focus ring.
Governance: no component may use a raw hex. A lint rule should enforce it in Phase 2.

## 11-12. COMPONENTS + MOTION (headline decisions)
- One primitive library, one implementation per pattern; the audit's duplicate list is the
  backlog. Objects/containers/plates/rules are the four surface archetypes.
- Motion: 120/180/240ms bands, one standard easing + one entrance spring. Motion is only allowed
  to express state, causality, progress or continuity. Reduced-motion removes all of it except
  opacity. Signature motions: filament travel (live), ladder advance (provisioning), plate copy
  confirm, drawer directional slide, wizard horizontal step.

## 13-14. RESPONSIVE + A11Y (headline decisions)
- Tables become object cards below md, never horizontal scroll for primary content.
- Sidebar -> bottom-anchored drawer; wizard steps become a single-column stack with a persistent
  price/summary bar pinned to the bottom (the price must never scroll away on mobile).
- AA contrast minimum on all text incl. muted-on-navy (today's muted tones are the main risk);
  visible focus ring token on every interactive; every icon-only control gets a label; live
  regions for provisioning/async status; reduced-motion honoured system-wide.
EOF

Game rows navigate to `/dashboard/servers/{id}` (`games/page.tsx:108`), so the customer's mental model ("my game server") and the URL/nav highlight ("Servers") diverge on every click. NxCloud is a fourth `Server`-backed product that is *hidden* from the Servers list (`servers/page.tsx:16`) and has no nav entry at all. Volumes sits under **Compute** in the sidebar but under **Storage** in `PortalHero` (`PortalHero.tsx:72`). 331 332 ### P2. Seven orphan routes with no nav entry, reachable only by inline text links 333 `/dashboard/nxcloud` (no in-portal link whatsoever), `/dashboard/projects` (only from `ProjectAssign.tsx:23`), `/dashboard/invoices` (+`[id]`), `/dashboard/affiliate` (only two inline links, yet still listed in `FEATURE_HREF` at `layout.tsx:25`), `/dashboard/feedback` (only `support/page.tsx:31`), `/dashboard/free-minecraft` (marketing only), `/dashboard/order` (nothing at all). The layout's own comment claims Invoices was merged "as a tab on the billing page" (`layout.tsx:85-86`) — it is a stacked section, not a tab (`billing/page.tsx:885`). 334 335 ### P3. Naming does not survive first contact 336 - Two adjacent AI entries: **"Build with AI"** → `/dashboard/claude-code` (a docs/prompt library that builds nothing) and **"Matrix"** → `/dashboard/build` (the actual builder). Label and URL are swapped relative to each other. 337 - "Website builder" (`/dashboard/sites`) vs "Websites" inside Shared Hosting vs `Website` rows inside a VPS control panel — three unrelated things called websites. 338 - "Inbox" vs "Mailboxes" needed a five-line explanatory comment in the nav definition (`layout.tsx:64-67`) to be distinguishable. 339 - The Resize tab is labelled "Upgrade" while its key, URL and every internal reference stay `resize` (`ServerTabs.tsx:20-25`). 340 - "Shared Hosting" vs "Servers" vs "Website builder" all use the same `globe`/`server` icons. 341 342 ### P4. Five incompatible tab mechanisms; two of them break Back and deep-linking 343 `ServerTabs` and `HostingTabs` switch tabs with `window.history.replaceState` (`ServerTabs.tsx:95`, `HostingTabs.tsx:62`), so the URL changes but no history entry is pushed — **Back leaves the page entirely** — and `?tab=` is honoured only on first render. `Settings` and `Games` use real `` navigations. `DeployHub` uses `router.replace` + `useSearchParams`. `FreeMcDashboard` and `HostingClient` keep tab/filter state purely in `useState` with **no URL at all**, so a customer cannot link a teammate to "the Roles tab of my free server". Billing has no tabs at all despite carrying six distinct concerns. 344 345 ### P5. A sidebar item ejects the customer from the portal 346 "Server Directory" points at `/game-servers/directory` (`layout.tsx:45`), which is `app/(marketing)/game-servers/directory/page.tsx` and therefore renders inside `MarketingLayout` — different header, different footer, no sidebar, no way back except browser Back. 347 348 ### P6. Flat 25-item sidebar with a shallow, mismatched taxonomy 349 Seven groups, but the grouping labels (`Compute`/`Build`/`Network`/`Mail`/`Tools`/`Account`) disagree with the `PortalHero` eyebrow taxonomy on the pages themselves (`Storage` for volumes, `Workspace` for projects, `Deploy` for order — none of which exist as sidebar groups). Group collapse is deliberately disabled for customers (`Shell.tsx:571`), so all 21 default-visible items are always expanded. Nothing in the sidebar is ever contextual to what the customer actually owns — a customer with one VPS sees the same 21 rows as one with hosting, domains, mail and a partner account. 350 351 ### P7. Purchase entry points are scattered across two incompatible patterns 352 The Deploy hub is described in-code as "a single source of truth for the money-audited flow" (`games/page.tsx:14`, `hosting/page.tsx:9`) but covers only 4 of ~11 purchasable things. Domains, email, volumes, NxCloud, wallet top-ups, dedicated IPs, extra disk, Backup+, resizes and hosting upgrades all buy in-page, each with its own layout and its own payment step. The hub's own "Business Email" card doesn't even open a wizard — it links out to `/dashboard/email` (`DeployHub.tsx:357`). 353 354 ### P8. Missing route-level scaffolding 355 One `loading.tsx` and one `error.tsx` for 58 routes, both at `/dashboard`. No `not-found.tsx` under `/dashboard`, so all six `notFound()` paths render the root 404 **outside** the portal Shell. Nine of the heaviest pages (`servers/[id]` doing Proxmox round-trips, `mail` doing IMAP, `games?tab=free` doing SSH) have no per-route `loading.tsx` and no `Suspense` boundary — only `/dashboard/deploy` has one (`deploy/page.tsx:287`). 356 357 ### P9. The command palette is a search box, not a command palette 358 No actions of any kind — no "deploy", "add funds", "open ticket", "restart server". It also fails to index volumes, SSL, invoices, projects, sites, nxcloud, migrations and free-MC servers (`app/api/search/route.ts`), and three of its result types resolve to a list page rather than the item. The trigger button fakes a `⌘K` `KeyboardEvent` on `window` instead of calling the palette (`Shell.tsx:838-843`). 359 360 ### P10. Layout/header inconsistency across the portal 361 34 pages use `PortalHero`, 4 use `PageHeader`, `/dashboard/hosting` deliberately switched to `PageHeader` (`hosting/page.tsx:14-18`), `/dashboard/sites` and `/dashboard/sites/[id]` render neither, `/dashboard/whats-new` uses a bare `

`, and `/dashboard/build` renders `aria-hidden` empty space that a shell-level fixed panel paints over. There is no shared page-shell contract. 362 363 ### Smaller observations 364 - `/dashboard/settings` is reachable on the admin and staff hostnames by design (`middleware.ts:29`); it is the only customer page that is. 365 - Middleware performs **no auth** — every gate is in `app/dashboard/layout.tsx`. A future route outside `/dashboard` would be unprotected by default. 366 - The sidebar balance card prints raw USD (`Shell.tsx:769`) while the top bar offers a `CurrencySwitcher` — the two disagree by design, but the customer isn't told. 367 - The homepage duplicates `MarketingHeader`/`Footer`/`PromoBar` instead of living in the `(marketing)` group (`app/page.tsx:100,316`). 368 - `lib/kb-system.ts:696-721` maintains a **hand-curated 26-entry portal page index** for the chat agent that is already drifting from the real route table (it lists `/dashboard/invoices`, `/dashboard/projects`, `/dashboard/affiliate`, `/dashboard/nxcloud` as first-class pages, and omits `deploy?product=`, `mail`, `whats-new`, `partner`, `sites`, `calendar`, `feedback`, `free-minecraft`). 369 - 17 `app/(marketing)/preview/*` design-preview pages and `app/(marketing)/v2` ship in the production route tree. 370

The Compute group has no consistent object model — one list per *product name*, one detail page per *backend table* "Servers", "Game Servers" and "Free Minecraft" are three nav-level concepts over two backends. Game rows navigate to `/dashboard/servers/{id}` (`games/page.tsx:108`), so the customer's mental model ("my game server") and the URL/nav highlight ("Servers") diverge on every click. NxCloud is a fourth `Server`-backed product that is *hidden* from the Servers list (`servers/page.tsx:16`) and has no nav entry at all. Volumes sits under **Compute** in the sidebar but under **Storage** in `PortalHero` (`PortalHero.tsx:72`). ### P2. Seven orphan routes with no nav entry, reachable only by inline text links `/dashboard/nxcloud` (no in-portal link whatsoever), `/dashboard/projects` (only from `ProjectAssign.tsx:23`), `/dashboard/invoices` (+`[id]`), `/dashboard/affiliate` (only two inline links, yet still listed in `FEATURE_HREF` at `layout.tsx:25`), `/dashboard/feedback` (only `support/page.tsx:31`), `/dashboard/free-minecraft` (marketing only), `/dashboard/order` (nothing at all). The layout's own comment claims Invoices was merged "as a tab on the billing page" (`layout.tsx:85-86`) — it is a stacked section, not a tab (`billing/page.tsx:885`). ### P3. Naming does not survive first contact - Two adjacent AI entries: **"Build with AI"** → `/dashboard/claude-code` (a docs/prompt library that builds nothing) and **"Matrix"** → `/dashboard/build` (the actual builder). Label and URL are swapped relative to each other. - "Website builder" (`/dashboard/sites`) vs "Websites" inside Shared Hosting vs `Website` rows inside a VPS control panel — three unrelated things called websites. - "Inbox" vs "Mailboxes" needed a five-line explanatory comment in the nav definition (`layout.tsx:64-67`) to be distinguishable. - The Resize tab is labelled "Upgrade" while its key, URL and every internal reference stay `resize` (`ServerTabs.tsx:20-25`). - "Shared Hosting" vs "Servers" vs "Website builder" all use the same `globe`/`server` icons. ### P4. Five incompatible tab mechanisms; two of them break Back and deep-linking `ServerTabs` and `HostingTabs` switch tabs with `window.history.replaceState` (`ServerTabs.tsx:95`, `HostingTabs.tsx:62`), so the URL changes but no history entry is pushed — **Back leaves the page entirely** — and `?tab=` is honoured only on first render. `Settings` and `Games` use real `` navigations. `DeployHub` uses `router.replace` + `useSearchParams`. `FreeMcDashboard` and `HostingClient` keep tab/filter state purely in `useState` with **no URL at all**, so a customer cannot link a teammate to "the Roles tab of my free server". Billing has no tabs at all despite carrying six distinct concerns. ### P5. A sidebar item ejects the customer from the portal "Server Directory" points at `/game-servers/directory` (`layout.tsx:45`), which is `app/(marketing)/game-servers/directory/page.tsx` and therefore renders inside `MarketingLayout` — different header, different footer, no sidebar, no way back except browser Back. ### P6. Flat 25-item sidebar with a shallow, mismatched taxonomy Seven groups, but the grouping labels (`Compute`/`Build`/`Network`/`Mail`/`Tools`/`Account`) disagree with the `PortalHero` eyebrow taxonomy on the pages themselves (`Storage` for volumes, `Workspace` for projects, `Deploy` for order — none of which exist as sidebar groups). Group collapse is deliberately disabled for customers (`Shell.tsx:571`), so all 21 default-visible items are always expanded. Nothing in the sidebar is ever contextual to what the customer actually owns — a customer with one VPS sees the same 21 rows as one with hosting, domains, mail and a partner account. ### P7. Purchase entry points are scattered across two incompatible patterns The Deploy hub is described in-code as "a single source of truth for the money-audited flow" (`games/page.tsx:14`, `hosting/page.tsx:9`) but covers only 4 of ~11 purchasable things. Domains, email, volumes, NxCloud, wallet top-ups, dedicated IPs, extra disk, Backup+, resizes and hosting upgrades all buy in-page, each with its own layout and its own payment step. The hub's own "Business Email" card doesn't even open a wizard — it links out to `/dashboard/email` (`DeployHub.tsx:357`). ### P8. Missing route-level scaffolding One `loading.tsx` and one `error.tsx` for 58 routes, both at `/dashboard`. No `not-found.tsx` under `/dashboard`, so all six `notFound()` paths render the root 404 **outside** the portal Shell. Nine of the heaviest pages (`servers/[id]` doing Proxmox round-trips, `mail` doing IMAP, `games?tab=free` doing SSH) have no per-route `loading.tsx` and no `Suspense` boundary — only `/dashboard/deploy` has one (`deploy/page.tsx:287`). ### P9. The command palette is a search box, not a command palette No actions of any kind — no "deploy", "add funds", "open ticket", "restart server". It also fails to index volumes, SSL, invoices, projects, sites, nxcloud, migrations and free-MC servers (`app/api/search/route.ts`), and three of its result types resolve to a list page rather than the item. The trigger button fakes a `⌘K` `KeyboardEvent` on `window` instead of calling the palette (`Shell.tsx:838-843`). ### P10. Layout/header inconsistency across the portal 34 pages use `PortalHero`, 4 use `PageHeader`, `/dashboard/hosting` deliberately switched to `PageHeader` (`hosting/page.tsx:14-18`), `/dashboard/sites` and `/dashboard/sites/[id]` render neither, `/dashboard/whats-new` uses a bare `

# IA PROPOSAL DRAFT (blueprint section 7) — grounded in audit-01

## The core diagnosis to fix
The sidebar is organised by PRODUCT NAME (25 items, 7 groups) while the app is organised by
BACKEND TABLE. Game servers are `Server` rows, so a game server's detail page is
/dashboard/servers/{id}: label, URL and nav highlight disagree on every click. NxCloud is a
fourth Server-backed product hidden from the Servers list with no nav entry. Nothing in the
sidebar is contextual to what the customer owns: one VPS or a full estate, both see 21 rows.

## Principle
Navigate by OBJECT, not by product-name. A customer thinks "my Minecraft server", "my site",
"my domain", "my mailbox". They never think "a Proxmox VM with gamePlanId set".
Corollary: one detail-page contract per object KIND, and the URL says what the object is.

## Proposed structure (6 top-level, plus contextual object routes)

HOME                     the estate: what I have, what needs me, what I'm spending
DEPLOY                   one hub, ALL purchasable things (today it covers 4 of ~11)
RESOURCES                one unified inventory of everything I own, filterable by kind
  - the list is ONE surface with kind filters (VPS - Game - Hosting - Site - Volume -
    NxCloud - Free Minecraft), not five sidebar rows over two backends
  - object routes become /dashboard/r/{kind}/{id} so the URL states the kind and the nav
    highlight is always right. Existing /dashboard/servers/{id} keeps working as a redirect
    (frontend-only change; no backend contract moves)
DOMAINS & MAIL           domains, DNS, SSL, mailboxes, inbox - the "identity" cluster
  - SSL moves here from its own row: it is an attribute of a domain, not a product
BUILD                    the AI builder (today "Matrix" at /dashboard/build) + the guides hub
  (today mislabelled "Build with AI" at /dashboard/claude-code) merged into ONE surface with
  a Guides tab. Two adjacent AI rows whose labels are swapped vs their URLs is indefensible.
ACCOUNT                  billing (invoices as a real tab), team, support, activity, referrals,
  partner, settings, what's new

Tools (16 utilities) demote from a sidebar row to a command-palette surface + a footer link;
they are duplicated verbatim at /tools/* on marketing and do not earn permanent nav weight.
Server Directory leaves the sidebar: it ejects the customer into the marketing layout.

## Rules the new IA must enforce
1. Every route has a nav home. Kills the seven orphans: nxcloud, projects, invoices,
   affiliate, feedback, free-minecraft, order. Projects becomes a grouping FILTER on Resources
   rather than a hidden page; invoices becomes a Billing tab; order dies; free-minecraft
   becomes a kind filter with the old URL kept as a redirect for marketing deep links.
2. One tab mechanism, URL-addressable, Back-safe. Today there are five, and the two most-used
   (ServerTabs, HostingTabs) use replaceState so Back exits the page and ?tab= only works on
   first render. New rule: tabs are real routes or pushState, always deep-linkable.
3. One page-shell contract. Today: 34 pages PortalHero, 4 PageHeader, 2 neither, 1 bare h1,
   1 aria-hidden void. One PageHeader primitive, one content width, one section rule.
4. The sidebar adapts to the estate. Kinds the customer owns are pinned; kinds they don't own
   collapse into "Explore" under Deploy. A one-VPS customer should not carry 21 rows.
5. The command palette becomes a real command palette: actions (deploy, add funds, restart,
   open ticket) plus the 8 entity types currently unindexed (volumes, SSL, invoices, projects,
   sites, nxcloud, migrations, free-MC).

echo ok

**Summary**

All four deploy products share one route (`app/dashboard/deploy/page.tsx` → `DeployHub.tsx`, tabbed on `?product=`), and one payment surface (`PaymentStep.tsx`, Stripe Custom Checkout embedded, settling through the idempotent `lib/fulfil-checkout.ts` bus). Pricing is provably display===charge: every wizard derives numbers from the same pure modules the server bills from, and the sold price is frozen into Stripe metadata.

The two-stage model is well supported on **Game** (nearly every Settings field is changeable via `saveGameConfig`, including `phase:"deploy"` ones — that flag means "restart", not "immutable"), partly on **Hosting** (domain and app install both have post-provision APIs; extra storage does not), and least on **VPS**, where four fields the provisioner consumes at clone time have **no post-provision change API at all**: `hostname` (`renameServer` only writes `label`), `sshPublicKey`, `addons.docker` and `addons.malwareScanner` (cloud-init one-shots). The Add-ons step's copy — "You can add or remove these later in your VPS dashboard" — is untrue for docker and malware.

Notable hard findings: marketing CTAs are 38 bare `href="/register"` links that discard the plan/product choice at signup; a page refresh mid-wizard loses everything (drafts are written but only read back on `?canceled=1`); `?paid=1` and `?pending=1` are written by six redirect sites and read by none, so paid-but-unfulfilled orders and all PayPal/Coinbase returns land silently; shared hosting sends **no email and no in-app notification** when an account goes ACTIVE; game orders charge **no VAT** while VPS does; and there is **no game tier upgrade or downgrade path** — `lib/resize.ts:97` refuses and points at a setting that doesn't exist.

| Product | Steps | Fields | Must stay pre-pay | Can move post-pay (existing API) | Payment | States |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| VPS | 5–6 | 14 | plan, term, IP, disk, backupTier, coupon; **imageId, hostname, pubKey, docker, malware (no change API)** | dedicatedIp, extraDisk, backupTier, autoBackup, plan (resize), OS (destructive reinstall) | Stripe embedded + GPay/ApplePay + PayPal + Coinbase + wallet | PENDING→PROVISIONING(6 labels)→RUNNING\|ERROR |
| Hosting | 5 | 7 | plan, term, **extraDiskGB (no API)** | domain/subdomain, appSlug | Stripe embedded + wallet + separate `mode:setup` card popup | PENDING→PROVISIONING(7 labels)→ACTIVE\|FAILED + HostingTask |
| Game | 4 | 8 + ≤9 schema | gamePlanId, term, IP, family, `required:true` fields | serverName, subdomain, variant, **all** config | Stripe embedded + wallet, no tax | PENDING→PROVISIONING(6)→RUNNING\|ERROR |
| Email | 3 | 4 | domain, plan, term | mailboxes, DNS verify | Stripe embedded + wallet | no overlay |
| Domains | 4–5 | domain, years, 9-field ICANN contact | all | — | Stripe embedded + wallet (renewals wallet-only) | active/refunded/needs-review |
| Volumes | 1 | size | size | attach later | **wallet only, no card** | attach job |

Win-back (`COMEBACK50`, 50% off) fires 30 min after the last funnel step, up to 30 days, capped 25/sweep — but `deploy_winback_enabled` defaults **off**, as do `email_verification_enforced`, `free_minecraft_enabled` and `nxcloud_ordering_enabled`; I could not check prod's live `Setting` values, so those are marked UNVERIFIED.</result>

You are one of several READ-ONLY audit agents for the Nxeon customer-portal redesign (Phase 1 = audit only). Codebase: /opt/nxeon (Next.js 15 App Router). Customer portal = app/dashboard/** + components/customer/** + components/portal/**. Static assets in public/**.

HARD RULES: STRICTLY READ-ONLY. Do NOT edit/create/delete ANY file under /opt/nxeon, /opt/nxeon-staging or /opt/nxeon-sandbox. No build, npm, prisma, db, git-write, or service commands. Do not read .env* files. Your ONLY write is your report file: /tmp/claude-0/-root/1716c7ee-ae35-4cf5-b557-9059709e07c4/scratchpad/audit-03-assets.md (Write tool). Exhaustive, factual, cite repo-relative file paths, use tables, mark uncertain items UNVERIFIED.

EFFICIENCY: use find/du/file and ImageMagick `identify` in batched shell calls to inventory quickly. Only open (Read) an image when its filename does not make its content obvious, and prefer opening a downscaled copy written to /tmp. Do not open more than ~20 images.

YOUR AUDIT: VISUAL ASSET INVENTORY with a KEEP / REWORK / REPLACE / REMOVE verdict per asset. The owner's rule: the default for DECORATIVE assets is REPLACE; nothing gets recycled merely because it exists; the logo/wordmark and legitimately-sourced game artwork are the main KEEP candidates; screenshots are never an asset source.
Produce:
1. public/** inventory: every image/svg/video/font/ico file. Group by folder (logos, game art/heroes/posters, illustrations, backgrounds, icons, og images, favicons, one-click app icons, OS icons, region/flag images, misc). For each (or each GROUP where a folder holds many near-identical files): path, dimensions, size, format, what it depicts, where referenced (grep the filename; flag UNREFERENCED files), and a verdict with a one-line reason. For game artwork note whether it appears to be official key art vs generated, and any licensing notes findable in the repo.
2. Logo / wordmark treatments: every Nxeon logo variant (svg/png, colour variants, favicon, og image, email logo, loading logo), where used, inconsistencies.
3. Inline decorative graphics inside portal components: grep for `<svg` in components/customer, components/portal, app/dashboard — glows, blobs, orbs, grids, mesh gradients, noise, hero backdrops, gradient text. List each with file:line and verdict. Distinguish DECORATIVE svg from FUNCTIONAL svg (icons, charts) — charts and icons are not decoration.
4. CSS-generated decoration: background-image utilities, radial/conic gradients in globals.css or components, animated backgrounds, blur orbs — list with verdict.
5. Empty-state / onboarding / success / error illustrations: what exists, style consistency, verdict.
6. Game catalogue visuals: the manifest/lib file listing games, image fields, aspect ratios, per-game hero/poster/logo, count of games, missing images, mixed aspect ratios.
7. One-click app / OS / region imagery: what represents Ubuntu/Debian/Docker/WordPress etc. and regions, source and verdict.
8. Email template imagery (lib/email-templates.ts or an emails/ dir) — list only, verdict.
9. Summary table: counts per verdict, plus the shortlist of what a NEW asset library must provide (categories + rough counts), without designing them.
Finish by writing the report, then reply with a ~10-line summary with counts per verdict.

**Summary**

All four deploy products share one route (`app/dashboard/deploy/page.tsx` → `DeployHub.tsx`, tabbed on `?product=`), and one payment surface (`PaymentStep.tsx`, Stripe Custom Checkout embedded, settling through the idempotent `lib/fulfil-checkout.ts` bus). Pricing is provably display===charge: every wizard derives numbers from the same pure modules the server bills from, and the sold price is frozen into Stripe metadata.

The two-stage model is well supported on **Game** (nearly every Settings field is changeable via `saveGameConfig`, including `phase:"deploy"` ones — that flag means "restart", not "immutable"), partly on **Hosting** (domain and app install both have post-provision APIs; extra storage does not), and least on **VPS**, where four fields the provisioner consumes at clone time have **no post-provision change API at all**: `hostname` (`renameServer` only writes `label`), `sshPublicKey`, `addons.docker` and `addons.malwareScanner` (cloud-init one-shots). The Add-ons step's copy — "You can add or remove these later in your VPS dashboard" — is untrue for docker and malware.

Notable hard findings: marketing CTAs are 38 bare `href="/register"` links that discard the plan/product choice at signup; a page refresh mid-wizard loses everything (drafts are written but only read back on `?canceled=1`); `?paid=1` and `?pending=1` are written by six redirect sites and read by none, so paid-but-unfulfilled orders and all PayPal/Coinbase returns land silently; shared hosting sends **no email and no in-app notification** when an account goes ACTIVE; game orders charge **no VAT** while VPS does; and there is **no game tier upgrade or downgrade path** — `lib/resize.ts:97` refuses and points at a setting that doesn't exist.

| Product | Steps | Fields | Must stay pre-pay | Can move post-pay (existing API) | Payment | States |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| VPS | 5–6 | 14 | plan, term, IP, disk, backupTier, coupon; **imageId, hostname, pubKey, docker, malware (no change API)** | dedicatedIp, extraDisk, backupTier, autoBackup, plan (resize), OS (destructive reinstall) | Stripe embedded + GPay/ApplePay + PayPal + Coinbase + wallet | PENDING→PROVISIONING(6 labels)→RUNNING\|ERROR |
| Hosting | 5 | 7 | plan, term, **extraDiskGB (no API)** | domain/subdomain, appSlug | Stripe embedded + wallet + separate `mode:setup` card popup | PENDING→PROVISIONING(7 labels)→ACTIVE\|FAILED + HostingTask |
| Game | 4 | 8 + ≤9 schema | gamePlanId, term, IP, family, `required:true` fields | serverName, subdomain, variant, **all** config | Stripe embedded + wallet, no tax | PENDING→PROVISIONING(6)→RUNNING\|ERROR |
| Email | 3 | 4 | domain, plan, term | mailboxes, DNS verify | Stripe embedded + wallet | no overlay |
| Domains | 4–5 | domain, years, 9-field ICANN contact | all | — | Stripe embedded + wallet (renewals wallet-only) | active/refunded/needs-review |
| Volumes | 1 | size | size | attach later | **wallet only, no card** | attach job |

Win-back (`COMEBACK50`, 50% off) fires 30 min after the last funnel step, up to 30 days, capped 25/sweep — but `deploy_winback_enabled` defaults **off**, as do `email_verification_enforced`, `free_minecraft_enabled` and `nxcloud_ordering_enabled`; I could not check prod's live `Setting` values, so those are marked UNVERIFIED.</result>

input.prompt:
You are one of several READ-ONLY audit agents for the Nxeon customer-portal redesign (Phase 1 = audit only). Codebase: /opt/nxeon (Next.js 15 App Router, React 19, Tailwind v4). Customer portal = app/dashboard/** + components/customer/** + components/portal/**.

HARD RULES: STRICTLY READ-ONLY. Do NOT edit/create/delete ANY file under /opt/nxeon, /opt/nxeon-staging or /opt/nxeon-sandbox. No build, npm, prisma, db, git-write, or service commands. Do not read .env* files. Do NOT log in to the live site or hit the live portal. Your ONLY write is your report file: /tmp/claude-0/-root/1716c7ee-ae35-4cf5-b557-9059709e07c4/scratchpad/audit-08-states-responsive-a11y-terms.md (Write tool). Exhaustive, factual, cite repo-relative file:line, use tables, mark uncertain items UNVERIFIED. Inventory + diagnosis, no design proposals.

EFFICIENCY: this is mostly grep/count work — use `grep -rn`, `grep -rc`, and `| sort | uniq -c | sort -rn` pipelines, batched in single messages.

CONTEXT FROM COMPLETED SIBLING AUDITS (do not re-derive): there is exactly ONE loading.tsx and ONE error.tsx for all 58 portal routes, both at app/dashboard/; there is no not-found.tsx under /dashboard. There are no toast/dialog/motion libraries in package.json — everything is hand-rolled. Every destructive VPS action uses window.confirm. Five different tab mechanisms coexist. Do NOT re-audit routes or the design-token system; a sibling owns those.

YOUR AUDIT: UI STATES / RESPONSIVE / ACCESSIBILITY / TERMINOLOGY / COPY.
1. LOADING STATES: the single loading.tsx; every skeleton component; every spinner implementation (count distinct); pages that show nothing while loading; long-running action feedback (provisioning overlays, reboot, DNS propagation, payment) and what the user actually sees; Suspense usage; optimistic updates; AutoRefresh/polling components and their intervals.
2. EMPTY STATES: for every list/collection in the portal (servers, games, hosting, sites, domains, mailboxes, volumes, invoices, tickets, activity, team, ssh keys, snapshots, backups, dns records, free-MC, projects, migrations) what the empty state shows (text + CTA + illustration) and how many distinct implementations exist.
3. ERROR STATES: the single error.tsx; error boundaries; how API/action errors surface (toast? inline? alert? thrown?); the actual error copy (grep 'Something went wrong', 'Failed to', 'error' strings) and whether errors say what happened / why / how to fix; retry affordances; 'technical details' disclosure; what a customer sees when a server action fails; 404 handling inside the portal.
4. SUCCESS STATES: after create/deploy/pay/save — toast, redirect, inline, or nothing; any celebration effects.
5. TOASTS / NOTIFICATIONS / BANNERS: how many notification mechanisms exist (hand-rolled toast? inline result boxes? the notification bell? banners?), their variants and positions; every banner type (promo, unverified email, impersonation, overdue, degraded chat, maintenance).
6. MODALS / DRAWERS / DIALOGS: every implementation and count; focus trapping; Escape/overlay close; how many use window.confirm / window.prompt instead of a real dialog (count and list them); whether confirmations state what happens, what is lost, and reversibility; typed-confirm patterns.
7. RESPONSIVE: Shell behaviour below lg (drawer), tables on mobile (overflow-x vs stacked cards — count min-w-[...] on tables), wizards/checkout on mobile, server/hosting panel tabs on mobile, charts on mobile, the terminal/console and file manager on mobile, fixed-width hazards (grep min-w-, w-[NNNpx], grid-cols-N without a breakpoint prefix), touch-target sizes. List the specific pages most likely to break and why.
8. ACCESSIBILITY: counts of aria-*, role=, aria-label; icon-only buttons WITHOUT an accessible name (list them); focus-visible styling; keyboard support in custom dropdowns/tabs/menus/command palette; prefers-reduced-motion handling; colour-contrast risk (list the text utilities used for secondary/muted text and the surface colours they sit on, and estimate which fail AA); form label association (count label htmlFor / aria-labelledby vs input/select/textarea); skip links; heading order; img without alt; live regions (aria-live) for async status.
9. TERMINOLOGY: build a glossary of every user-facing noun for the same concept and where each appears — server/VPS/instance/machine/node; game server/game; hosting/website/site/project/app/plan/account; domain/DNS/zone; mailbox/inbox/email/Business Email; plan/tier/package/size; region/location/node/datacenter; snapshot/backup/image; deploy/order/create/launch/provision/buy/checkout; team/org/workspace; wallet/balance/credits/funds. Note internal jargon leaking to customers (Proxmox, Mailcow, name.com, vmid, node IDs, worker, job, prisma). Note CTA label inconsistencies (Continue/Next/Deploy/Order/Buy/Pay/Place order).
10. COPY TONE: sample ~20 headings/subheads/CTAs across pages to characterise tone inconsistency; any placeholder/TODO/lorem copy; any customer-facing copy implying a third-party infrastructure provider exists (Nxeon must speak as the owner — flag these); NOTE: the '47 seconds' tagline is an intentional brand line, do NOT flag it.
Finish by writing the report, then reply with a ~12-line summary with key counts.

1	# Audit 07 — Purchase + Deployment Funnels (READ-ONLY, Phase 1)
2	
3	Codebase: `/opt/nxeon` @ 2026-09-03. All paths repo-relative. Facts only; no design proposals.
4	Anything I could not verify from source is marked **UNVERIFIED** (I did not touch the DB, Stripe,
5	name.com or any service).
6	
7	---
8	
9	## 0. Architecture in one paragraph
10	
11	All four "deploy" products live behind ONE route, `app/dashboard/deploy/page.tsx`, which is a server
12	component that fetches everything for all four wizards and hands them to
13	`components/customer/DeployHub.tsx`. The hub is a tab strip (`?product=vps|hosting|game|email`,
14	`router.replace`, no navigation) that mounts exactly one wizard at a time:
15	
16	| product | wizard component | server action entry |
17	|---|---|---|
18	| VPS | `components/customer/DeployWizard.tsx` (1913 L) | `payAndDeploy` (`lib/actions.ts:513`) |
19	| Shared Hosting | `components/customer/HostingDeployWizard.tsx` (1044 L) | `placeHostingOrder` (`lib/actions-hosting.ts:453`) |
20	| Game Servers | `components/customer/GameDeployWizard.tsx` (1659 L) | `payAndDeployGame` (`lib/actions-gameplans.ts:201`) |
21	| Business Email | `components/customer/EmailHosting.tsx` (1440 L) | `orderEmailHosting` (`lib/actions-email-hosting.ts:256`) |
22	
23	Domains have their own routes (`/dashboard/domains/register`, `/dashboard/domains/transfer`) and are
24	NOT in the hub. `app/dashboard/order/page.tsx` is a bare `redirect("/dashboard/deploy")`.
25	
26	Payment is uniform: an embedded `components/customer/PaymentStep.tsx` mounting a **Stripe Custom
27	Checkout session** (`ui_mode: "elements"`), plus PayPal and Coinbase rails that are only wired for
28	VPS. Everything settles through the single idempotent bus `lib/fulfil-checkout.ts`.
29	
30	---
31	
32	## 1. ENTRY POINTS
33	
34	### 1.1 Every route/CTA that starts a purchase flow
35	
36	| Entry | File | Target | Carries product? | Carries plan? |
37	|---|---|---|---|---|
38	| Portal nav "Deploy" | `app/dashboard/layout.tsx:40` | `/dashboard/deploy` | no (defaults to `vps`) | no |
39	| Dashboard home CTA ×2 | `app/dashboard/page.tsx` | `/dashboard/deploy` | no | no |
40	| Servers list + empty state | `app/dashboard/servers/page.tsx` | `/dashboard/deploy` | no | no |
41	| Games list + empty state | `app/dashboard/games/page.tsx` | `/dashboard/deploy?product=game` | yes | no |
42	| Hosting list + empty state | `app/dashboard/hosting/page.tsx`, `components/customer/HostingClient.tsx` | `/dashboard/deploy?product=hosting` | yes | no |
43	| Billing page ×2 | `app/dashboard/billing/page.tsx` | `/dashboard/deploy` | no | no |
44	| SSL page cross-sell | `components/customer/SslCertificates.tsx` | `/dashboard/deploy` | no | no |
45	| Claude Code hub ×2 | `components/customer/claude-code/ClaudeCodeHub.tsx` | `/dashboard/deploy` | no | no |
46	| Onboarding checklist | `lib/actions-onboarding.ts:57` | `/dashboard/deploy` | no | no |
47	| Marketing game configurator | `components/marketing/showcase/GameConfigurator.tsx:33` | `/dashboard/deploy?product=game` | yes | no |
48	| KB / chat-agent deep links | `lib/kb-plans.ts:45-48` | `?product=hosting|vps|game|email` | yes | no |
49	| Kodely partner SSO | `app/api/partner/checkout/route.ts:36,42` | `/dashboard/deploy?product=vps&ref=kodely` / `product=hosting&ref=kodely` | yes | no |
50	| Email templates | `lib/email-templates.ts:48` | `/dashboard/deploy` | no | no |
51	| Deploy win-back email | `worker/deploy-winback.ts` | deploy URL + `COMEBACK50` code | no | no |
52	| Marketing pricing cards | `components/marketing/PricingGrid.tsx`, `components/marketing/ProductPricing.tsx` | **`/register`** (bare) | **no** | **no** |
53	| Domains | `/dashboard/domains/register?...`, `/dashboard/domains/transfer` | n/a | n/a | domain carried via `initialDomain` |
54	
55	### 1.2 Guest checkout / signup mid-flow
56	
57	- **No guest checkout anywhere.** Every wizard route is under `/dashboard/**` and every action calls
58	  `requireUser()` first. `app/dashboard/deploy/page.tsx:37` starts with `await requireUser()`.
59	- **Marketing → purchase loses everything.** 38 marketing CTAs resolve to a bare `href="/register"`
60	  (`components/marketing/PricingGrid.tsx`, `components/marketing/ProductPricing.tsx`, etc.). The
61	  register page supports `?next=` (`app/register/page.tsx:27`, validated by `safeNext`), and
62	  `register()` honours it (`lib/actions.ts` ~line 320), but **no marketing CTA sets `next`** — only
63	  `components/AuthForms.tsx:260` (login→register handoff) does. So a visitor who clicks "Buy Starter"
64	  on `/pricing` signs up and lands on `/dashboard?signup=1`, not on the deploy wizard with Starter
65	  selected. Plan/product/term choice is discarded at the signup boundary.
66	- `?ref=` is captured into cookies at both ends: `ReferralCapture` (register page, `nxeon_ref`, 30d)
67	  and `PartnerSourceCapture` (every dashboard page, `nx_partner_ref`, 24h,
68	  `KNOWN_PARTNERS = ["kodely"]`).
69	- **Email-verification purchase gate** (`lib/email-verification.ts:123` `emailVerificationError`) is
70	  consulted by `payAndDeploy`, `payAndDeployGame`, `placeHostingOrder`, `orderEmailHosting`,
71	  `purchaseDomain`, `resizeServer`, `purchaseDedicatedIp`, `renewNow`. It **ships OFF** —
72	  `getSettingBool("email_verification_enforced", false)` — and additionally stands down if
73	  `mailConfigured()` is false. UNVERIFIED whether prod has flipped it on.
74	- `assertNotImpersonating()` blocks every spend path while an admin impersonates.
75	
76	---
77	
78	## 2. STEP MAPS
79	
80	### 2.1 VPS — `DeployWizard.tsx`
81	
82	Steps (`DeployWizard.tsx:320`): `["Plan", (Location if nodes>1), "Install", "Add-ons", "Access", "Review"]`
83	→ **5 steps today** (single node) or 6.
84	
85	| # | Step | Fields | Type / default | Validation | Price-affecting |
86	|---|---|---|---|---|---|
87	| 1 | Plan | `planId` | card grid; default `defaultPlanId` (`default_plan_slug` setting) else `plans[0]` | must exist | **YES** |
88	| 1 | Plan | `termMonths` | `TermLadder`, default `defaultTermMonths` (`default_term`) else 1 | must be in `VPS_TERMS` | **YES** |
89	| 1 | Plan | custom-plan builder (cpu/ram/disk sliders) | opt-in disclosure; floor = current Max plan | server `quoteCustomPlanAction` capacity check debounced 450 ms; `confirmCustomPlanAction` mints an inactive Plan row | **YES** |
90	| 2 | Location | `nodeId` | card grid, default `nodes[0]` | node must be enabled | no (capacity/availability) |
91	| 3 | Install | `imageId` | 4 tabs (OS / Control Panels / Applications / Games) + search + `VersionPickerModal`; default = first `PLAIN_OS` | `planMeetsImage` (`plan.ramMB >= image.minRamMB && plan.diskGB >= image.minDiskGB`) | no (gates plan eligibility) |
92	| 4 | Add-ons | `addons.malware`, `addons.backup`, `addons.docker` | 3 free toggles, all default **false** | none | no ($0) |
93	| 4 | Add-ons → "Advanced options (optional)" `<details>` | `dedicatedIp` bool (default false); `extraDiskGB` slider 0–`EXTRA_DISK_MAX_ADD_GB` step `EXTRA_DISK_STEP_GB` (default 0, one-way); `backupTier` FREE\|PLUS (default FREE) | | `effectiveDiskGB <= EXTRA_DISK_MAX_TOTAL_GB` | **YES** (all three) |
94	| 5 | Access | `hostname` | text, **auto-prefilled** `<imageFamily>-<rand4>` (`defaultHostnameFor`), `hostnameTouchedRef` stops overwrite after first keystroke | `/^[a-z0-9]([a-z0-9-]*[a-z0-9])?$/i` and length 3–40 (client says 3–40, `hostnameValid` only enforces `>= 3`; server `orderSchema` enforces 3–40) | no |
95	| 5 | Access | root password | **not a field** — generated server-side, honest copy only (`DeployWizard.tsx:1383-1395`) | — | — |
96	| 5 | Access → "Advanced (optional)" `<details>` | `pubKey` textarea | default "" | server-side regex `^(ssh-(rsa\|ed25519)\|ecdsa-sha2-\S+)\s+\S+` before persisting | no |
97	| 5 | Access | `free` checkbox | **admin only** | — | yes (admin grant) |
98	| 6 | Review | `couponInput` → `couponApplied` | server-verified via `previewOrderCoupon` | server `couponOrderDiscountCents` | **YES** |
99	| 6 | Review | `useWallet` | default ON when `balanceCents > 0` | — | yes (split only) |
100	
101	- **State mechanism:** all React `useState`. Every selection is mirrored into hidden inputs on a
102	  single `<form action={payAndDeploy}>` (`DeployWizard.tsx:857-871`).
103	- **Draft:** `sessionStorage` key `nxeon.deploy.draft.v1` written on every change
104	  (`DeployWizard.tsx:468-479`). It is **only read back when the URL carries `?canceled=1`**, then
105	  deleted. A plain page refresh, tab close, or navigating away and back **loses everything** — the
106	  wizard remounts at step 0 with defaults. There is no DB draft/order record.
107	- **Auto-advance:** none on VPS. Every step needs an explicit Continue.
108	- **Back navigation:** `← Back` (or `PaymentStep`'s own Back) decrements `step`; state is preserved
109	  because the component never unmounts.
110	- **Two hard-won safety guards** documented in-file: distinct React `key`s on the Continue/Deploy
111	  buttons and an `onSubmit` guard that refuses submission unless `isLast` — a prior incident had
112	  "Continue" on the Access step placing five real orders (`DeployWizard.tsx:827-855`).
113	- **Reassurance copy** on every non-Review step: "You're a few clicks from live… We've picked
114	  sensible defaults — change anything you like, or just keep clicking Continue."
115	- **Sticky cart** (`WizardStickyCart`) follows every step with plan name + `/mo` incl. add-ons, and
116	  duplicates the Continue/Deploy handler. Suppressed once `PaymentStep` mounts.
117	- **Blockers** are surfaced in words on the step that can fix them (`primaryBlocker`,
118	  `installBlocker`, `accessBlocker`, `deployBlocker`) and wired via `aria-describedby`.
119	
120	### 2.2 Shared Hosting — `HostingDeployWizard.tsx`
121	
122	Steps (`:126`): `["Plan", "Domain", (Install if apps.length>0), "Add-ons", "Review"]` → **5 steps**.
123	
124	| # | Step | Fields | Default | Validation | Price-affecting |
125	|---|---|---|---|---|---|
126	| 1 | Plan | `planId` | `plans[0]` | active plan | **YES** |
127	| 1 | Plan | `termMonths` (TermLadder) | **`ANNUAL_TERM_MONTHS` (12)** — annual pre-selected | in `PRODUCT_TERMS` | **YES** |
128	| 2 | Domain | `domainMode` "temp"\|"own" | `"temp"` (badged "Recommended") | — | no |
129	| 2 | Domain | `subLabel` (temp mode, optional) | "" → server derives `<username>.<base>` | debounced 400 ms `checkHostingSubdomain`; blocks Continue if typed-but-unavailable | no |
130	| 2 | Domain | `domain` (own mode) | "" | `/^([a-z0-9]([a-z0-9-]*[a-z0-9])?\.)+[a-z]{2,}$/` | no |
131	| 3 | Install | `appSlug` | `""` ("None for now") | must be in `apps` | no |
132	| 4 | Add-ons | `extraDiskGB` −/+ stepper | 0 | 0…`EXTRA_DISK_MAX_ADD_GB` | **YES** |
133	| 5 | Review | `useWallet` | ON if balance > 0 | — | split only |
134	| 5 | Review | renewal-method gate (`addCard`) | — | `savedCard \|\| balance >= renewalCents \|\| cardCents > 0` | — |
135	
136	- **No promo-code field on hosting.** (VPS, and only VPS, has one.)
137	- **Draft:** `sessionStorage` key `nxeon.hosting.deploy.draft.v1`, written **only** by `saveDraft()`
138	  which is called **only from `addCard()`** (`:299,311`). Restored only when the URL carries
139	  `?card_setup=<sid>` (`:246-297`), which also finalises the saved card via `finalizeCardSetup` and
140	  jumps to Review. So: unlike VPS there is no continuous draft write — abandoning at any point other
141	  than the card-setup round-trip loses everything, and there is no `?canceled=1` restore path at all.
142	- **Idempotency:** one client token per mount (`idemRef`, `crypto.randomUUID()`), sent as
143	  `idempotencyKey`; server claims `FulfilledSession("hostorder:<key>")`.
144	- Two distinct Stripe primitives coexist: `StripeCheckoutModal` (mode `setup`, capture a renewal
145	  card, old `embedded_page` ui_mode) and `PaymentStep` (mode `payment`, Custom Checkout).
146	
147	### 2.3 Game Servers — `GameDeployWizard.tsx`
148	
149	Steps (`:286`): `["Game", "Plan", "Settings", "Review"]` → **4 steps**.
150	
151	| # | Step | Fields | Default | Validation | Price-affecting |
152	|---|---|---|---|---|---|
153	| 1 | Game | `game` (family) | `games[0].family` | family must have tiers | indirectly |
154	| 1 | Game | search / category pills / sort; grid capped at 12 with "Show all" | `gameSort="featured"` | — | no |
155	| 2 | Plan | `selected` (tier id) | **`null`** — nothing pre-selected | required | **YES** |
156	| 2 | Plan | `termMonths` | **12 (Annual)** | `PRODUCT_TERMS` | **YES** |
157	| 2 | Plan | custom-plan builder + "how many players?" slider (`recommendedSpecForPlayers`) | — | server capacity check | **YES** |
158	| 3 | Settings | `serverName` | "" (optional, max 60) | — | no |
159	| 3 | Settings | `hostname` | "" (optional, auto-generated server-side by `randSuffix`) | 3–40, `HOSTNAME_RE` when non-empty | no |
160	| 3 | Settings | `subdomain` (**Minecraft only, REQUIRED**) | "" | `validateSubdomainFormat` (3–20, not reserved) + uniqueness at insert | no |
161	| 3 | Settings → "Advanced options (optional)" | `dedicatedIp` | false | — | **YES** |
162	| 3 | Settings | `variant` (server type/loader) | `schema.defaultVariant` | `isValidVariant` | no |
163	| 3 | Settings | per-family `values` (`GAME_CONFIG_SCHEMAS`, 32 families) | schema defaults (`defaultValues`) | `validateConfig`; `required: true` fields (e.g. DST `TOKEN`) block checkout | no |
164	| 4 | Review | `useWallet` | ON if balance > 0 | — | split only |
165	
166	- Per-family field counts: Minecraft 9, Rust 5, Palworld 5, CS2 4, Valheim 2 (`lib/game-config.ts`).
167	  Every field carries `phase: "deploy" \| "live"`; `"deploy"` is labelled "applied at deploy" in the
168	  wizard and "restart" in the post-purchase `GameSettings.tsx` — it is a *restart* marker, **not** an
169	  immutability marker.
170	- **No promo-code field** on game.
171	- **Auto-advance:** clicking a game tile calls `pickGame()` which **jumps straight to step 2**
172	  (`:509-520`) and resets tier/variant/values. This is the only auto-advance in any wizard.
173	- **Draft:** `sessionStorage` `nxeon.gamedeploy.draft.v1`, written continuously (`:566-575`),
174	  restored only on `?canceled=1` (`:523-563`), same one-shot pattern as VPS.
175	
176	### 2.4 Business Email — `EmailHosting.tsx` (cross-comparison only)
177	
178	`ORDER_STEPS = ["Domain", "Plan", "Review"]` (`:169`). Fields: `domain` (defaults to first ACTIVE
179	owned domain; free text otherwise → `isExternal` DNS path), `planId` (`plans[0]`), `termMonths`
180	(default 12), `useWallet`. No promo code. **No sessionStorage draft at all.**
181	
182	### 2.5 Domains (cross-comparison only)
183	
184	`DomainRegisterWizard.tsx`: `BASE_STEPS = ["Domain","Term","Contact"]` + optional `"Email"` (when
185	`freeInboxPlan` is seeded) + `"Review"` → **4–5 steps**. The Contact step is a full ICANN registrant
186	form (firstName, lastName, address1, city, stateProvince, postalCode, country, phone, email) with
187	optional Geoapify address autocomplete. `DomainTransferInWizard.tsx` is its own multi-step flow.
188	No sessionStorage draft in either.
189	
190	---
191	
192	## 3. REQUIRED-BEFORE-PAYMENT vs POST-PAYMENT MATRIX
193	
194	Legend for **Class**: `PRICE` = changes the amount charged · `CAP` = capacity/oversell check ·
195	`AVAIL` = region/availability · `ELIG` = eligibility/promo · `CREATE` = the provisioner needs it at
196	VM/account creation · `LATER` = cosmetic or changeable after provisioning.
197	
198	### 3.1 VPS
199	
200	| Field | Class | Post-provision change API | Verdict |
201	|---|---|---|---|
202	| `planId` | PRICE, CAP | `resizeServer` (`lib/actions-server.ts:160`) UP only; `resizeServerDown` (`lib/actions-server-lifecycle.ts:194`) with guards; both prorate | **must stay pre-payment** (it is the price) |
203	| `termMonths` | PRICE | none (only `renewNow` / `toggleAutoRenew`) | **must stay pre-payment** |
204	| `nodeId` (Location) | AVAIL, CAP | **none** — no VM-migration action exists | must stay pre-payment (only shown when >1 node) |
205	| `dedicatedIp` | PRICE, AVAIL (`freeIps > 0`) | `purchaseDedicatedIp` (`lib/actions-dedicated-ip.ts:31`), prorated to term end | **could move post-payment** (API exists), but it is a paid add-on so it changes the quote |
206	| `extraDiskGB` | PRICE, CAP (`diskCapacityCheck`) | `expandServerDisk` (`lib/actions-disk.ts:37`) via `AddStorage.tsx`, prorated | **could move post-payment** (add-only either way) |
207	| `backupTier` (FREE/PLUS) | PRICE | `upgradeServerBackupTier` (`lib/actions-backup.ts:33`) via `BackupTierUpsell.tsx` | **could move post-payment** |
208	| `couponCode` | PRICE, ELIG | n/a | pre-payment by definition |
209	| `useWallet` | split only | n/a | pre-payment |
210	| `osTemplateId` (Install) | CREATE (worker clones this template) + gates plan minimums | `reinstallToOs` (`lib/actions-server-lifecycle.ts:119`) — **destructive re-clone**, blocked if any Volume is pinned | needed at create; a post-payment setup step would have to run **before** the PROVISION job |
211	| `hostname` | CREATE (`Server.name`/`hostname`, cloud-init, invoice text, DNS/SSH copy) | **NONE.** `renameServer` (`lib/actions-server-extra.ts:20`) only writes `Server.label`. Grep for any `hostname:` write outside order placement found nothing. | **cannot move post-payment without backend work** — must stay pre-payment or take the existing auto-generated default |
212	| `sshPublicKey` | CREATE (worker reads `db.sshKey` for the user at clone time, `worker/index.ts:588`) | `addSshKey` (`lib/actions-account.ts:93`) adds to the **account**, but nothing re-injects into a live VM | **cannot move post-payment without backend work** (customer can add manually over SSH) |
213	| `addons.docker` | CREATE (cloud-init `curl … get.docker.com`, `worker/index.ts:251`) | **NONE** | **cannot move post-payment**; wizard copy "You can add or remove these later in your VPS dashboard" is **not true** for docker |
214	| `addons.malwareScanner` | CREATE (cloud-init ClamAV, `worker/index.ts:252`) | **NONE** | same as above |
215	| `addons.dailyBackup` | bridged at sale to `autoBackup`+`backupIntervalHours` (`lib/order.ts:922-926`) | `setBackupSchedule` (`lib/actions-server-lifecycle.ts:45`) | **can move post-payment** |
216	| `free` (admin) | ELIG | n/a | admin-only |
217	
218	### 3.2 Shared Hosting
219	
220	| Field | Class | Post-provision change API | Verdict |
221	|---|---|---|---|
222	| `planId` | PRICE, CAP | `upgradeHostingPlan` (`lib/actions-hosting.ts:1309`) | pre-payment (it is the price) |
223	| `termMonths` | PRICE | none | pre-payment |
224	| `extraDiskGB` | PRICE (quota snapshot = `(plan.diskGB + extraDiskGB) × 1024`) | **NONE** — `AddStorage.tsx` calls `expandServerDisk`, which is VPS-only. No hosting analogue found. | **cannot move post-payment without backend work** |
225	| `domain` (own) / `subdomainLabel` | CREATE (`primaryDomain` = nginx `server_name`, cert SAN, unique hostname claim) | `createAddonDomain` + `setPrimaryHostingDomain` (`:1580`, `:1744`), `createSubdomain` (`:1533`) | **can move post-payment** — a temp subdomain is already the recommended default and a real domain can be attached later |
226	| `appSlug` (WordPress etc.) | LATER (queued as a `HostingTask` after ACTIVE) | `installWordPress` (`:1195`), `installApp` (`:1240`) | **already post-payment in effect**; the wizard step is pure pre-selection |
227	| `useWallet` | split only | n/a | pre-payment |
228	
229	### 3.3 Game Servers
230	
231	| Field | Class | Post-provision change API | Verdict |
232	|---|---|---|---|
233	| `gamePlanId` (tier) | PRICE, CAP | **NONE** — `lib/resize.ts:97` explicitly throws for any `server.gamePlanId` ("Game server plans are fixed bundles") | pre-payment; and **no self-service tier change exists at all** |
234	| `termMonths` | PRICE | none | pre-payment |
235	| `dedicatedIp` | PRICE, AVAIL | `purchaseDedicatedIp` works on any Server row | could move post-payment |
236	| `game` family | CREATE (selects `osTemplateId` + base plan) | none (would be a reinstall) | pre-payment |
237	| `hostname` | CREATE | **NONE** (same as VPS) | already optional + auto-generated — fine |
238	| `serverName` | LATER (`Server.label`) | `renameServer` | **can move post-payment** |
239	| `subdomain` (Minecraft, required) | CREATE (`Server.subdomain` unique + `SYNC_GAME_DNS`) | `changeGameSubdomain` (`lib/actions-server.ts:349`, rate-limited 5/5min) | **can move post-payment** — but is currently a **hard checkout blocker** |
240	| `variant` (loader/server type) | CREATE (worker renders game config) | `saveGameConfig` (`lib/actions-game-config.ts:84`, enqueues `GAME_CONFIG` job) | **can move post-payment** |
241	| all `GAME_CONFIG_SCHEMAS` `values` | CREATE-ish | `saveGameConfig` — same validation, same schema, same UI (`GameSettings.tsx`) | **can move post-payment**, including every `phase:"deploy"` field (that flag only means "needs a restart"). Exception: `required:true` fields (DST `TOKEN`) are enforced in **both** places, so leaving one blank would produce a non-starting server. |

243	### 3.4 Fields with no post-provision API (backend must not change → must stay pre-payment or get a safe default)

280	### 4.2 Pricing / promo / coupon / tax
281	
282	- **Wizard-displayed price === charged price by construction.** Every wizard derives its numbers from
283	  the same pure modules the server charges from: `lib/renewal-quote.ts`, `lib/billing-terms.ts`
284	  (`termPriceCents`), `lib/wallet-split.ts`. Extensive in-file comments cite two real incidents
285	  (2026-07-26 "H1" wrong renewal figure, "H2" post-payment re-quote) that produced this discipline.
286	- **Sold price is frozen** in Stripe metadata as `OrderPrice` (`lib/order.ts:162`) /
287	  `GameOrderPrice`, and `placeOrder`/`placeGameOrder` bill off `sold ?? quote`, never a re-quote.
288	- **Terms**: `VPS_TERMS` = 1 / 3? / 12 / 24 / 36 months — 1 (0 %), 12 (`annual_discount_percent`,
289	  live admin setting), 24 (30 %), 36 (40 %). `PRODUCT_TERMS` is the same array.
290	- **first-month-free** — `firstMonthFreeAppliesTo("HOSTING")` only. `app/dashboard/deploy/page.tsx`
291	  deliberately gates the *VPS display* the same way `lib/order.ts` gates the *charge*, so the VPS
292	  wizard never shows "$0 first month". Eligibility is per-`userId` **and** per-`ipHash`
293	  (`firstMonthFreeEligible`). On the card path it is **RESERVED** before the Checkout session is
294	  created (`reserveFirstMonthFree`, `payAndDeploy:627-657`), CONFIRMED at fulfilment, RELEASED on
295	  `checkout.session.expired`, and swept as a backstop. A lost reserve re-quotes at full price and
296	  recomputes the split.
297	- **Coupons** (`COMEBACK50` etc.) — VPS only. `previewOrderCoupon` verifies server-side; the applied
298	  discount is **cleared whenever `planId`/`termMonths`/`dedicatedIp`/`extraDiskGB` changes**
299	  (`DeployWizard.tsx:710-713`). Same reserve→confirm→release protocol as the promo
300	  (`reserveOrderCoupon`), with guards for `firstTimeOnly`, `maxRedemptions`, one-per-account,
301	  one-per-IP.
302	- **Riddle $100** (`lib/riddle.ts`) is a **wallet credit** (`balanceCents` increment), so it flows
303	  through "Apply my balance", not through the coupon field.
304	- **Referral** (`nxeon_ref`) is attributed at signup, and `maybeRewardReferral(user.id)` fires after
305	  a paid `placeOrder` — it is not a checkout-time discount.
306	- **Currency**: display-only. `useCurrency()` + `convertAndFormat`; every posted value and every
307	  charge stays **USD cents**. The wizards print "Prices shown in {CUR} for reference — you're billed
308	  in USD ($X)".
309	- **Tax/VAT**: `taxContextForUser(user)` from the billing country; 0 for anyone with no billing
310	  country on file. Shown as a "VAT / Tax (X% · CC)" line and folded into `dueCents`; the rate + cents
311	  are stamped onto `OrderPrice` so fulfilment settles the same total. **Game and Hosting orders carry
312	  no tax at all** (`GameOrderPrice` is `{chargeCents}` only; `placeGameOrder` writes
313	  `taxCents: 0, taxRatePercent: 0`).

315	### 4.3 Records, statuses, webhooks, idempotency
316	
317	| Record | Where | Status values |
318	|---|---|---|
319	| `Server` | `lib/order.ts:896` / `lib/game-order.ts:~400` | `PENDING, PROVISIONING, RUNNING, STOPPED, SUSPENDED, REINSTALLING, DELETING, ERROR` |
320	| `Job` | `tx.job.create({type:"PROVISION"})` in the same tx | `QUEUED, RUNNING, DONE, FAILED` |
321	| `HostingAccount` | `orderHostingAccountFor` | `PENDING, PROVISIONING, ACTIVE, SUSPENDED, FAILED, DELETING` |
322	| `Invoice` | in-tx, `status: "PAID"`, itemised lines that sum to the debit | — |
323	| `WalletTransaction` | in-tx, negative amount | — |
324	| `FulfilledSession` | the one-winner idempotency primitive, `UNIQUE(stripeSessionId)` | `CLAIMED, DONE, FAILED` |
325	| `DeployFunnelEvent` | `/api/track/deploy-step` + server-side | `type: step \| error \| complete` |
326	
327	- **Webhook**: `app/api/stripe/webhook/route.ts` handles exactly two events —
328	  `checkout.session.completed` (→ `fulfilCheckoutSession`) and `checkout.session.expired` (→ release
329	  promo/coupon holds). The success redirect `app/api/stripe/confirm/route.ts` calls the *same*
330	  function; whichever arrives first wins the `FulfilledSession` claim, the other is a no-op. The
331	  route explicitly documents that a browser redirect must never be the fulfilment trigger.
332	- **Dispatch** (`lib/fulfil-checkout.ts` `runFulfilment`): `unpaid` → no-op; `unreadable` → claim +
333	  settle FAILED + notify; then `order` / `gameOrder` / `hostOrder` / `emailOrder` / `domainOrder` /
334	  `resize` / `diskExpand` / … branches. Card money is first credited to the wallet
335	  (`creditCheckoutSession`, `UNIQUE stripeSessionId`) and then debited back out by the placement
336	  function — so the wallet is never touched before the card clears.
337	- **Hosting idempotency** additionally uses a client `idempotencyKey` →
338	  `FulfilledSession("hostorder:<key>")`, shared by the wallet path and the card path.

340	### 4.4 What the user sees while waiting for the webhook
341	
342	- Card confirm navigates the **top window** to `/api/stripe/confirm`, which runs fulfilment
343	  synchronously and 302s to the product page with `?purchase=1` (+ `pv`, `pc`, `pe`, `prod` for the
344	  pixel). So there is no "waiting for webhook" screen in the happy path — the redirect *is* the
345	  fulfilment.
346	- If `fulfilCheckoutSession` **throws**, the user lands on `/dashboard/billing?pending=1`.
347	  **`pending` is not read by `app/dashboard/billing/page.tsx`** (it destructures only
348	  `paid`, `canceled`, `card_setup`), so this is a **silent dead end** — the customer sees the billing
349	  page with no explanation.
350	- PayPal/Coinbase return to `/dashboard/deploy?paid=1` (`lib/actions-payment-providers.ts:393`) —
351	  and **`paid=1` is read by nothing on the deploy page** either. Same silent landing.
