# Audit 07 — Purchase + Deployment Funnels (READ-ONLY, Phase 1)

Codebase: `/opt/nxeon` @ 2026-09-03. All paths repo-relative. Facts only; no design proposals.
Anything I could not verify from source is marked **UNVERIFIED** (I did not touch the DB, Stripe,
name.com or any service).

---

## 0. Architecture in one paragraph

All four "deploy" products live behind ONE route, `app/dashboard/deploy/page.tsx`, which is a server
component that fetches everything for all four wizards and hands them to
`components/customer/DeployHub.tsx`. The hub is a tab strip (`?product=vps|hosting|game|email`,
`router.replace`, no navigation) that mounts exactly one wizard at a time:

| product | wizard component | server action entry |
|---|---|---|
| VPS | `components/customer/DeployWizard.tsx` (1913 L) | `payAndDeploy` (`lib/actions.ts:513`) |
| Shared Hosting | `components/customer/HostingDeployWizard.tsx` (1044 L) | `placeHostingOrder` (`lib/actions-hosting.ts:453`) |
| Game Servers | `components/customer/GameDeployWizard.tsx` (1659 L) | `payAndDeployGame` (`lib/actions-gameplans.ts:201`) |
| Business Email | `components/customer/EmailHosting.tsx` (1440 L) | `orderEmailHosting` (`lib/actions-email-hosting.ts:256`) |

Domains have their own routes (`/dashboard/domains/register`, `/dashboard/domains/transfer`) and are
NOT in the hub. `app/dashboard/order/page.tsx` is a bare `redirect("/dashboard/deploy")`.

Payment is uniform: an embedded `components/customer/PaymentStep.tsx` mounting a **Stripe Custom
Checkout session** (`ui_mode: "elements"`), plus PayPal and Coinbase rails that are only wired for
VPS. Everything settles through the single idempotent bus `lib/fulfil-checkout.ts`.

---

## 1. ENTRY POINTS

### 1.1 Every route/CTA that starts a purchase flow

| Entry | File | Target | Carries product? | Carries plan? |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Portal nav "Deploy" | `app/dashboard/layout.tsx:40` | `/dashboard/deploy` | no (defaults to `vps`) | no |
| Dashboard home CTA ×2 | `app/dashboard/page.tsx` | `/dashboard/deploy` | no | no |
| Servers list + empty state | `app/dashboard/servers/page.tsx` | `/dashboard/deploy` | no | no |
| Games list + empty state | `app/dashboard/games/page.tsx` | `/dashboard/deploy?product=game` | yes | no |
| Hosting list + empty state | `app/dashboard/hosting/page.tsx`, `components/customer/HostingClient.tsx` | `/dashboard/deploy?product=hosting` | yes | no |
| Billing page ×2 | `app/dashboard/billing/page.tsx` | `/dashboard/deploy` | no | no |
| SSL page cross-sell | `components/customer/SslCertificates.tsx` | `/dashboard/deploy` | no | no |
| Claude Code hub ×2 | `components/customer/claude-code/ClaudeCodeHub.tsx` | `/dashboard/deploy` | no | no |
| Onboarding checklist | `lib/actions-onboarding.ts:57` | `/dashboard/deploy` | no | no |
| Marketing game configurator | `components/marketing/showcase/GameConfigurator.tsx:33` | `/dashboard/deploy?product=game` | yes | no |
| KB / chat-agent deep links | `lib/kb-plans.ts:45-48` | `?product=hosting|vps|game|email` | yes | no |
| Kodely partner SSO | `app/api/partner/checkout/route.ts:36,42` | `/dashboard/deploy?product=vps&ref=kodely` / `product=hosting&ref=kodely` | yes | no |
| Email templates | `lib/email-templates.ts:48` | `/dashboard/deploy` | no | no |
| Deploy win-back email | `worker/deploy-winback.ts` | deploy URL + `COMEBACK50` code | no | no |
| Marketing pricing cards | `components/marketing/PricingGrid.tsx`, `components/marketing/ProductPricing.tsx` | **`/register`** (bare) | **no** | **no** |
| Domains | `/dashboard/domains/register?...`, `/dashboard/domains/transfer` | n/a | n/a | domain carried via `initialDomain` |

### 1.2 Guest checkout / signup mid-flow

- **No guest checkout anywhere.** Every wizard route is under `/dashboard/**` and every action calls
  `requireUser()` first. `app/dashboard/deploy/page.tsx:37` starts with `await requireUser()`.
- **Marketing → purchase loses everything.** 38 marketing CTAs resolve to a bare `href="/register"`
  (`components/marketing/PricingGrid.tsx`, `components/marketing/ProductPricing.tsx`, etc.). The
  register page supports `?next=` (`app/register/page.tsx:27`, validated by `safeNext`), and
  `register()` honours it (`lib/actions.ts` ~line 320), but **no marketing CTA sets `next`** — only
  `components/AuthForms.tsx:260` (login→register handoff) does. So a visitor who clicks "Buy Starter"
  on `/pricing` signs up and lands on `/dashboard?signup=1`, not on the deploy wizard with Starter
  selected. Plan/product/term choice is discarded at the signup boundary.
- `?ref=` is captured into cookies at both ends: `ReferralCapture` (register page, `nxeon_ref`, 30d)
  and `PartnerSourceCapture` (every dashboard page, `nx_partner_ref`, 24h,
  `KNOWN_PARTNERS = ["kodely"]`).
- **Email-verification purchase gate** (`lib/email-verification.ts:123` `emailVerificationError`) is
  consulted by `payAndDeploy`, `payAndDeployGame`, `placeHostingOrder`, `orderEmailHosting`,
  `purchaseDomain`, `resizeServer`, `purchaseDedicatedIp`, `renewNow`. It **ships OFF** —
  `getSettingBool("email_verification_enforced", false)` — and additionally stands down if
  `mailConfigured()` is false. UNVERIFIED whether prod has flipped it on.
- `assertNotImpersonating()` blocks every spend path while an admin impersonates.

---

## 2. STEP MAPS

### 2.1 VPS — `DeployWizard.tsx`

Steps (`DeployWizard.tsx:320`): `["Plan", (Location if nodes>1), "Install", "Add-ons", "Access", "Review"]`
→ **5 steps today** (single node) or 6.

| # | Step | Fields | Type / default | Validation | Price-affecting |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Plan | `planId` | card grid; default `defaultPlanId` (`default_plan_slug` setting) else `plans[0]` | must exist | **YES** |
| 1 | Plan | `termMonths` | `TermLadder`, default `defaultTermMonths` (`default_term`) else 1 | must be in `VPS_TERMS` | **YES** |
| 1 | Plan | custom-plan builder (cpu/ram/disk sliders) | opt-in disclosure; floor = current Max plan | server `quoteCustomPlanAction` capacity check debounced 450 ms; `confirmCustomPlanAction` mints an inactive Plan row | **YES** |
| 2 | Location | `nodeId` | card grid, default `nodes[0]` | node must be enabled | no (capacity/availability) |
| 3 | Install | `imageId` | 4 tabs (OS / Control Panels / Applications / Games) + search + `VersionPickerModal`; default = first `PLAIN_OS` | `planMeetsImage` (`plan.ramMB >= image.minRamMB && plan.diskGB >= image.minDiskGB`) | no (gates plan eligibility) |
| 4 | Add-ons | `addons.malware`, `addons.backup`, `addons.docker` | 3 free toggles, all default **false** | none | no ($0) |
| 4 | Add-ons → "Advanced options (optional)" `<details>` | `dedicatedIp` bool (default false); `extraDiskGB` slider 0–`EXTRA_DISK_MAX_ADD_GB` step `EXTRA_DISK_STEP_GB` (default 0, one-way); `backupTier` FREE\|PLUS (default FREE) | | `effectiveDiskGB <= EXTRA_DISK_MAX_TOTAL_GB` | **YES** (all three) |
| 5 | Access | `hostname` | text, **auto-prefilled** `<imageFamily>-<rand4>` (`defaultHostnameFor`), `hostnameTouchedRef` stops overwrite after first keystroke | `/^[a-z0-9]([a-z0-9-]*[a-z0-9])?$/i` and length 3–40 (client says 3–40, `hostnameValid` only enforces `>= 3`; server `orderSchema` enforces 3–40) | no |
| 5 | Access | root password | **not a field** — generated server-side, honest copy only (`DeployWizard.tsx:1383-1395`) | — | — |
| 5 | Access → "Advanced (optional)" `<details>` | `pubKey` textarea | default "" | server-side regex `^(ssh-(rsa\|ed25519)\|ecdsa-sha2-\S+)\s+\S+` before persisting | no |
| 5 | Access | `free` checkbox | **admin only** | — | yes (admin grant) |
| 6 | Review | `couponInput` → `couponApplied` | server-verified via `previewOrderCoupon` | server `couponOrderDiscountCents` | **YES** |
| 6 | Review | `useWallet` | default ON when `balanceCents > 0` | — | yes (split only) |

- **State mechanism:** all React `useState`. Every selection is mirrored into hidden inputs on a
  single `<form action={payAndDeploy}>` (`DeployWizard.tsx:857-871`).
- **Draft:** `sessionStorage` key `nxeon.deploy.draft.v1` written on every change
  (`DeployWizard.tsx:468-479`). It is **only read back when the URL carries `?canceled=1`**, then
  deleted. A plain page refresh, tab close, or navigating away and back **loses everything** — the
  wizard remounts at step 0 with defaults. There is no DB draft/order record.
- **Auto-advance:** none on VPS. Every step needs an explicit Continue.
- **Back navigation:** `← Back` (or `PaymentStep`'s own Back) decrements `step`; state is preserved
  because the component never unmounts.
- **Two hard-won safety guards** documented in-file: distinct React `key`s on the Continue/Deploy
  buttons and an `onSubmit` guard that refuses submission unless `isLast` — a prior incident had
  "Continue" on the Access step placing five real orders (`DeployWizard.tsx:827-855`).
- **Reassurance copy** on every non-Review step: "You're a few clicks from live… We've picked
  sensible defaults — change anything you like, or just keep clicking Continue."
- **Sticky cart** (`WizardStickyCart`) follows every step with plan name + `/mo` incl. add-ons, and
  duplicates the Continue/Deploy handler. Suppressed once `PaymentStep` mounts.
- **Blockers** are surfaced in words on the step that can fix them (`primaryBlocker`,
  `installBlocker`, `accessBlocker`, `deployBlocker`) and wired via `aria-describedby`.

### 2.2 Shared Hosting — `HostingDeployWizard.tsx`

Steps (`:126`): `["Plan", "Domain", (Install if apps.length>0), "Add-ons", "Review"]` → **5 steps**.

| # | Step | Fields | Default | Validation | Price-affecting |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Plan | `planId` | `plans[0]` | active plan | **YES** |
| 1 | Plan | `termMonths` (TermLadder) | **`ANNUAL_TERM_MONTHS` (12)** — annual pre-selected | in `PRODUCT_TERMS` | **YES** |
| 2 | Domain | `domainMode` "temp"\|"own" | `"temp"` (badged "Recommended") | — | no |
| 2 | Domain | `subLabel` (temp mode, optional) | "" → server derives `<username>.<base>` | debounced 400 ms `checkHostingSubdomain`; blocks Continue if typed-but-unavailable | no |
| 2 | Domain | `domain` (own mode) | "" | `/^([a-z0-9]([a-z0-9-]*[a-z0-9])?\.)+[a-z]{2,}$/` | no |
| 3 | Install | `appSlug` | `""` ("None for now") | must be in `apps` | no |
| 4 | Add-ons | `extraDiskGB` −/+ stepper | 0 | 0…`EXTRA_DISK_MAX_ADD_GB` | **YES** |
| 5 | Review | `useWallet` | ON if balance > 0 | — | split only |
| 5 | Review | renewal-method gate (`addCard`) | — | `savedCard \|\| balance >= renewalCents \|\| cardCents > 0` | — |

- **No promo-code field on hosting.** (VPS, and only VPS, has one.)
- **Draft:** `sessionStorage` key `nxeon.hosting.deploy.draft.v1`, written **only** by `saveDraft()`
  which is called **only from `addCard()`** (`:299,311`). Restored only when the URL carries
  `?card_setup=<sid>` (`:246-297`), which also finalises the saved card via `finalizeCardSetup` and
  jumps to Review. So: unlike VPS there is no continuous draft write — abandoning at any point other
  than the card-setup round-trip loses everything, and there is no `?canceled=1` restore path at all.
- **Idempotency:** one client token per mount (`idemRef`, `crypto.randomUUID()`), sent as
  `idempotencyKey`; server claims `FulfilledSession("hostorder:<key>")`.
- Two distinct Stripe primitives coexist: `StripeCheckoutModal` (mode `setup`, capture a renewal
  card, old `embedded_page` ui_mode) and `PaymentStep` (mode `payment`, Custom Checkout).

### 2.3 Game Servers — `GameDeployWizard.tsx`

Steps (`:286`): `["Game", "Plan", "Settings", "Review"]` → **4 steps**.

| # | Step | Fields | Default | Validation | Price-affecting |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Game | `game` (family) | `games[0].family` | family must have tiers | indirectly |
| 1 | Game | search / category pills / sort; grid capped at 12 with "Show all" | `gameSort="featured"` | — | no |
| 2 | Plan | `selected` (tier id) | **`null`** — nothing pre-selected | required | **YES** |
| 2 | Plan | `termMonths` | **12 (Annual)** | `PRODUCT_TERMS` | **YES** |
| 2 | Plan | custom-plan builder + "how many players?" slider (`recommendedSpecForPlayers`) | — | server capacity check | **YES** |
| 3 | Settings | `serverName` | "" (optional, max 60) | — | no |
| 3 | Settings | `hostname` | "" (optional, auto-generated server-side by `randSuffix`) | 3–40, `HOSTNAME_RE` when non-empty | no |
| 3 | Settings | `subdomain` (**Minecraft only, REQUIRED**) | "" | `validateSubdomainFormat` (3–20, not reserved) + uniqueness at insert | no |
| 3 | Settings → "Advanced options (optional)" | `dedicatedIp` | false | — | **YES** |
| 3 | Settings | `variant` (server type/loader) | `schema.defaultVariant` | `isValidVariant` | no |
| 3 | Settings | per-family `values` (`GAME_CONFIG_SCHEMAS`, 32 families) | schema defaults (`defaultValues`) | `validateConfig`; `required: true` fields (e.g. DST `TOKEN`) block checkout | no |
| 4 | Review | `useWallet` | ON if balance > 0 | — | split only |

- Per-family field counts: Minecraft 9, Rust 5, Palworld 5, CS2 4, Valheim 2 (`lib/game-config.ts`).
  Every field carries `phase: "deploy" \| "live"`; `"deploy"` is labelled "applied at deploy" in the
  wizard and "restart" in the post-purchase `GameSettings.tsx` — it is a *restart* marker, **not** an
  immutability marker.
- **No promo-code field** on game.
- **Auto-advance:** clicking a game tile calls `pickGame()` which **jumps straight to step 2**
  (`:509-520`) and resets tier/variant/values. This is the only auto-advance in any wizard.
- **Draft:** `sessionStorage` `nxeon.gamedeploy.draft.v1`, written continuously (`:566-575`),
  restored only on `?canceled=1` (`:523-563`), same one-shot pattern as VPS.

### 2.4 Business Email — `EmailHosting.tsx` (cross-comparison only)

`AVAIL` = region/availability · `ELIG` = eligibility/promo · `CREATE` = the provisioner needs it at
VM/account creation · `LATER` = cosmetic or changeable after provisioning.

## 4. CHECKOUT + PAYMENT

### 4.1 Mechanism

| | VPS | Hosting | Game | Email | Domains |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Card | Stripe **Custom Checkout** (`ui_mode:"elements"`), embedded `PaymentElement` in `PaymentStep.tsx`, **no redirect** | same | same | same | same |
| Express | `ExpressCheckoutElement` (Google Pay / Apple Pay, `link:"never"`, `paypal:"never"`) — single instance, hidden via CSS until `onReady` reports availability | same | same | same | same |
| PayPal | **YES** — `@paypal/react-paypal-js`, `createOrderPayPalOrder` / `captureExternalPayPalOrder` (`lib/actions-payment-providers.ts`) | **stubbed off** (`hostingPaymentUnavailable`) | **stubbed off** | **stubbed off** | UNVERIFIED |
| Coinbase Commerce | **YES** — `createOrderCoinbaseCharge`, redirects to Coinbase hosted page | off | off | off | — |
| Wallet | `walletSplit` (`lib/wallet-split.ts`), "Apply my balance" default ON | same | same | same | same |
| Saved card | checkbox is rendered **checked and `disabled`** (`PaymentStep.tsx` ~line 396) — copy: "Nxeon plans renew automatically… this isn't optional for a subscription product" | same | same | same | `DomainRegisterWizard` overrides `saveCardExplainer` because domain renewals never draw a card |

- **Billing details** are never collected in the wizard. `PaymentElement` is configured
  `fields: { billingDetails: { name: "never" } }`; a plain "Cardholder name" input is rendered
  beside it and — as written — **is never passed to `checkout.confirm()`** (`payWithCard()` only
  sends `{ savePaymentMethod: saveCard }`). The account email is shown read-only.
- **Billing address / country** comes from `BillingProfile` elsewhere; `taxContextForUser` reads it.
- **3DS**: handled entirely by `checkoutActions.confirm()`; on success Stripe navigates the top
  window to the session `return_url` = `/api/stripe/confirm?session_id=…`. No custom 3DS code.
- **Card minimum**: `STRIPE_MIN_CENTS = 50`. `walletSplit` guarantees `cardCents` is 0 or ≥ 50, and
  the wizards surface "Card payments have a $0.50 minimum…" when clamped.

### 4.2 Pricing / promo / coupon / tax

- **Wizard-displayed price === charged price by construction.** Every wizard derives its numbers from
  the same pure modules the server charges from: `lib/renewal-quote.ts`, `lib/billing-terms.ts`
  (`termPriceCents`), `lib/wallet-split.ts`. Extensive in-file comments cite two real incidents
  (2026-07-26 "H1" wrong renewal figure, "H2" post-payment re-quote) that produced this discipline.
- **Sold price is frozen** in Stripe metadata as `OrderPrice` (`lib/order.ts:162`) /
  `GameOrderPrice`, and `placeOrder`/`placeGameOrder` bill off `sold ?? quote`, never a re-quote.
- **Terms**: `VPS_TERMS` = 1 / 3? / 12 / 24 / 36 months — 1 (0 %), 12 (`annual_discount_percent`,
  live admin setting), 24 (30 %), 36 (40 %). `PRODUCT_TERMS` is the same array.
- **first-month-free** — `firstMonthFreeAppliesTo("HOSTING")` only. `app/dashboard/deploy/page.tsx`
  deliberately gates the *VPS display* the same way `lib/order.ts` gates the *charge*, so the VPS
  wizard never shows "$0 first month". Eligibility is per-`userId` **and** per-`ipHash`
  (`firstMonthFreeEligible`). On the card path it is **RESERVED** before the Checkout session is
  created (`reserveFirstMonthFree`, `payAndDeploy:627-657`), CONFIRMED at fulfilment, RELEASED on
  `checkout.session.expired`, and swept as a backstop. A lost reserve re-quotes at full price and
  recomputes the split.
- **Coupons** (`COMEBACK50` etc.) — VPS only. `previewOrderCoupon` verifies server-side; the applied
  discount is **cleared whenever `planId`/`termMonths`/`dedicatedIp`/`extraDiskGB` changes**
  (`DeployWizard.tsx:710-713`). Same reserve→confirm→release protocol as the promo
  (`reserveOrderCoupon`), with guards for `firstTimeOnly`, `maxRedemptions`, one-per-account,
  one-per-IP.
- **Riddle $100** (`lib/riddle.ts`) is a **wallet credit** (`balanceCents` increment), so it flows
  through "Apply my balance", not through the coupon field.
- **Referral** (`nxeon_ref`) is attributed at signup, and `maybeRewardReferral(user.id)` fires after
  a paid `placeOrder` — it is not a checkout-time discount.
- **Currency**: display-only. `useCurrency()` + `convertAndFormat`; every posted value and every
  charge stays **USD cents**. The wizards print "Prices shown in {CUR} for reference — you're billed
  in USD ($X)".
- **Tax/VAT**: `taxContextForUser(user)` from the billing country; 0 for anyone with no billing
  country on file. Shown as a "VAT / Tax (X% · CC)" line and folded into `dueCents`; the rate + cents
  are stamped onto `OrderPrice` so fulfilment settles the same total. **Game and Hosting orders carry
  no tax at all** (`GameOrderPrice` is `{chargeCents}` only; `placeGameOrder` writes
  `taxCents: 0, taxRatePercent: 0`).

### 4.3 Records, statuses, webhooks, idempotency

| Record | Where | Status values |
|---|---|---|
| `Server` | `lib/order.ts:896` / `lib/game-order.ts:~400` | `PENDING, PROVISIONING, RUNNING, STOPPED, SUSPENDED, REINSTALLING, DELETING, ERROR` |
| `Job` | `tx.job.create({type:"PROVISION"})` in the same tx | `QUEUED, RUNNING, DONE, FAILED` |
| `HostingAccount` | `orderHostingAccountFor` | `PENDING, PROVISIONING, ACTIVE, SUSPENDED, FAILED, DELETING` |
| `Invoice` | in-tx, `status: "PAID"`, itemised lines that sum to the debit | — |
| `WalletTransaction` | in-tx, negative amount | — |
| `FulfilledSession` | the one-winner idempotency primitive, `UNIQUE(stripeSessionId)` | `CLAIMED, DONE, FAILED` |
| `DeployFunnelEvent` | `/api/track/deploy-step` + server-side | `type: step \| error \| complete` |

- **Webhook**: `app/api/stripe/webhook/route.ts` handles exactly two events —
  `checkout.session.completed` (→ `fulfilCheckoutSession`) and `checkout.session.expired` (→ release
  promo/coupon holds). The success redirect `app/api/stripe/confirm/route.ts` calls the *same*
  function; whichever arrives first wins the `FulfilledSession` claim, the other is a no-op. The
  route explicitly documents that a browser redirect must never be the fulfilment trigger.
- **Dispatch** (`lib/fulfil-checkout.ts` `runFulfilment`): `unpaid` → no-op; `unreadable` → claim +
  settle FAILED + notify; then `order` / `gameOrder` / `hostOrder` / `emailOrder` / `domainOrder` /
  `resize` / `diskExpand` / … branches. Card money is first credited to the wallet
  (`creditCheckoutSession`, `UNIQUE stripeSessionId`) and then debited back out by the placement
  function — so the wallet is never touched before the card clears.
- **Hosting idempotency** additionally uses a client `idempotencyKey` →
  `FulfilledSession("hostorder:<key>")`, shared by the wallet path and the card path.

### 4.4 What the user sees while waiting for the webhook

- Card confirm navigates the **top window** to `/api/stripe/confirm`, which runs fulfilment
  synchronously and 302s to the product page with `?purchase=1` (+ `pv`, `pc`, `pe`, `prod` for the
  pixel). So there is no "waiting for webhook" screen in the happy path — the redirect *is* the
  fulfilment.
- If `fulfilCheckoutSession` **throws**, the user lands on `/dashboard/billing?pending=1`.
  **`pending` is not read by `app/dashboard/billing/page.tsx`** (it destructures only
  `paid`, `canceled`, `card_setup`), so this is a **silent dead end** — the customer sees the billing
  page with no explanation.
- PayPal/Coinbase return to `/dashboard/deploy?paid=1` (`lib/actions-payment-providers.ts:393`) —
  and **`paid=1` is read by nothing on the deploy page** either. Same silent landing.

### 4.5 Payment-failure paths

| Failure | Where the user lands | Config survives? |
|---|---|---|
| Card declined in `PaymentElement` | stays on the Review/Payment step, inline red message | **yes** (never left the page) |
| Stripe session creation fails | `stripePhase="error"` → amber "Card payments aren't available right now (…) try again" | yes |
| Stripe Checkout **cancelled** (legacy redirect path) | `/dashboard/deploy?canceled=1` → VPS/Game restore draft + banner "Checkout cancelled — you weren't charged." | **yes**, for VPS & Game only |
| Hosting card-setup cancelled | `?card_setup=canceled` → restores draft, lands on Review, note shown | yes |
| Card cleared but `placeOrder` threw | `settle(FAILED)` + `notifyStalled(userId)` + `recordDeployFunnelError("PAID_ORDER_FAILED")`; redirect `/dashboard/deploy?paid=1` (VPS/hosting), `/dashboard/games?paid=1` (game) | **no** — the wizard is remounted fresh and `?paid=1` renders nothing |
| Fulfilment throw | `/dashboard/billing?pending=1` | no |
| PayPal/Coinbase paid | `/dashboard/deploy?paid=1` | no |
| Insufficient wallet | inline `OrderError("Insufficient balance.")` on Review | yes |
| Spend cap hit | `assertSpendCap` → `OrderError` inline | yes |
| Server-count cap | `serverLimitError` / `gameOrderGate` (`max_servers_per_user`, default 10) | yes |

### 4.6 Deploy-abandonment win-back (`worker/deploy-winback.ts`)

- **Master kill-switch first line**: `DEPLOY_WINBACK_ENABLED === "true"` **or**
  `getSettingBool("deploy_winback_enabled", false)`. **Defaults OFF.** UNVERIFIED whether prod has it on.
- Trigger: users with any `DeployFunnelEvent{type:"step"}` whose **most recent** step is
  older than `deploy_winback_delay_minutes` (default **30 min**) and newer than
  `deploy_winback_max_age_days` (default **30 days**).
- Excludes: users who completed, already own a server, unverified/opted-out, or already received the
  `deploy_winback` template (deduped on `EmailLog.template`).
- Offer: `COMEBACK50`, `WINBACK_PERCENT_OFF = 50`, expiry label = last day of next month. The coupon
  itself is **not minted by this code** — the owner must create a matching coupon.
- Caps: `MAX_SENDS_PER_SWEEP = 25`, `SEND_GAP_MS = 1200`. Uses `product_news` NotifyKind so the
  marketing opt-out and unsubscribe footer apply.

### 4.7 Analytics per step

| Signal | Fired where |
|---|---|
| `trackDeployStep(product, stepLabel, i)` | on every step change. **VPS delays it 3 s** (`DeployWizard.tsx:335-342`) to avoid counting instant bounces; hosting/game/email fire immediately. De-duped per tab-session in `sessionStorage`. |
| `trackDeployStep(product, "Payment", steps.length)` | on final submit (`onSubmit` of the form / `place()` / `submit()`) |
| `trackDeployError(product, step, i, code, msg)` | on any action error; **not** de-duped |
| completion | **server-side only** — `recordDeployFunnelComplete` inside `placeOrder` (`stepIndex 8`), `placeGameOrder` (5), `placeHostingOrderCore` (7). Client `trackDeployComplete` exists but is no longer called by the wizards. |
| `PAID_ORDER_FAILED` | `recordDeployFunnelError` from `lib/fulfil-checkout.ts` |
| Meta CAPI `Purchase` | `reportPurchase` in `lib/fulfil-checkout.ts` (card path), with `_fbc`/`_fbp`/UA/IP when a request scope exists |
| Meta CAPI `Subscribe` | `placeHostingOrderCore` server-side, event_id = the idempotency key, value = renewal (not $0) |

| browser `nxTrack('hosting'\|'email'\|'card')` | consent-gated globals from `ConversionTags` |
| `?purchase=1&pv&pc&pe&prod` | stamped on the success redirect; read by `PurchaseTracker` (layout) and by `ProvisioningOverlay` via the server-side `searchParams` |

### 5.1 Real state machine

**VPS / Game** (`worker/index.ts` `provision()`):
`PENDING` (row created with the PROVISION job) → `PROVISIONING` (`:438`, clears `provisionError`,
nulls `provisioningStep`) → step labels written to `Server.provisioningStep` (`:446`):
1. `"Allocating your server…"` (`:546`)
2. `"Configuring the network…"` (`:576`)
3. `"Starting your server…"` (`:640`)
4. `"Booting the operating system…"` (`:652`, skipped in SANDBOX)
5. `"Waiting for network access…"` (`:677`)
6. `"Starting the game server…"` (`:695`, game orders only)
→ `RUNNING` (`:746`, `provisioningStep: null`). On failure → `ERROR` + `provisionError` +
in-app `notify()` + `emails.provisionFailed`.

**Hosting** (`worker/hosting.ts`): `PENDING` → `PROVISIONING` → steps:
`"Creating your account…"` (:328), `"Setting your storage quota…"` (:344), `"Configuring PHP…"`
(:348), `"Issuing a security certificate…"` (:358), `"Configuring your web server…"` (:381),
`"Preparing your site…"` (:386), `"Enabling secure file transfer…"` (:390) → `ACTIVE` (:505, sets
`provisionedAt`, `sftpPasswordEnc`). After ACTIVE, `hostingProvisioningStep` keeps reporting a live
`HostingTask` (e.g. `"Installing WordPress…"`) so the overlay survives the app install.

`lib/provisioning-step.ts` reads these columns back; a null step falls back to cosmetic cycling text
in `ProvisioningOverlay` (`PROVISION_STEPS`, 3.5 s ticks) — explicitly labelled "purely cosmetic" in
the source. Copy shown: *"This usually takes under two minutes. Feel free to leave this tab."*

### 5.2 Is there a "setup" step today?

**No.** No product has any post-payment configuration step. The overlay is read-only progress + a
success card, then the customer is dropped onto the full product management page.

### 5.3 First-value moment

- **VPS/Game** — `ProvisioningOverlay` `SuccessView` shows hostname, connect address (`ssh root@IP`
  or `IP:port`), plan, OS, and the **root password** (via `RevealPassword`/`CopyText` from
  `ServerAccess.tsx`), plus "Go to your server".
- **Hosting** — the same overlay with `rootPasswordLabel="SFTP password"` and `extraInfo` rows (SFTP
  username, Website URL); `readyStatus="ACTIVE"`.
- **Email** — no overlay; the customer must go to `/dashboard/email` and run
  `getEmailDnsRecords` / `verifyEmailDomain` for an external domain (or `autoCreateEmailDns` via
  Cloudflare) before mail flows.
- **Domain** — `/dashboard/domains/<id>?new=1`.

317	**info/accent surface** colour, the **highlight text** colour and the **page background** wash —

# Audit 02 — Design System / CSS / Component Duplication / Icons / Typography / Motion

**Scope:** `app/dashboard/**`, `components/customer/**`, `components/portal/**` (+ `components/ui/*`).
**Method:** read-only. Whole-file reads limited to `app/globals.css`, `components/ui/primitives.tsx`,
`components/customer/cpanel/shared.tsx`, `components/customer/hosting/shared.tsx`. Everything else is
`grep -rno … | sort | uniq -c` census. Counts are **occurrence counts of the literal token in `.tsx` source**,
not runtime render counts. Regex census can slightly over/under-count where a class string spans lines —
those places are marked.

**Portal size:** 245 `.tsx` files, ~59,300 LOC. 169 of 245 are `"use client"`.
64 route files under `app/dashboard/**`, 181 components under `components/customer/**`, 3 under `components/portal/**`.

---

## 1. TOKENS — the design system as actually defined

### 1.1 Build config

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Tailwind | v4.1.11, **CSS-first** (`@import "tailwindcss"` + `@theme` in `app/globals.css`) |
| `tailwind.config.{js,ts,mjs}` | **Does not exist** — verified, no config file outside `node_modules` |
| PostCSS | `postcss.config.mjs` → single plugin `@tailwindcss/postcss` |
| Global stylesheet | `app/globals.css` — **596 lines, the only global CSS in the portal** |
| CSS Modules in portal | **0** (5 `.module.css` files exist but all under `components/marketing/*template/`) |
| CSS-in-JS libs | none |
| Design-token source of truth | `app/globals.css` `@theme` block only |

### 1.2 Fonts

Loaded in `app/layout.tsx` via `next/font/google`, self-hosted:

```
const geistSans = Geist({ subsets:["latin"], variable:"--font-geist-sans", display:"swap" });
const geistMono = Geist_Mono({ subsets:["latin"], variable:"--font-geist-mono", display:"swap" });
```

Mapped in `@theme`:

| Token | Value |
|---|---|
| `--font-sans` | `var(--font-geist-sans), ui-sans-serif, system-ui, -apple-system, "Segoe UI", Roboto, sans-serif` |
| `--font-mono` | `var(--font-geist-mono), ui-monospace, "SFMono-Regular", "Menlo", monospace` |

`body { @apply … font-sans }` — one typeface site-wide, no per-route font overrides found in the portal.

### 1.3 Colour scales (every named colour + hex)

**`brand` (violet) — 10 stops**

**The dominance mechanism, concretely:**
1. `.btn-primary` (163 uses) *is* the violet→blue gradient. Every primary CTA in the portal is violet.
2. `.nav-item-active` is the same gradient. The whole left rail's selected state is violet.
3. The signature gradient recipe `from-accent-blue … to-brand-500` appears **44 times inline** on top of that,
   in 7 opacity variants (`/90`, `/30`, `/25`, `/20`, `/15`, `/[0.08]`, and bare).
4. `bg-brand-500/N` tinted surfaces appear **121 times in 12 different opacities**
   (`/10` 41, `/20` 29, `/15` 23, `/[0.06]` 10, `/[0.07]` 6, `/[0.08]` 5, `/[0.12]` 2, `/[0.05]`, `/[0.03]`, `/90`, `/30`, `/25`).
5. `text-brand-300` (180) + `text-brand-200` (96) is the default "highlighted text" colour, so violet
   also carries most emphasised inline text.
6. The `<body>` itself paints a fixed violet radial glow.

Net: violet is simultaneously the **primary action** colour, the **selected-nav** colour, the
**info/accent surface** colour, the **highlight text** colour and the **page background** wash —
it has no single semantic job, which is why the UI reads as uniformly purple.

Cyan/blue barely register as a counterweight (`accent-cyan` 15 uses, `accent-blue` 70 — and 24 of those
70 are inside the `from-accent-blue to-brand-500` gradient, i.e. subordinate to violet).

### 6.3 Transitions

`transition-colors` 127 · `transition` (all properties) 71 · `transition-transform` 21 ·
`transition-all` 17 · `transition-opacity` 4 = **240 transition sites.**

Durations are almost never specified: `duration-200` 8, `duration-500` 5, `duration-150` 2 — **15 of 240**

(`ease-out` 3, `ease-in` 3). `.btn-primary`/`.btn-*` bake in `duration-150`; `.card-hover` bakes in
`duration-200` — so a card and a button next to it animate at different speeds.

`transition` (bare, = `transition-property: all`) at 71 sites is a perf/consistency smell
alongside 127 `transition-colors`.

### 6.4 Reduced motion

**Handled in globals.css** for: `.glow-spin-a/-b` + `.glow-clip-a/-b`, `.btn-deploy` (transition,
sweep, arrow), `.nav-underline::after`, and all 9 `pv-*` classes — 4 `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)`
blocks.

**In the portal itself:** only **3 files** contain a `prefers-reduced-motion` block, all inside `<style jsx>`-style
inline CSS: `customer/FreeMinecraftLoader.tsx:152`, `customer/DomainIdeaGenerator.tsx:128`,
`customer/mail/Composer.tsx:440`.

Only **8 `motion-safe:` prefixes** exist portal-wide. That leaves **61 of 69 animations unguarded**, including:
- `animate-pulse` ×23 (pulsing status dots, skeletons)
- `animate-fade-up` ×21 (every page mount + panel switch)
- `animate-spin` ×11 (spinners — arguably fine)
- `animate-bounce` ×3
- `animate-pulse-dot` ×3 (the running-server indicator)

So a reduced-motion user still gets a fading page on every navigation and pulsing dots throughout.

### 6.5 Keyframes defined inside portal components (bypassing the system)

7 keyframe blocks live inside `.tsx` files rather than globals.css:
`FreeMinecraftLoader.tsx` — `cp-glow`, `cp-hiss`, `cp-shock`, `cp-particle` (4);
`DomainIdeaGenerator.tsx` — `nx-name-in`, `nx-skel` (2);
`DomainSearch.tsx` — `domainResultIn` (1).

---

## 7. LAYOUT GEOMETRY

### 7.1 Page shell

`components/portal/Shell.tsx` (988 LOC) owns the frame:

| Region | Geometry |
|---|---|
| Sidebar | `fixed inset-y-0 left-0 z-40 w-60 border-r border-white/[0.06] bg-navy-900/80 backdrop-blur-xl`, `lg:sticky lg:top-0 lg:h-screen` |
| Mobile scrim | `fixed inset-0 z-30 bg-black/50 lg:hidden` |
| Header | `sticky top-0 z-20 h-16 border-b border-white/[0.06] bg-navy-950/70 px-4 backdrop-blur-xl sm:px-6` |
| Main (normal) | `mx-auto w-full flex-1 px-4 py-8 sm:px-6 animate-fade-up max-w-7xl` |
| Main (wide) | same but `max-w-[100rem]` |
| Main (fullBleed) | `min-h-0 flex-1 overflow-hidden` — **no padding, no max-width** |

So there are **three mutually exclusive page geometries** selected by props (`wideContent`, `fullBleed`),
and the wide one uses an arbitrary `max-w-[100rem]` (1600px) rather than a scale step.
`.rail` (`max-w-6xl`) from globals.css — the marketing content rail — is **never used** in the portal, so
portal (1280/1600px) and marketing (1152px) content rails don't match.

### 7.2 Per-route max-width

Of 58 `page.tsx` files, **46 declare no `max-w-*` at all** (they inherit Shell's `max-w-7xl`).
The 12 that do:

| max-width | Route |
|---|---|
| `max-w-2xl` | `calendar/page.tsx`, `mail/page.tsx`, `tools/page.tsx` |
| `max-w-72` | `domains/[id]/page.tsx` |
| `max-w-md` | `feedback/page.tsx`, `page.tsx` (dashboard home), `servers/[id]/page.tsx` |
| `max-w-xl` | `domains/page.tsx`, `domains/register/page.tsx` |
| `max-w-xs` | `billing/page.tsx`, `invoices/[id]/page.tsx`, `invoices/page.tsx` |

(These are *first-occurrence* values — in most cases they constrain an inner element, not the page —
but the point stands that there is no page-level width convention.)

**Portal-wide `max-w-*` census:** `md` 36, `xs` 21, `xl` 21, `2xl` 13, `sm` 8, `lg` 6, `7xl` 4, `full` 3,
`3xl` 2, `none` 1, plus **17 distinct arbitrary widths** (`[12rem]`, `[10rem]`, `[24rem]`, `[200px]`,
`[260px]`, `[220px]`, `[180px]`, `[15rem]`, `[14rem]`, `[8rem]`, `[100rem]`, `[92vw]`,
`[min(100%,42rem)]`, `[calc(…)]`, `[92…]`, `[88…]`, `[85…]`, `[70…]`, `[65…]`, `[60…]`).

### 7.3 Grid patterns

`sm:grid-cols-2` 64 · `grid-cols-1` 19 · `grid-cols-2` 18 · `lg:grid-cols-4` 16 · `sm:grid-cols-3` 14 ·
`lg:grid-cols-2` 14 · `lg:grid-cols-3` 12 · `sm:grid-cols-4` 7 · `md:grid-cols-2` 6 · `xl:grid-cols-5` 4 ·
`grid-cols-9` 4 · `grid-cols-7` 3 · `grid-cols-4` 3 · `grid-cols-3` 3 · plus `sm:grid-cols-6`,
`xl:grid-cols-4`, `xl:grid-cols-3`, `sm:grid-cols-5`, `md:grid-cols-8`, `md:grid-cols-4`, and
`grid-cols-[1fr_320px]` ×3.

The card-grid responsive ladder is inconsistent: `sm:grid-cols-2 lg:grid-cols-4` (16),
`sm:grid-cols-2 lg:grid-cols-3` (12), `sm:grid-cols-2 lg:grid-cols-2` (14), `md:grid-cols-2` (6) —
**four different breakpoint ladders for the same "grid of tiles" idea**, so tile widths jump differently
page to page at the same viewport.

### 7.4 Breakpoints

| Prefix | Usages |
|---|---|
| `sm:` | **181** |
| `lg:` | **118** |
| `md:` | 35 |
| `xl:` | 9 |
| `2xl:` | 1 |

The portal is effectively **sm/lg only** — `md:` (768px) is skipped in 84% of responsive decisions, so
tablet-width layouts inherit either the phone or the desktop treatment depending on which file you're in.
`components/customer/mail/*` is the main `md:` user (three-pane mail), which is why mail behaves
differently from every other page at tablet width.

### 7.5 Z-index census

| Value | Count | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `z-10` | 14 | |
| `z-50` | 13 | modals/palette |
| `z-20` | 11 | Shell header, notification scrim |
| `z-30` | 8 | mobile scrim, dropdown |
| `z-40` | 3 | sidebar |
| `z-[55]` | 2 | **arbitrary** |
| `z-[60]` | 4 | **arbitrary** |
| `z-[70]` | 5 | **arbitrary** |
| `z-[100]` | 4 | **arbitrary** |

**15 arbitrary z-index escapes above the scale**, i.e. four ad-hoc stacking tiers (55/60/70/100) invented
to sit above `z-50` modals. Shell's own layering is `sidebar z-40 < scrim z-30 < header z-20`, which
means the header sits *below* the mobile scrim — and CommandPalette at `z-50` sits above the sidebar,
but a `z-[70]` toast-ish overlay sits above the palette. No documented stacking contract.

### 7.6 Padding pattern

Page padding is `px-4 py-8 sm:px-6` (Shell) for normal pages, **zero** for `fullBleed` pages —
so full-bleed routes (mail, terminal, claude-code, calendar) have no shared inner gutter and each
re-establishes its own.

---

## 8. CHART / VISUALISATION LIBRARIES

| Library | Present |
|---|---|
| recharts | **no** |
| chart.js | **no** |
| d3 (full) | **no** |
| visx / nivo / victory | **no** |
| `d3-geo` + `topojson-client` + `world-atlas` | yes — but for the **admin** visitor map, not the portal (UNVERIFIED that no portal route uses it; no portal import found) |

**All portal charts are hand-written SVG** in `components/ui/charts.tsx` (dependency-free, server-safe):
`Sparkline`, `AreaChart`, `Donut`, `MeterBar`.

Adoption: **8 files** import from `ui/charts.tsx` — `MeterBar` 6, `AreaChart` 2, `Sparkline` 1,
**`Donut` 0 (dead export)**. Users: `customer/DiskUsageChart.tsx` (`AreaChart` + `MeterBar`),
`customer/MetricsPanel.tsx` (3× `AreaChart`), `app/dashboard/servers/[id]/page.tsx`,
`components/customer/HostingClient.tsx`, `app/dashboard/billing/page.tsx`,
`components/customer/cpanel/CronServicesPanel.tsx`, `components/customer/gamepanel/GameOverview.tsx`,
plus `StatCard`'s `Sparkline`.

Everything else that looks like a chart is bespoke: 25 files draw `<polyline>`/`<path d=>`/`<circle cx=>`
directly, and `<canvas>` appears in `claude-code/BuildConsole.tsx` and `claude-code/voice.tsx`.
Chart colours are passed as **hex strings** (`stroke = "#8a70fb"` default in both `Sparkline` and
`StatCard`), not tokens — so a theme change would not reach any chart.

---

## 9. DIAGNOSIS — top inconsistencies, ranked, with evidence

| # | Finding | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | **The design system covers marketing, not the portal.** Of ~30 `@layer components` classes, roughly half (`tone-*`, `eyebrow*`, `hero-aura`, `lift`, `rail`, `nav-trigger`, `nav-underline`, `grad-text`, the auth glow ring, 9 `pv-*`) have **zero portal usage**, while the portal's most repeated patterns (badge, tab, modal, panel-surface, toggle, meter, empty state, code chip) have **no class at all**. | §1.7, §3 |
| 2 | **`primitives.tsx` is 187 lines and mostly formatters.** 79 import sites, but 45 (57%) import `fmtMoney`/`timeAgo`/`fmtBytes`. `PageHeader` reaches 7 files, `StatCard` 2, `ComingSoon` **0**. 166 of 245 portal files import nothing from it. | §3.0 |
| 3 | **7 badge/status-pill implementations** + **26 distinct inline bordered-pill signatures** + **13 borderless** + **20 files with their own status→colour map**. The green "success" pill alone has 7 colour recipes. | §3.2 |
| 4 | **8 tab-bar implementations** (2xl/navy-70, 2xl/navy-80, sticky 2xl, xl/white-3, inline-flex xl/white-3, inline-flex xl/navy-70, border-b-2 underline, rounded-md micro) + 8 more one-off segmented pill rows. 25 files hold tab state; zero shared `<Tabs>`. | §3.4, §3.5 |
| 5 | **24 independent modal/overlay implementations** (`fixed inset-0` ×28 in 24 files), 8 local `*Modal` components, disagreeing backdrops and z-indexes — *while* **60 destructive confirmations use the browser's native `confirm()`** across 30+ files. | §3.6, §3.7 |
| 6 | **21 spellings of "an inset panel"** (`rounded-{lg,xl,2xl} border border-white/{.03–.10} bg-white/{.01–.08}`), ~145 occurrences. Combined with **11 border-white opacities** and **14 bg-white opacities** (including duplicate spellings `/5` vs `/[0.05]`, `/10` vs `/[0.10]`), surface elevation is effectively random. | §2.8, §3.3 |
| 7 | **No icon system.** 0 icon-library imports; **214 inline `<svg>` in 50 files**; ~40 locally-defined `*Icon` components with 10 name collisions across files; **18 distinct strokeWidths**; **15 distinct hardcoded pixel widths** plus three competing Tailwind sizing idioms (`h-4 w-4` / `size-4` / `width="16"`); 70 emoji doing icon duty alongside hand-drawn equivalents of the same glyphs. | §4 |
| 8 | **Type scale is bypassed more than it's used at the small end.** 385 arbitrary `text-[Npx]` (231× `text-[11px]`, 113× `text-[10px]`) vs 1155 `text-xs`; real ramp is 16 sizes of which 7 are scale steps. No tier above `text-2xl` except one `text-4xl` — the portal has **no display type**. `font-semibold` (582) carries almost all emphasis, so hierarchy rests on colour alone. | §5.2, §5.3 |
| 9 | **Page headers are the least consistent surface.** `<h1>` exists in only 10 of 245 files, in **6 different class recipes**; 4 of 64 routes use `<PageHeader>`; most routes have no `<h1>`. `<h2>` has 24 distinct class strings, the top 3 being bare `font-semibold` with different margins. | §3.23, §3.24 |
| 10 | **Violet has no semantic job**, which is why it dominates: it is simultaneously primary CTA (`.btn-primary` ×163), active nav (`.nav-item-active`), info surface (`bg-brand-500/N` ×121 in **12 opacities**), highlight text (`text-brand-300` 180 + `text-brand-200` 96), the signature gradient (44 inline `from-accent-blue…to-brand-500` in 7 opacity variants), and the page background wash. `brand-*` = 787 utility usages vs `accent-cyan` 15. | §2.4 |
| 11 | **Motion is unguarded.** 69 animation applications, only **8** `motion-safe:`-prefixed; 3 portal files handle `prefers-reduced-motion`. `animate-fade-up` fires on `<main>` **and** on inner panels, double-animating tab switches. 225 of 240 transitions never set a duration; `.card-hover` (200ms) and `.btn-*` (150ms) disagree. 10 of 17 `--animate-*` tokens are portal-dead; all 9 `pv-*` classes are dead. | §6 |
| 12 | **~50 of 185 hex literals restate an existing token**, and 3 are *near-misses* of it (`#0a0e1a`, `#05060f`, `#05060d` vs `navy-900 #0a101f` / `navy-950 #060a14`) — visually a slightly-wrong surface. A duplicate of `.nav-item-active`'s shadow is pasted inline 4× as `shadow-[0_4px_16px_-6px_rgb(111_71_245_/_0.6)]`. Chart strokes are hardcoded `#8a70fb`, so charts can never be re-themed. | §2.3, §2.2, §8 |
| 13 | **6 toggle-switch implementations** in 2 sizes and 2 DOM strategies (JS state vs `peer-checked`), across 14 files; no `role="switch"` convention. Checkboxes use 4 different accent colours (`accent-brand-500` 18, `accent-brand-400` 5, `accent-sky-500` 1, none 16). | §3.22 |
| 14 | **Two parallel control panels** (`components/customer/cpanel/*` for VPS, `components/customer/hosting/*` for shared hosting) reimplement Websites, Databases, Cron, Apps and FileManager, each with its own `shared.tsx` that redefines `EmptyState`, a status pill, a skeleton and a copy button already present in `primitives.tsx`/globals.css. | §3.20 |
| 15 | **13 copy-to-clipboard implementations**, **~15 `<code>` skins** (6 different backgrounds for the same idea), **10 places rendering DNS record rows**, **6 terminal/console surfaces** (2 xterm + 4 hand-rolled), **2 file browsers**, **5 local `Row` + 4 local `Field`** components, **8 wizards each drawing their own step indicator**, **12 hand-rolled progress bars** in 4 track recipes. | §3.13–§3.21 |
| 16 | **Layout has no contract.** Three page geometries selected by Shell props; 46 of 58 routes declare no width; 17 arbitrary `max-w-[…]`; portal rail (`max-w-7xl`/`max-w-[100rem]`) ≠ marketing rail (`.rail max-w-6xl`, unused here); `md:` skipped in 84% of responsive decisions; **15 arbitrary z-index escapes** (55/60/70/100) above a `z-50` modal tier with no documented stacking order; `.card`'s own `p-6` overridden in 63 of 314 uses. | §7, §2.9 |
| 17 | **`text-[var(--fg)]` (23 uses, all in `components/customer/freemc/*`) imports the marketing light/dark tone token into the always-dark portal**, where no `.tone-light` ancestor exists — a cross-system borrow that is a no-op today and a latent bug if tones ever land in the portal. | §3.24, §1.3 |
| 18 | **Tables:** 41 `<table>` vs 34 `.table-shell`; 8 distinct `min-w-[…]` scroll widths; the scroll wrapper class `table-wrap` is referenced but **has no definition in globals.css** (UNVERIFIED whether defined elsewhere — no definition found). | §3.9 |
| 19 | **`tabular-nums` used only 17×** despite 30 large numeric readouts and many live counters — metric tiles and tables jitter as digits change. | §5.6 |
| 20 | **No toast/notification system at all.** 19+ files hold local `setMsg`/`setNotice`/`setError` state rendered as an inline coloured strip, in at least 2 spellings *within the same file* (`hosting/DbManager.tsx` uses both `rounded-xl … px-4 py-3 text-xs` and `rounded-lg … px-2 py-1.5 text-[11px]` for the same error idea). `alert()` is still used for some errors. | §3.8 |

### Highest-leverage consolidation targets (inventory view, no design proposal)

Ordered by (occurrences saved × files touched):

1. **Surface/panel class** — collapses 21 signatures / ~145 sites.
2. **Badge + status-tone table** — collapses 7 impls / ~40 inline pills / 20 status maps.
3. **Button size variants** — removes ~48 bespoke buttons and every `btn-* px-N py-N text-[Npx]` override.
4. **Tabs component** — collapses 8 tab-bars + 8 segmented rows across 25 stateful files.
5. **Modal + ConfirmDialog** — collapses 24 overlays and retires 60 native `confirm()` calls.
6. **Icon module** (adopt a library, or promote `marketing/icons.tsx` + `OverviewIcons.tsx` into one set) — retires ~40 local `*Icon` components and normalises 214 inline SVGs, 18 strokeWidths, 15 pixel sizes.
7. **Type scale extension** (add 10px/11px/13px steps as tokens) — removes 385 arbitrary `text-[Npx]`.
8. **Toast system** — replaces ~19 files' bespoke inline status strips.
9. **PageHeader adoption** — 60 of 64 routes currently bypass it.
10. **Meter/Progress + Skeleton/Spinner primitives** — collapses 12 bars (4 track recipes) and 4 loading idioms.

content.text:
Approach this as the design lead at a small studio known for their versatility, giving every client a visual identity pitched at the treatment the task actually calls for. Make deliberate choices about palette, typography, and layout that are specific to this subject, and avoid templated designs.

## Read the request first

Calibrate treatment, not whether to design. A doc deserves the same craft as a landing page - what changes is the treatment that craft is delivered in. Format is not part of this read: author HTML, and publish Markdown only when a loaded skill explicitly instructs it - a Markdown publish keeps its filename as its title and takes almost none of the craft below, and is never a way to save time.

Many requests call for a more utilitarian treatment: a plan, a memo, a demo. Make it polished: include real typographic hierarchy, considered spacing, and a proper palette, but avoid over-designing. Most pages do not need a flashy, gigantic hero. Keep flourishes tasteful and limited.

Some requests call for an editorial treatment: a landing page, a game, an app or tool they'll keep or share.

When unsure: a well-composed page is never the wrong answer; an over-designed visual identity sometimes is.

Fundamentals below apply to everything. The editorial process after that runs only when the read above says so.

## Fundamentals for every artifact

**Honor what's already there** Look for an existing design system first - CLAUDE.md, a tokens or theme file, existing component styles. When one exists, apply it; everything below fills gaps and never overrides. Precedence is always: the user's own words, then the project's existing system, then your choices.

**Ground it in the subject.** If the subject isn't already clear, pin it: one concrete subject, its audience, and the page's single job. The subject's own world - its materials, instruments, vernacular - is where distinctive choices come from. Whatever the treatment, carry at least one detail only this subject would have - its real units and scales, its document conventions, its terms of art - as content, not ornament; it costs a plain page nothing. Build with real content throughout, never lorem.

**Pair typefaces** Typography carries the page even when the page isn't about typography. Google Fonts is the one font host the Artifact CSP admits - link it directly (`<link rel="stylesheet" href="https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=...&display=swap">`); a face from anywhere else must be inlined as a @font-face data URI or it falls back silently. Either way, declare a real fallback stack. Keep running text near 65 characters wide; set a type scale and stay on it; give headings `text-wrap: balance`, body text room to breathe, and uppercase labels a touch of letter-spacing.

**Load libraries, don't paste them.** When the page genuinely needs a library - React, a charting or highlighting package - load its UMD build from cdnjs (only the script - a library's stylesheet still has to be inlined) with one pinned `<script src="https://cdnjs.cloudflare.com/ajax/libs/...">` placed before the inline script that uses its global, instead of inlining the library's source or hand-writing a stand-in; the Artifact tool's description lists the few other script hosts the CSP admits. The page's own CSS and JS, its images and its data ship with the page. Most pages need no library at all - reach for one only when it carries real weight.

**Choose neutrals, don't default to them.** A pure mid-grey reads as unconsidered; a grey with a slight hue bias toward the page's accent reads as chosen. Pure white and near-black are fine grounds when they suit the subject - the point is that the neutral was picked, not inherited.

**Design both themes.** The page renders in the viewer's theme, and the viewer has three states, not two: an explicit choice stamps `data-theme="dark"` / `data-theme="light"` on the root element, and the default "system" setting stamps *nothing* - most viewers see the un-stamped document, where only `prefers-color-scheme` separates light from dark. Structure the CSS token-level for all three: the bare `:root` block defines the complete light palette (for a deliberately dark-first design, swap light and dark consistently through this whole pattern); `@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark)` redefines only the tokens, guarded as `:root:not([data-theme="light"])` so an explicit light choice beats a dark OS; `:root[data-theme="dark"]` redefines them again so the toggle also wins in the other direction. Style components through the tokens, never directly inside a media or `[data-theme]` block - a color whose only definition sits behind `[data-theme]` never applies in the un-stamped state, and the page renders one theme's text on the other theme's ground. Two more rules keep each theme resolving as a set: the artifact composites over a ground the viewer paints in *its* theme, so `body` must set an explicit `background` from a token - a transparent body silently borrows the host's ground; and every element that sets a color takes it from the same token set as the surface behind it, never a literal that only works in one theme. Declare every token in the bare `:root` block before any media or `[data-theme]` block redefines it - a color that exists only inside one of those blocks is the classic unreadable-artifact bug. Give the second theme the same care as the first - don't naively invert; keep contrast legible and the accent working on both grounds. A design that deliberately commits to one visual world (a neon arcade screen, a letterpress invitation) may stay single-theme - then skip the media query and stamps entirely but still paint the background and every color explicitly, so the page holds on either host ground; make it a choice, not an omission.

**Let layout do the spacing.** Lay out sibling groups with flex or grid and `gap`, not per-element margins that silently collapse or double. Wide content - tables, code, diagrams - gets `overflow-x: auto` on its own container so the page body never scrolls sideways. Reach for `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums` wherever digits line up in columns.

**Compose repeated things as one object.** Cards in a row, label/value pairs down a list, badges on siblings: same edges, baselines and inner padding from one to the next, and a recurring element sits in the same place on each. Let content set a container's height and pick a column count the items fill, so nothing stretches over dead space or sits alone in a row. Text that can outgrow its track wraps or scrolls in its own container; clipped text is a bug.

**Not everything is a card.** Border, fill, radius and shadow each say "separate object" - spend them by role, lifting the one thing that needs it, instead of one radius and one shadow stamped on every block, which flattens the hierarchy. Lead with big-number tiles only when those figures are the point of the page.

**Draw charts to the scale.** One scale places marks, ticks and labels, and every label names a value the chart reaches; chart text takes its color from the theme tokens so it reads in both themes; marks, labels and edges stay clear of one another and inside the drawing's bounds - in SVG, leave room in the viewBox for the outermost labels and give every drawn shape an explicit fill.

**Show the page at rest.** Everything meant to be read is visible once the page has loaded, without scrolling to trigger it - that first still frame is what a thumbnail, a shared link, and a skimming reader all get. A section may animate in, but from a visible resting state, never parked at `opacity: 0` waiting on an observer. Size a hero to what it holds, not to the viewport; a `100vh` opener pushes the page itself out of that first frame. A tool or app opens in a realistic working state - the user's real data where it exists, otherwise example rows, a loaded sample, a form someone plausibly filled, plainly marked as examples and never passed off as the user's own figures - so the first look shows what it does; an empty shell waiting for input shows nothing.

**Avoid AI-generated design** AI-generated design currently clusters around a few looks: warm cream (#F4F1EA) with a serif display and terracotta accent; near-black with a lone acid-green or vermilion pop; broadsheet hairline rules with dense columns; a purple-to-blue gradient hero on white; Inter or Space Grotesk as the "safe" face; emoji as section markers; everything centered; `rounded-lg` everywhere; accent bar/rail on rounded cards. Where the user pins down a visual direction, follow it exactly - their words always win, including when they ask for one of these looks. Where nothing is specified, don't spend that freedom on one of these defaults.

**Build cleanly** Be cognizant of overlapping elements, cascade collisions, silent font fallbacks. Close every non-void element, double-quote attributes, give keyboard focus a visible state, respect `prefers-reduced-motion`. For generative or decorative graphics, reach for Canvas or WebGL rather than hand-authoring long SVG path data.

**CSS rules** When writing the CSS, watch your selector specificities. It is easy to generate classes that cancel each other out - a type-based selector like `.section` fighting an element-based one like `.cta` over padding and margins between sections. Structure the cascade so it doesn't silently undo your spacing.

**Writing the copy** Words are design material, not decoration. Write from the user's side of the screen - name things by what people recognize, not how the system is built (a person manages *notifications*, not *webhook config*). Active voice; a control says exactly what happens ("Publish", then a toast that says "Published"). Errors explain what went wrong and how to fix it - no apologies, no vagueness. Specific beats clever.

**Name the page like a product, not a caption.** The `<title>` is the artifact's name in the gallery and the browser tab, and it sets the reader's first impression of care. Give the page a real name: a short noun phrase, typically two to four words, specific to the subject - or, for a page that exists to answer one question, that question itself, which is then the page's name. Stop at the name - a title that carries its own explainer after a dash or colon reads as generated filler. The name must also identify the page among many: in the gallery it sits beside dozens of other artifacts, and a generic category label that could sit on any of them fails as a name just as surely as an appended explainer. When a candidate title pairs the name with a generic word - a greeting, a category, a page-type label - the name is the half to keep; a trim that drops the identity and keeps the generic word produces exactly the title that could sit on any page. And the rule removes explainers, it does not impose brevity: a multi-word title that already reads as one specific name is finished, and shortening it further only makes it generic. The one-sentence publish `description` is where the explanation belongs; the gallery shows it right under the title.

**Structure is information** Structural devices, numbering, eyebrows, dividers, labels, should encode something true about the content, not decorate it. Many generic designs use numbered markers (01 / 02 / 03), but that's only appropriate if the content actually is a sequence - like a real process or a typed timeline where order carries information the reader needs. Question if choices like numbered markers actually make sense before incorporating them.

**When it's a UI, not a document** A dashboard or tool is scanned and operated, not read top-to-bottom, so the craft shifts from typography to information design. Surface the summary before the detail; encode state in form as well as number - a pill, a chip, a severity stripe - so what needs attention reads at a glance. Semantic color (good / warning / critical) is separate from the accent hue and doesn't count as your accent. Give sparklines and charts the same care as type: an area fill, a faint grid, an emphasized endpoint. What's interactive should look interactive.



## Process

Before writing code, sketch a short design plan - a compact token system with color, type, and layout:
- **Color**: describe the palette as 4-6 named hex values.
- **Type**: typefaces for 2+ roles - a characterful display face used with restraint, a complementary body face, and a utility face for captions or data if needed.
- **Layout**: a layout concept in one or two sentences.

Then build, following the plan and deriving every color and type decision from it.

**Write, look once, publish.** Before publishing you may look at the rendered page once - one screenshot of the local file, or the Artifact tool's preview where it offers one - then one pass of edits for what it shows, without a second look. For a page that charts real numbers, take that look rather than skip it, and spend it on the chart. Don't build a test loop around your own file: no repeated screenshots, no pulling the script out to run it through node, no scripts that probe the DOM. That loop spends the session re-checking what a careful write already settled, while the user waits for a link. Then publish, check once any `window.claude` call the preview couldn't run, and stop: the live page is the review surface, and further polish is the user's to ask for. If the user reports something visibly broken - a clipped column, unreadable text, a control that does nothing - fix that and republish once.

## When the request is editorial

The stance shifts: the client has already rejected proposals that felt templated, and is paying for a distinctive point of view. Make opinionated calls, and take one real aesthetic risk where it serves the work.

Review the design plan against the subject before building: if any part of it reads like the generic default you would produce for any similar page, revise that part, and note what you changed and why. Only after you've confirmed the plan's uniqueness do you write the code, following the revised plan exactly.

**Principles** 

- The hero is a thesis: open with the most characteristic thing in the subject's world - headline, image, live demo, interactive moment. 
- Typography carries the personality of the page. Pair the display and body faces deliberately, not the same families you would reach for on any other project, and set a clear type scale with intentional weights, widths, and spacing. Make the type treatment itself a memorable part of the design, not a neutral delivery vehicle for the content. 
- Leverage motion deliberately. Think about where and if animation can serve the subject: a page-load sequence, hover micro-interactions, ambient atmosphere. An orchestrated moment usually lands harder than scattered effects; choose what the direction calls for. However, sometimes less is more, and extra animation contributes to the feeling that the design is AI-generated. 
- Match complexity to the vision. Maximalist directions need elaborate execution; minimal directions need precision in spacing, type, and detail. Elegance is executing the chosen vision well.
- Spend your boldness in one place; keep everything around it quiet. If the accent fights the ground, shift it toward analogous or drop saturation rather than replacing it.
I have the design approach: the blueprint as a technical drafting sheet, using the very typefaces it recommends. Waiting on the last five audits before I build it.

Summary (~10 lines):

1. **Models**: a paid game server is a plain `Server` row discriminated by `gamePlanId`; `planId` points at the *base* VPS plan that sizes the VM, never at what's billed. Game-only fields: `gameVariant`, `gameConfig`, `subdomain`, `autoUpdate`, `publicListing`, `customDomain`, plus `GameSchedule`/`ServerMod`/`PlayerSession`. Free Minecraft is a completely separate `FreeMinecraftServer` model (Docker container on `freemc-host`, no jobs, no billing, no worker).
2. **`ServerStatus` is the VM's status only** — whether the game process is actually up is never persisted anywhere.
3. **Biggest structural finding**: the game branch of `app/dashboard/servers/[id]/page.tsx` returns at line 1008, so the VPS `ServerTabs` never renders. That makes **Renew now, auto-renew, Cancel service, Delete, snapshots, networking, reinstall and VM-level power unreachable for every game customer**, and kills `GameManage.tsx` — which is the *only* consumer of the working `GAME_BACKUP` world-archive capability (`createGameBackup`/`getGameBackups`). The worker still emails "Download it from the Manage → Worlds tab", a tab that doesn't exist.
4. **RCON reality**: only `minecraft`, `cs2`, `palworld` have working RCON. Rust is declared-but-deferred; **44 of 47 families are `rcon:"none"`**, so console commands, player list, kick/ban, quick commands, roles and inventory are inert for them — and the panel only discovers this from an error-string regex.
5. **Two flag-gated features are effectively off in prod**: `GAME_CONFIG` saves (`ENABLE_REAL_GAMECFG`) and mod installs (`ENABLE_REAL_GAMEMODS`). Both fail *honestly* rather than lying, but the customer copy promises a working feature. Even with the flags on, config appliers exist for 5 families and mod installers for 3 families / 4 of 15 sources. (Prod `.env` not read — marked UNVERIFIED.)
6. **Mod Store** fabricates ratings, install counts, screenshots, reviews and version history from `hash(slug)`; the version dropdown is display-only. Mods and Plugins are the same tab with a keyword filter.
7. **Worlds is read-only** (no reset/upload/download/seed; no `level-seed` field), the **file manager has no unzip**, and "Startup, environment & crash recovery" is an explicit *coming soon* stub.
8. **Wizard**: 4 steps (Game / Plan / Settings / Review). Game + tier + term + dedicated-IP are pre-payment and price-bearing; name, subdomain, variant and all config fields are changeable later. Tier changes are hard-refused post-sale by both `resize.ts` and `actions-server-lifecycle.ts` — and both error messages point at a settings control that doesn't exist. Provisioning reports exactly **6** coarse `provisioningStep` labels via a full-route 5s `AutoRefresh` (no polling endpoint, no %, no ETA, no per-phase game/mod/DNS progress).
9. **Free MC** reuses the paid `MINECRAFT` schema (`schemaFor("minecraft")` + `validateConfig`), the subdomain rules and the 26-node LuckPerms command catalogue; everything else (console, players, roles actions, inventory, settings UI) is duplicated. It has **no upgrade-to-paid path at all**, an unenforced disk quota, a send-only console, and both Mods and Roles gate on the *deprecated* `preset` column — which `applyFreeMinecraftSettings` sets to `"custom"`, silently disabling both tabs.
10. **Catalogue**: 47 families, 32 with config schemas, 30 with real art. `ark` points at the `ark-asa` art slug while the correct `ark-ase_*` files sit unused; `dayz_*` art is orphaned; 17 families ship with no hero/poster. No regions exist anywhere. Games never receive promos or coupons (schema supports `CouponServiceKind.GAME`, no code path reads it). Permissions are ownership-or-admin only — `Organization`/`Membership` exist but no game path consults them, so there is no per-server sharing or delegated access.</result>

<note>A task-notification fires each time this agent stops with no live background children of its own. The user can send it another message and resume it, so the same task-id may notify more than once.</note>
<result>Report written to `/tmp/claude-0/-root/1716c7ee-ae35-4cf5-b557-9059709e07c4/scratchpad/audit-09-competitor-ux.md` (635 lines). Nothing under /opt/nxeon touched; no visual/branding detail captured, principles and flow structure only.

Covered with fetched sources: DigitalOcean, Hetzner Cloud, Vultr, Vercel, Railway, Cloudflare (registrar + add-site), Porkbun, Google Workspace, Aternos, Shockbyte, Apex, Pterodactyl-class panels, plus Hostinger as the closest structural analogue. Namecheap and a few detail-page tab lists are marked MEMORY (fetches 404'd/403'd) and are never the sole basis for a recommendation.

Key findings:

- **The single most transferable pattern is two-stage checkout.** Hostinger takes payment on plan/term/region and collects hostname, root password and SSH key *after*, ending in "Finish setup". Shockbyte and Apex defer game software/modpack to a post-purchase one-click installer. Google Workspace defers its entire DNS/email setup.
- **Pre-payment fields should be only price-determining or legally-required.** The comparison table shows no competitor selling to non-experts asks for optional config before the commit — except Hetzner, whose 16-step flow is the longest and worst in the set.
- **Provisioning honesty:** Aternos is the standout — queue position, ETA, and a liveness confirmation before consuming capacity, plus a visible countdown before auto-sleep. Cloudflare admits its DNS scan may be incomplete; Google states real time windows. The recommended pattern for coarse backends is named real stages + elapsed time + p50/p90 expectation, never an interpolated percentage.
- **Pricing trust:** Porkbun shows registration/renewal/transfer in one row; Cloudflare renews at registry cost with no upsells; Hetzner shows hourly rate + monthly cap and (crucially) that a powered-off server still bills.
- **Game pickers:** Apex publishes a real player-count→RAM mapping but leaves it in a guide article, not the picker — that's the gap Nxeon should close, with a "change plan any time" de-risk. Free-tier upgrade prompts should fire at the moment a limit bites and must promise world/config continuity.
